Plan ahead: stop methotrexate ≥ 3 months pre-conception (both parents). Continue hydroxychloroquine + sulfasalazine + low-dose prednisolone + certolizumab pegol (no placental transfer). Refer specialist obstetric + rheumatology.
Physio + OT + podiatry. Patient education. Screen + manage CVD risk (RA itself doubles CV risk). Annual flu vaccine, 5-yearly pneumococcal.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
presentation: Multi-system autoimmune disease — 9× more common in women, peak 15–45 yrs
Constitutional: fever, fatigue, weight loss, lymphadenopathy
Cutaneous: malar (butterfly) rash, discoid lupus, photosensitivity
Musculoskeletal: arthralgia + non-erosive arthritis
Renal: lupus nephritis (proteinuria + active sediment)
Neuropsychiatric: psychosis, seizure, stroke, neuropathy
Haematological: cytopenias, AIHA, ITP
Serositis: pleuritis, pericarditis
SSA / Afro-Caribbean populations — more severe disease + earlier renal involvement
redFlags: Lupus nephritis — rapid progression to ESRD
Pregnancy with active disease — flare + neonatal lupus + congenital heart block

diagnostics.test: ACR/EULAR 2019 classification criteria — entry criterion ANA + score ≥ 10
ANA + anti-dsDNA + anti-Sm + complement (C3, C4) + lupus anticoagulant + ACL + anti-β2-GP1
diagnostics.rationale: anti-dsDNA correlates with disease activity + renal; anti-Sm specific; low complement = active

diagnostics.test: FBC + U+E + LFT + CRP + ESR + urinalysis + UPCR / 24-h urine protein
Renal biopsy in any suspected lupus nephritis

management.detail: Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BD (5 mg/kg/day max) — first-line for all patients regardless of activity. Reduces flares + improves survival. Annual ophthalmology screening for retinal toxicity.
HCQ + low-dose prednisolone (≤ 7.5 mg/day) ± methotrexate 15–25 mg weekly. Topical steroid / tacrolimus for cutaneous.
Above + immunosuppressant: methotrexate, azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day, mycophenolate 1.5–3 g/day. Higher initial steroid burst.

management.step: Severe organ involvement (lupus nephritis / NPSLE / DAH)
management.detail: Induction: methylprednisolone pulses 0.5–1 g × 3 days + mycophenolate 2–3 g/day (or IV cyclophosphamide). Maintenance: mycophenolate 1.5–2 g/day OR azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day × 3–5 years. Belimumab + anifrolumab biologics — adjunct (specialist). Rituximab for refractory.

Multidisciplinary clinic. HCQ + low-dose steroid continued. Stop mycophenolate + methotrexate + cyclophosphamide ≥ 3 months pre-conception → switch to azathioprine / tacrolimus. Aspirin 75 mg from 12 weeks + LMWH if APS / prior fetal loss. Anti-Ro+ → fetal echo (congenital heart block).
Sun protection (factor 50+). Smoking cessation. CVD risk reduction (RA-like premature atherosclerosis). Vaccinate (no live vaccine while immunosuppressed). Mental health support.

title: Cardiac arrest — adult ALS algorithm
presentation: Unresponsive + not breathing normally → start CPR
Shockable rhythms: VF + pulseless VT (20–30 % of arrests; best survival)
Non-shockable: PEA + asystole (most common; poorer outcome)
redFlags: Delay in recognition or CPR initiation > 1 min reduces survival 7–10 % per minute
Reversible causes — 4Hs (Hypoxia, Hypovolaemia, Hypo/hyperkalaemia + metabolic, Hypothermia) + 4Ts (Thrombosis pulmonary/cardiac, Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade, Toxins)
Pregnancy ≥ 20 weeks — perimortem caesarean within 4 min of arrest
Hypothermia — 'not dead until warm and dead'

diagnostics.test: Rhythm check on cardiac monitor / AED
Echo during pulse check — wall motion, RV strain, tamponade, hypovolaemia

management.step: Recognise + call for help + start CPR + attach defibrillator
management.detail: Chest compressions 100–120/min, depth 5–6 cm, full recoil, minimise interruptions. Compression:ventilation 30:2 (or continuous if intubated). High-flow O₂ via BVM with reservoir.

Shock 150–200 J biphasic (escalate after 3rd shock to max). Resume CPR immediately × 2 min then re-assess. Adrenaline 1 mg IV after 3rd shock + every 3–5 min thereafter. Amiodarone 300 mg IV after 3rd shock + 150 mg after 5th.
Adrenaline 1 mg IV as soon as access available + every 3–5 min. Continue CPR + treat reversible causes.

Hypoxia → secure airway. Hypovolaemia → IV fluids + blood. Hypo/hyperkalaemia → 10 mL 10 % calcium gluconate + insulin-glucose / NaHCO₃. Hypothermia → rewarming. Tension pneumothorax → needle thoracostomy. Tamponade → pericardiocentesis / thoracotomy. PE → thrombolysis (continue CPR ≥ 60 min after). Tablets → specific antidote.
Left lateral tilt (manual displacement of uterus). PERIMORTEM CAESAREAN within 4 min of arrest if no ROSC — improves maternal venous return + may save fetus.
12-lead ECG. Target SpO₂ 94–98 %, normoxia. Targeted temperature management 32–36 °C × 24 h (if comatose). Treat precipitant (PCI for STEMI). Glycaemic control. Neuro-prognostication at ≥ 72 h.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Atrial fibrillation — acute presentation
presentation: Palpitations, breathlessness, chest discomfort, syncope, fatigue, embolic stroke / TIA presentation
Irregularly irregular pulse
Causes: HTN, IHD, valvular disease (rheumatic in SSA), thyrotoxicosis, alcohol, sepsis, PE, electrolytes, structural heart disease
Classify by haemodynamics + duration
redFlags: Haemodynamic instability — hypotension, pulmonary oedema, ischaemic chest pain, syncope → urgent cardioversion
Pre-excitation (delta wave, WPW + AF) — avoid AV nodal blockers; use IV flecainide / amiodarone / cardiovert

diagnostics.test: 12-lead ECG — irregularly irregular, absent P waves, fibrillatory waves

diagnostics.rationale: stroke + bleeding risk for anticoagulation decision

management.detail: Synchronised DC cardioversion 100–200 J biphasic, escalate. Anaesthesia + heparin pre-cardioversion. If onset < 48 h, no pre-procedure TOE needed; if > 48 h or unknown, anticoagulate × 3 weeks OR TOE-guided.
First-line: β-blocker (bisoprolol 2.5–10 mg/day) OR non-DHP CCB (diltiazem 120–360 mg/day; avoid in HFrEF). Target HR < 110 (RACE II) or < 80 if symptomatic. Add digoxin if HF / inadequate control.

management.step: Rhythm control (selected — symptomatic despite rate control, young, paroxysmal)
management.detail: Acute pharmacologic — flecainide 300 mg PO single (LV ejection > 35 %, no structural disease) OR amiodarone 300 mg IV over 30 min then 900 mg over 24 h. Catheter ablation (PVI) for selected refractory cases.

Score ≥ 2 (men) or ≥ 3 (women) — DOAC first-line (apixaban 5 mg BD; reduce 2.5 mg BD if ≥ 2 of: age ≥ 80, weight ≤ 60 kg, creatinine ≥ 133). Warfarin (target INR 2.5) for mechanical valves + moderate-severe mitral stenosis (valvular AF). NOT aspirin.
Thyrotoxicosis: control hyperthyroid. Alcohol-related: cessation. Sepsis / PE / electrolytes: treat. Reassess rhythm after cause addressed; many resolve.

Annual review of CHA₂DS₂-VASc + bleeding risk + symptoms + rate / rhythm. Patient education re symptoms + pulse self-monitoring. Lifestyle (exercise, weight, sleep apnoea screen, alcohol < 7 units/week, BP control < 130/80).

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Infective endocarditis
presentation: Fever (most common — 90 %), new / changed murmur, embolic phenomena (Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, Roth spots, splinter haemorrhages, septic emboli, cerebral abscess, glomerulonephritis)
Risk: prosthetic valve, congenital heart disease, prior IE, IVDU, rheumatic heart disease (SSA common), recent dental / surgical / vascular catheter / haemodialysis
SSA — rheumatic heart disease remains a major substrate
redFlags: Large vegetation (> 10 mm) — embolic stroke risk

diagnostics.test: Modified Duke criteria — 2 major / 1 major + 3 minor / 5 minor
Blood cultures × 3 from separate sites over 24 h BEFORE antibiotics
Transthoracic echo (TTE) — initial; transoesophageal (TOE) if negative + high suspicion / prosthetic valve / TTE limited
CT brain / CT angiography if neurological signs
ECG (heart block — root abscess), CRP, FBC, U+E, urinalysis (haematuria from emboli)

management.step: Empirical antibiotic — start after 3 sets of blood cultures
management.detail: Native valve / community-acquired: amoxicillin 2 g IV every 4 h + gentamicin 1 mg/kg every 8 h. Healthcare-associated / prosthetic / MRSA risk: vancomycin + gentamicin ± rifampicin. Adjust on cultures + sensitivities — total 4–6 weeks.

Streptococci (viridans, bovis): benzylpenicillin 12 g/day IV ± gentamicin × 4–6 weeks. Staphylococci: flucloxacillin 12 g/day (MSSA) or vancomycin (MRSA) ± rifampicin (prosthetic) × 4–6 weeks. Enterococcus: amoxicillin + gentamicin (or ceftriaxone). HACEK: ceftriaxone.

management.step: Surgical indications — within days, not weeks
management.detail: Heart failure (from valve regurgitation), uncontrolled infection (persistent positive cultures > 7 days, abscess, large vegetation), high embolic risk (> 10 mm vegetation), prosthetic valve dehiscence, fungal IE. Multidisciplinary 'Endocarditis Team'.

Heart block — temporary pacing + surgery for abscess. Stroke — supportive, avoid thrombolysis (mycotic aneurysm bleeding risk). Splenic embolus / abscess — drainage. AKI — hydration, avoid nephrotoxics.
Multidisciplinary care. Continue antibiotics throughout. Caesarean if surgical intervention near term. Lactation usually possible.

TTE on completion of treatment for baseline. 6-monthly review × 1 year. Lifelong endocarditis awareness card. Dental hygiene + antibiotic prophylaxis for high-risk procedures per local protocol (AHA + ESC differ from NICE).

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: COPD exacerbation — clinical management
presentation: Acute worsening of dyspnoea + cough + sputum (often purulent) + wheeze in known COPD patient
Sometimes oedema (cor pulmonale), confusion (CO₂ retention), tachypnoea, accessory muscle use, pursed-lip breathing
Triggers: viral / bacterial infection (most), pollution, weather change, non-adherence, comorbidity (PE, MI, HF, pneumothorax)
redFlags: Severe dyspnoea / cyanosis / inability to speak
Acidosis on ABG — type 2 respiratory failure
Failure to respond to initial treatment

diagnostics.rationale: type 1 vs type 2 respiratory failure, acidosis severity, NIV decision

diagnostics.test: FBC + U+E + CRP + glucose + procalcitonin (if available)
Blood cultures + sputum culture if severe / refractory

management.detail: Venturi 24–28 % initially in CO₂-retainers. Recheck ABG at 30–60 min. Do NOT chase normal SpO₂ — risks hypercapnia + acidosis.
Salbutamol 5 mg + ipratropium 500 µg nebulised in air (not O₂, to avoid hypercapnia) every 4–6 h. Spacer can substitute in mild.
Prednisolone 30 mg PO OD × 5 days (REDUCE trial — non-inferior to 14 days). IV hydrocortisone 100 mg every 6 h if vomiting / NBM.

management.step: Antibiotic — if 2 of 3 Anthonisen criteria (increased dyspnoea, sputum volume, sputum purulence)
management.detail: First-line: amoxicillin 500 mg every 8 h × 5 days OR doxycycline 200 mg loading + 100 mg OD × 5 days. Severe / hospital-acquired: co-amoxiclav / piperacillin-tazobactam.

management.step: NIV — for persistent type 2 RF (pH < 7.35, PaCO₂ > 6.5, RR > 23) despite optimal medical therapy
management.detail: Bi-level positive airway pressure: IPAP 12–20, EPAP 4–8, titrate to target SpO₂ + pH normalisation. Repeat ABG at 1 h. Failure → intubation + IMV (assess ceiling-of-care decision).

Optimise inhaler technique + check adherence. Review GOLD step. Pulmonary rehab referral. Smoking cessation. Vaccinate (flu, pneumococcal, COVID). LTOT assessment if hypoxic at rest. Self-management plan + rescue pack (steroid + antibiotic at home for next exacerbation).

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management of Common Conditions (MOH)

title: Helicobacter pylori — eradication
presentation: Most asymptomatic (50 % of world population infected; high SSA prevalence)

Indications for testing + treating: peptic ulcer (gastric / duodenal), MALT lymphoma, post-resection of early gastric cancer, family history gastric cancer, unexplained iron deficiency, ITP, long-term NSAID + dyspepsia, dyspepsia in < 60 (test-and-treat)
Reflux is NOT an indication
redFlags: Alarm features in dyspepsia — > 55 yrs new onset, weight loss, dysphagia, vomiting, GI bleed, anaemia, mass → urgent endoscopy
Persistent symptoms after eradication — re-test (urea breath test)
Antibiotic resistance — rising clarithromycin + metronidazole resistance

diagnostics.test: Stool antigen test OR urea breath test (UBT)
diagnostics.rationale: non-invasive; both > 90 % sensitive + specific; stop PPI ≥ 2 weeks + antibiotics ≥ 4 weeks before test

diagnostics.test: Endoscopic biopsy + rapid urease test + histology
diagnostics.rationale: in patients undergoing endoscopy for other reason

diagnostics.test: Serology — limited use (doesn't distinguish past vs active) — not recommended for diagnosis

management.detail: Standard triple — 7-day course: PPI BD (omeprazole 20 mg / lansoprazole 30 mg) + amoxicillin 1 g BD + clarithromycin 500 mg BD. AVOID clarithromycin if used in past year or in areas with > 15 % resistance.
PPI BD + clarithromycin 500 mg BD + metronidazole 400 mg BD × 7 days.

management.step: Bismuth quadruple therapy (1st-line in high clarithromycin resistance, OR after first-line failure)
management.detail: PPI BD + bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg QDS + metronidazole 400 mg QDS + tetracycline 500 mg QDS × 10–14 days.
PPI BD + amoxicillin 1 g BD + levofloxacin 500 mg OD × 10 days.
Stool antigen / UBT at ≥ 4 weeks after completing therapy + ≥ 2 weeks off PPI. Retest if persistent / recurrent symptoms.
Defer eradication until postpartum (clarithromycin avoided 1st trimester; tetracycline contraindicated). Continue PPI for symptomatic ulcer.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Delirium
presentation: Acute (hours-days) fluctuating change in consciousness + attention + cognition
Hyperactive (agitation, hallucinations), hypoactive (drowsy, withdrawn — often missed), or mixed
Disorientation, perceptual disturbance, sleep-wake reversal
Common precipitants — infection (UTI, pneumonia), drugs (anticholinergic, opioid, benzo), pain, constipation, urinary retention, electrolyte (Na, glucose), hypoxia, alcohol withdrawal, post-op
Predisposing — age > 65, cognitive impairment, frailty, hearing/visual impairment, polypharmacy
redFlags: Acute behavioural disturbance with confusion in elderly — ALWAYS exclude delirium first
Reduced consciousness — CT brain + LP indicated
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome (drug-induced delirium with autonomic instability)

diagnostics.test: 4AT — quick bedside screening (Alertness, AMT4, Attention, Acute change)
CAM (Confusion Assessment Method) — gold standard bedside diagnosis
diagnostics.rationale: acute onset + fluctuating + inattention + (disorganised thinking OR altered consciousness)

diagnostics.test: Identify cause — FBC, U+E, glucose, calcium, magnesium, LFTs, TSH, B12, CRP, urinalysis, CXR, ECG, drug review, urinary retention check, stool review
CT brain if focal neuro / head injury / atypical / no clear cause

management.detail: Treat infection / dehydration / hypoxia / electrolyte / pain / constipation / retention. Review + stop unnecessary medications (especially anticholinergics, opioids, BZD).

Quiet single room, hearing aids + glasses available, family photos + objects, reorientation (clock, calendar), avoid restraints, avoid catheter unless essential. Re-establish day-night cycle. Mobilise. Family presence.

management.step: Pharmacological — last resort for risk to self / others / impossible care
management.detail: Haloperidol 0.25–0.5 mg PO/IM (very low dose; max 2 mg/day in elderly) OR olanzapine 2.5–5 mg PO. AVOID in Parkinson disease + DLB (extreme sensitivity) — use quetiapine 12.5–25 mg.
Chlordiazepoxide / diazepam symptom-triggered (CIWA-Ar) + thiamine 200 mg IV before glucose + IV fluids.
Physical / chemical restraints worsen outcomes + increase mortality. Use 1:1 nursing / family presence instead.

Delirium often persists for weeks. Inform GP + family. Cognitive assessment at 4 weeks + 3 months after resolution (delirium unmasks pre-existing dementia in 30 %). Geriatric / memory clinic if persistent.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Suicide risk assessment + management
presentation: Recent self-harm (intentional injury / poisoning regardless of intent)
Stated suicidal ideation, plan, intent, preparatory acts
Indirect presentations — substance overdose, accident, presenting with feeling 'unable to go on'

Risk factors — male, age > 50 OR adolescent, prior attempt (strongest predictor), depression / psychosis / substance use, recent loss / discharge / bereavement, chronic pain / illness, access to lethal means, social isolation, family history
SSA contexts — agricultural pesticide self-poisoning is leading method; access restriction is most evidence-based intervention
redFlags: Active suicidal plan with means + intent
Persistent suicidal ideation + agitation + insomnia + hopelessness
Command auditory hallucinations to harm self
Children + adolescents — adult-equivalent risk factors plus impulsivity + access to firearms / pesticides

diagnostics.test: Direct sensitive enquiry — open + closed questions
diagnostics.rationale: asking does NOT increase risk; concealment is a major safety issue

diagnostics.test: Validated tools — Columbia C-SSRS, Beck Suicide Intent Scale
diagnostics.rationale: supplement clinical judgement; do not rely on score alone

diagnostics.test: Physical exam — exclude / treat injury, ingestion, withdrawal

management.detail: 1:1 nursing observation. Remove lethal means. Stay with patient in private safe space. Calm validating engagement. Do not leave alone if active risk. Notify senior + mental health team.

Treat overdose / injury per toxicology / surgical protocol. ABCDE. Antidote where applicable (NAC for paracetamol, atropine + pralidoxime for organophosphate, naloxone for opioid). Activated charcoal if recent + airway protected. Bloods including paracetamol + salicylate + ethanol if any uncertainty.
Specialist mental health team review BEFORE discharge if any self-harm. Joint formulation with patient + family — identify modifiable risk + protective factors + warning signs.

Depression: sertraline / SNRI + psychotherapy (CBT, IPT). ECT for severe + suicidal depression refractory or pregnancy. Psychosis: antipsychotic. Substance use: detoxification + relapse prevention. Personality disorder: DBT / MBT.

Written collaborative safety plan: warning signs, internal coping strategies, social contacts, professional contacts, crisis line numbers, restriction of lethal means. Provide patient + family. SSA — secure pesticide storage / replace high-lethality pesticides.
Specialist mental health follow-up within 7 days of discharge. Reach out actively if patient misses appointment. Family / carer support. Address social determinants (housing, finance, isolation).

references.label: WHO Preventing Suicide 2014 + LIVE LIFE Toolkit 2021
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for the Management of Common Mental Disorders / Kenya-adapted WHO mhGAP (MOH)

title: Chronic kidney disease (CKD)
presentation: Reduced eGFR (< 60) OR markers of kidney damage (albuminuria, haematuria, structural / pathological / electrolyte) for > 3 months
KDIGO classification: G1 (≥ 90) to G5 (< 15), and A1 (< 3 mg/mmol) to A3 (≥ 30 mg/mmol) by albuminuria
Common causes in SSA — hypertensive nephrosclerosis, diabetic nephropathy, HIV-associated nephropathy, schistosomiasis, sickle nephropathy, glomerulonephritis (post-strep, infective)
Often asymptomatic until late stage — fatigue, oedema, pruritus, anorexia, nausea, restless legs, dyspnoea (volume), uraemic encephalopathy
redFlags: Rapid decline (eGFR drop > 5 in 1 year or > 25 % from baseline)
ESRD — symptoms / signs needing dialysis (uraemia, refractory K, fluid overload, acidosis)

diagnostics.test: Repeat eGFR + ACR at 3 months to confirm chronicity
Urinalysis + urine ACR + urine protein:creatinine ratio
FBC + ferritin + transferrin saturation + B12 + folate + PTH + calcium + phosphate + vitamin D
Cause screen — autoimmune (ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, complement), HIV, HBV, HCV, immunoglobulins, SPEP, Bence-Jones, urine microscopy
diagnostics.rationale: identify treatable cause (especially if rapid decline / atypical)

diagnostics.test: USS kidneys — size, symmetry, obstruction, polycystic disease

management.detail: HTN: target BP < 130/80 (ACEi / ARB if albuminuria — major outcome benefit). Diabetes: HbA1c 7–8 % (less tight in advanced CKD); SGLT2i (dapagliflozin / empagliflozin) for CKD with diabetes / proteinuria > 25 mg/mmol — major mortality + renal benefit (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY). HIV: optimise ART. Glomerular: cause-specific (steroids, cyclophosphamide, MMF).
Statin (atorvastatin 20 mg) for all CKD ≥ stage 3 regardless of cholesterol. Aspirin only for established CVD. BP < 130/80. Smoking cessation. Weight management.

Iron — target ferritin 100–500 + TSAT > 20 %. ESA (epoetin) if Hb < 100 + adequate iron + no contraindication, target Hb 100–115. Phosphate restriction + binder (sevelamer / calcium acetate) if PO₄ > 1.78. Vitamin D + analogues (alfacalcidol) for renal bone disease. Cinacalcet for refractory hyperparathyroidism.
AVOID NSAIDs, gentamicin, IV contrast where possible, herbal nephrotoxins (aristolochic acid). Review all drug doses for eGFR. Pause metformin if eGFR < 30.

Counsel + decision-making re modality (haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, conservative). Place vascular access (AVF) ≥ 6 months ahead of expected dialysis. Hepatitis B vaccine. Transplant assessment + listing if eligible.

Multidisciplinary obstetric + nephrology care. ACEi / ARB stopped on conception → labetalol / methyldopa. Aspirin from 12 weeks. Increased risk of pre-eclampsia, preterm delivery, fetal growth restriction.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management of Common Conditions (MOH)

title: Renal stones (urolithiasis)
presentation: Sudden severe loin-to-groin colicky pain, restless, sweating
Nausea + vomiting
Haematuria (microscopic or visible)
Lower urinary tract symptoms (urgency / frequency) if stone near vesico-ureteric junction
Stone composition: calcium oxalate (most), calcium phosphate, struvite (infection), uric acid, cystine
redFlags: Sepsis + obstructed kidney → urgent decompression within 6 h
Persistent symptoms / not improving in 48 h

diagnostics.rationale: near 100 % sensitivity for stone; size + location

diagnostics.test: USS in pregnancy + children + < 5 mm probable stone
diagnostics.rationale: no radiation; lower sensitivity for ureteric stone

diagnostics.test: FBC + U+E + creatinine + calcium + urate + glucose + PTH (recurrent stones)

management.detail: Diclofenac 75 mg IM / suppository (more effective than opioid for renal colic — Cochrane). Alternative: paracetamol IV 1 g. Add IV morphine if severe / NSAID contraindicated. Antiemetic.
80 % pass spontaneously within 4 weeks. Strain urine to capture stone. α-blocker (tamsulosin 400 µg OD) — expulsive therapy for 5–10 mm ureteric stones (mostly distal ureter).

management.step: Refractory pain or stones > 5 mm — urology referral
management.detail: Ureteroscopy + lithotripsy (URS) — first-line for ureteric stones / impacted stones. ESWL (extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy) for renal pelvis + upper ureteric stones < 2 cm. PCNL (percutaneous nephrolithotomy) for staghorn / large stones.
IV antibiotic + urgent decompression within 6–12 h: percutaneous nephrostomy (preferred) or ureteric stent. Definitive stone treatment delayed until infection cleared.

management.step: Recurrence prevention (lifetime risk 50 % after first stone)
management.detail: Fluid intake 2.5 L/day. Reduce sodium + animal protein. Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day (low-Ca diet INCREASES oxalate stones). Specific: hypercalciuria → thiazide; hyperuricaemia → allopurinol + alkalinise urine; recurrent struvite → identify + treat infection.
USS first-line. Tamsulosin acceptable. Analgesia: paracetamol → opioid → avoid NSAID. Ureteroscopy is safe in pregnancy. Stent / nephrostomy for obstruction.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Asthma — chronic management (GINA)
presentation: Recurrent episodes of wheeze, cough, breathlessness, chest tightness — variable + reversible
Worse at night / early morning / exercise / triggers (cold air, infection, allergen, NSAID, β-blocker)
Family / personal atopic history
GINA assessment: symptoms / SABA use ≥ 2 days per week, nocturnal awakening, activity limitation
redFlags: Previous ICU admission / intubation for asthma
Frequent SABA use (canister/month — > 3 = uncontrolled, > 12 = increased death risk)

diagnostics.rationale: FEV1 / FVC reduced + > 12 % + 200 mL improvement after SABA = reversible obstruction

diagnostics.test: Skin prick / specific IgE — atopy assessment

management.detail: Smoking cessation (active + passive). Allergen avoidance. Vaccinate (annual flu, pneumococcal). Inhaler technique check at each visit.
Step 1–2: low-dose ICS-formoterol PRN. Step 3: low-dose ICS-formoterol maintenance + reliever (MART). Step 4: medium-dose ICS-formoterol MART. Step 5: high-dose + add-on (LAMA, biologic).
Step 1–2: ICS daily + SABA PRN. Step 3: low-dose ICS-LABA + SABA. Step 4: medium-dose ICS-LABA + SABA. Step 5: high-dose ICS-LABA + add-on.

LAMA (tiotropium) for ≥ step 4. Leukotriene receptor antagonist (montelukast — adolescent monitoring for psychiatric AE). Theophylline (specialist). Macrolide (azithromycin) for neutrophilic asthma (specialist).

Omalizumab (IgE-driven), mepolizumab / benralizumab (eosinophilic), dupilumab (Type 2 + atopic + nasal polyp). Specialist-only after maximised conventional therapy + uncontrolled despite optimised step 4–5.
ICS + LABA + SABA — all safe + ESSENTIAL (uncontrolled asthma worse for fetus than medications). Continue maintenance. Manage exacerbations as in non-pregnant.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management of Common Conditions (MOH)

title: COPD — chronic management (GOLD)
presentation: Persistent respiratory symptoms + airflow limitation due to airway / alveolar abnormalities, usually from significant tobacco / biomass exposure
Chronic productive cough, wheeze, exertional dyspnoea worsening over years
MRC dyspnoea scale 1–5
Cor pulmonale features in advanced disease
SSA — biomass fuel exposure in women (cooking smoke) is major + under-recognised cause
redFlags: Cor pulmonale (peripheral oedema, raised JVP, hepatomegaly)

diagnostics.rationale: diagnostic; severity by FEV1 (GOLD 1 ≥ 80, GOLD 2 50–79, GOLD 3 30–49, GOLD 4 < 30)

diagnostics.test: CAT (COPD Assessment Test) + mMRC dyspnoea scale + exacerbation history
diagnostics.rationale: ABE classification: A (low symptoms + low exacerbations), B (high symptoms + low exacerbations), E (frequent exacerbations)
guides ICS use: > 0.3 strong indication, < 0.1 no benefit

management.step: Smoking + biomass cessation — single most important intervention
management.detail: Brief intervention at every contact. Behavioural + pharmacological (NRT, varenicline, bupropion). Biomass cooking — improve ventilation, switch to clean fuel (LPG, electric) where feasible.
Annual influenza, 5-yearly pneumococcal, COVID, RSV (≥ 60 yrs in some settings).

Group A: bronchodilator (SAMA / SABA / LAMA / LABA). Group B: LAMA + LABA combination. Group E: LAMA + LABA + ICS if eos > 0.3 or asthma overlap. Avoid ICS monotherapy. Use LAMA-LABA (tiotropium/olodaterol, indacaterol/glycopyrronium, umeclidinium/vilanterol) for Group B/E.
ALL symptomatic patients (mMRC ≥ 2) — exercise training + education + nutritional + psychological support × 6–8 weeks. Reduces hospital admission + improves QoL.
Indications: PaO₂ ≤ 7.3 (or ≤ 8.0 with cor pulmonale / secondary polycythaemia). Improves survival. Smoking cessation required.

Roflumilast (PDE4 inhibitor) — chronic bronchitis phenotype + frequent exacerbations + FEV1 < 50 %. Macrolide (azithromycin 250 mg OD or 500 mg 3×/week) — frequent exacerbations not on smoking. Lung-volume reduction surgery / bronchoscopic valves — emphysematous phenotype with hyperinflation. Lung transplantation in selected.
Advance care planning. Palliative care input. Opioid for refractory breathlessness. Anxiolytic + non-pharm dyspnoea management.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management of Common Conditions (MOH)

title: Type 2 diabetes — chronic management
presentation: Asymptomatic on screening — fasting plasma glucose ≥ 7.0 / HbA1c ≥ 48 (6.5 %) / OGTT 2-h ≥ 11.1
Polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss / weight gain, fatigue, recurrent infections
Complications at diagnosis (10–30 %) — retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, ASCVD, MI / stroke
SSA — rising prevalence with urbanisation; later presentations + younger age + thinner phenotypes than Western diabetes
redFlags: HbA1c > 86 (10 %) with weight loss / ketones — exclude T1DM / LADA / pancreatic disease

diagnostics.rationale: individualised target (typically 53 mmol/mol = 7 %, but 58–69 for elderly / frail / multimorbid)

diagnostics.test: Annual lipids + BP + weight + foot exam + eye screen (retinal photography)

management.detail: Structured education (DESMOND / similar). Weight loss 5–10 % if BMI > 25. Mediterranean / low-GI diet. Physical activity 150 min/week moderate. Smoking cessation. Alcohol moderation.
Metformin 500 mg OD with food, titrate to 1 g BD (or MR if intolerant). Continue while tolerated + eGFR > 30 (caution 30–45).

management.step: Second agent — choose by patient phenotype (ADA 2024)
management.detail: ASCVD / HF / CKD: SGLT2i (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) — major outcome benefit. ASCVD without CKD: GLP-1 RA (semaglutide, liraglutide). Cost / availability: sulfonylurea (gliclazide). Weight concern: SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA. Hypoglycaemia concern: DPP-4i (sitagliptin).

management.step: Insulin — start when HbA1c persistently high despite oral max
management.detail: Basal-only first (NPH or glargine 10 units OD or 0.1–0.2 units/kg, titrate by FBM 4–7 mmol/L). Intensify with prandial when HbA1c not at target. Premix 30/70 BD for resource-limited / simple regimen.

BP < 130/80 — ACEi/ARB first-line (esp. with albuminuria). LDL: statin (atorvastatin 20 mg) for primary prevention (most T2DM); LDL target < 1.8 in CVD or > 75 yrs at high risk. Aspirin only secondary prevention. Annual foot care + flu vaccine + pneumococcal.

Pre-conception: HbA1c < 48 ideal, folic acid 5 mg, switch to safer agents. Pregnancy: metformin acceptable + insulin first-line; stop GLP-1, SGLT2i, DPP-4i, statin, ACEi. Postpartum: re-initiate non-pregnancy regimen + continue breastfeeding (insulin + metformin compatible).

references.label: Kenya National Clinical Guidelines for Management of Diabetes Mellitus, Ministry of Health

title: Hypertension — chronic management
presentation: Usually asymptomatic — 'silent killer'
Detected on screening — confirm with ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) or home BPM ≥ 7 days
Stage 1: clinic ≥ 140/90 + ABPM ≥ 135/85. Stage 2: clinic ≥ 160/100 + ABPM ≥ 150/95. Severe: ≥ 180/110
End-organ damage — LVH, retinopathy, nephropathy, CV events
redFlags: Hypertensive emergency (SBP ≥ 180 + DBP ≥ 120 + end-organ damage) — see separate condition
Accelerated / malignant HTN (grade III/IV retinopathy + end-organ damage)
Secondary HTN suspicion — < 40 yrs + treatment-resistant + abrupt onset + clinical features (hypokalaemia, palpitations + sweating, abdominal bruit)

diagnostics.test: Confirm with ABPM (24 h) or 7-day home BP
diagnostics.rationale: rule out white-coat HTN; one-off readings unreliable

diagnostics.test: End-organ assessment — urinalysis + ACR, eGFR, electrolytes, fasting lipids + glucose, ECG (LVH)
Cardiovascular risk score (QRISK3 / SCORE2 / WHO/ISH chart)
Secondary HTN screen if clinical suspicion
diagnostics.rationale: renal artery stenosis (US Doppler), Conn (aldo:renin ratio), phaeochromocytoma (metanephrines), Cushing (cortisol), thyroid

management.detail: Salt < 5 g/day. Weight loss if BMI > 25 — each 1 kg reduces SBP ~1 mmHg. Aerobic + resistance exercise 150 min/week. DASH-style diet. Alcohol ≤ 14 units/week. Smoking cessation. Adequate sleep.

Treat stage 1 if: < 80 yrs + (CVD / target organ damage / CKD / diabetes / QRISK3 ≥ 10 %) OR sustained ≥ 150/95. Treat all stage 2. Treat severe (≥ 180/110) immediately. Target < 140/90 (< 130/80 if diabetes / CKD / CVD).

< 55 yrs / non-Black: ACEi (ramipril 2.5–10 mg) or ARB (losartan 50–100 mg). ≥ 55 yrs OR Black African / African-Caribbean (any age) without diabetes: CCB (amlodipine 5–10 mg). Add 2nd if not at target.

Add 2nd (ACEi + CCB or ACEi + thiazide-like). Step 3: ACEi + CCB + thiazide-like (indapamide 2.5 mg). Step 4 (resistant HTN — confirm adherence + check 24-h ABPM): spironolactone 25 mg (if K < 4.5); α-blocker (doxazosin) or β-blocker; refer to specialist.

Labetalol first-line (or methyldopa, nifedipine MR). Aspirin 75 mg from 12 weeks if pre-eclampsia risk factors. STOP ACEi / ARB / spironolactone on confirmed pregnancy (teratogenic). Severe HTN (≥ 160/110) — emergency see eclampsia / severe pre-eclampsia.
BP, U+E (especially if ACEi/ARB/spironolactone), ACR, lipids, weight, lifestyle. Re-assess CVD risk. Address comorbidities + adherence.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management (MOH)

title: Dyslipidaemia + statin therapy
presentation: Usually asymptomatic — detected on lipid screening
Tendon xanthomata + xanthelasma + corneal arcus (< 50 yrs) → familial hypercholesterolaemia
Triglycerides > 10 → pancreatitis risk + lipaemic serum
Family history of premature CVD (M < 55, F < 65)
redFlags: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) — heterozygous prevalence 1:250; homozygous 1:1M (devastating early CVD)

diagnostics.test: Non-fasting lipid panel (total, LDL, HDL, TG) — preferred over fasting (less burden, similar prognostic value)

diagnostics.rationale: secondary causes (hypothyroid, hepatic, renal, diabetes) + baseline

diagnostics.test: Familial hypercholesterolaemia screening (Simon Broome / DLCN) — total cholesterol > 7.5 or LDL > 4.9 with family history

management.step: Lifestyle for all + assess CV risk
management.detail: Mediterranean diet. Reduced saturated fat. Increase oily fish / nuts / olive oil. Aerobic exercise. Weight loss if BMI > 25. Smoking cessation. Alcohol moderation. Treat diabetes + HTN.
Atorvastatin 20 mg OD first-line. Aim ≥ 40 % LDL reduction. NOT routinely titrated to LDL target in primary prevention.
Atorvastatin 80 mg OD (or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg if statin-intolerant at high dose). Target LDL < 1.4 (ESC 2019).

High-intensity statin from time of diagnosis (atorvastatin 40–80 mg / rosuvastatin 20–40 mg). Add ezetimibe 10 mg OD. Refer to lipid clinic for cascade family testing + PCSK9 inhibitor consideration if not at target.
Fenofibrate 160 mg OD + omega-3 fatty acids 2–4 g/day + treat secondary causes (alcohol, diabetes). Reduce dietary fat. Avoid alcohol completely. Pancreatitis risk.
LFTs + lipids at 3 months. Don't stop statin for asymptomatic LFT < 3× ULN. CK only if myalgia / weakness. Annual review of adherence + CV risk.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Ischaemic stroke — acute + secondary prevention
presentation: Sudden focal neurological deficit — FAST screen (Facial droop, Arm weakness, Speech slurred, Time to call emergency)
Cortical: hemiparesis, hemianopia, dysphasia, neglect
Subcortical lacunar: pure motor / pure sensory / mixed motor-sensory
Posterior circulation: cerebellar ataxia, vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, drop attacks
Risk factors: HTN (most), AF, diabetes, smoking, dyslipidaemia, age, sickle cell (SSA), HIV, COVID-19
redFlags: Time of onset critical for thrombolysis / thrombectomy window
Cerebellar / posterior fossa — risk of brainstem compression

diagnostics.rationale: MUST be done before thrombolysis. Early ischaemic signs subtle in first 6 h

diagnostics.test: MRI DWI — definitive for ischaemic stroke
diagnostics.rationale: high sensitivity in first 24 h (vs CT)

diagnostics.test: FBC + U+E + glucose + INR + lipids + HbA1c + HIV + RPR (if SSA + atypical)

management.step: Hyperacute — IV thrombolysis (window 4.5 h from onset)
management.detail: Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg IV (max 90 mg) — 10 % bolus over 1 min, remainder over 60 min. Exclusion: haemorrhage on CT, recent surgery / trauma / bleed, BP > 185/110, INR > 1.7 / DOAC last dose, severe stroke vs minor stroke benefit-risk. Tenecteplase emerging alternative.
For large-vessel occlusion (ICA, M1, M2, basilar). DAWN / DEFUSE 3 — up to 24 h with perfusion mismatch. NIHSS ≥ 6 typical threshold. Stroke centre transfer.
Aspirin 300 mg load then 75 mg daily after 24 h. Dual antiplatelet (aspirin + clopidogrel) × 21 days for minor stroke / high-risk TIA (CHANCE / POINT).
Pre-thrombolysis: BP < 185/110. Post-thrombolysis: < 180/105 × 24 h. Otherwise tolerate up to 220/120 in first 24 h. Beyond 24 h: gradual reduction to < 140/90.

Antiplatelet — clopidogrel 75 mg OD (or aspirin + dipyridamole). High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg). BP < 130/80. Anticoagulate if AF (DOAC > warfarin in non-valvular AF). Carotid endarterectomy if symptomatic stenosis > 50 %. Smoking cessation. Diabetes control. Lifestyle.

Early multidisciplinary stroke unit. PT, OT, SLT. Swallowing assessment (NG feed if dysphagia). DVT prophylaxis. Catheter avoidance. Pressure care. Mood (post-stroke depression in 30 %). Driving advice — 1 month off after stroke (UK).

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Heart failure — chronic management
presentation: Dyspnoea, fatigue, ankle swelling, orthopnoea, PND
Reduced exercise tolerance — NYHA I–IV

Causes: ischaemic (most), HTN, valvular, cardiomyopathy (dilated, hypertrophic, restrictive), congenital, peri/myocarditis, alcohol, anthracyclines, infiltrative (amyloid, sarcoid, haemochromatosis), tachycardia-mediated, hyperthyroidism, anaemia
SSA — rheumatic heart disease + endomyocardial fibrosis + Chagas + HIV cardiomyopathy + peripartum CM
redFlags: Refractory to GDMT — advanced HF assessment (ICD, CRT, LVAD, transplant)

diagnostics.rationale: exclude HF if low; non-specific positive

diagnostics.test: FBC + U+E + LFT + TFT + glucose + lipids + iron + HIV
diagnostics.rationale: anaemia, electrolytes, HIV CM in SSA

management.detail: ALL 4 simultaneously, low-dose initiation, then titrate over 4–6 weeks: 1) ACEi (ramipril 1.25–10 mg) OR ARB OR ARNI (sacubitril-valsartan 24/26–97/103 mg BD); 2) β-blocker (bisoprolol / carvedilol / nebivolol — titrate weekly); 3) MRA (spironolactone 25 mg or eplerenone 25–50 mg); 4) SGLT2i (dapagliflozin 10 mg or empagliflozin 10 mg) — irrespective of diabetes.
SGLT2i (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin) — EMPEROR-Preserved + DELIVER. Diuretic for congestion. Control comorbidities (HTN, AF, obesity, sleep apnoea). MRA may help (TOPCAT).
Furosemide 20–80 mg OD-BD for congestion. Bumetanide alternative. Restrict fluid 1.5–2 L/day if symptomatic. Daily weight monitoring.
ICD: LVEF ≤ 35 % despite ≥ 3 months optimal GDMT + life expectancy > 1 yr. CRT: above + LBBB + QRS > 130 ms (≥ 150 strong; 130–150 conditional). LVAD as bridge / destination in advanced HF.
AF: anticoagulate (DOAC); rate control with β-blocker / digoxin. VT: optimise GDMT + ICD.
Stop ACEi/ARB/ARNI/MRA on conception. Switch to hydralazine + nitrate. Continue β-blocker (avoid atenolol — IUGR). Peripartum CM: bromocriptine + standard HF therapy + anticoagulate (high VTE risk).
Cardiac rehabilitation. Influenza + pneumococcal vaccine. Smoking + alcohol cessation. Dietary salt < 5 g. Patient education + self-monitoring (weights). Palliative care for advanced refractory.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Acne vulgaris
presentation: Open + closed comedones, inflammatory papules + pustules, nodules + cysts (severe)
Distribution — face, chest, back, shoulders
Mild: comedones + few inflammatory lesions. Moderate: many inflammatory + some nodules. Severe: extensive nodulocystic + scarring
Pubertal onset; persists into 20s–30s in 20 %
Hormonal (PCOS, late-onset)
redFlags: Nodulocystic / scarring — refer for systemic / isotretinoin
Acne fulminans (rare) — severe ulcerative + fever + arthralgia
Psychological impact — depression / anxiety / suicide screen

diagnostics.test: Hormonal screen if hyperandrogenism / hirsutism / menstrual irregularity — testosterone + SHBG + 17-OH-progesterone + DHEA-S + prolactin + TSH

management.detail: Gentle wash twice daily. Non-comedogenic cosmetics. Avoid picking / squeezing. Diet — moderate dairy / high-GI reduction (limited evidence). Allow 8–12 weeks for response to any therapy.
Topical retinoid (adapalene 0.1 % / tretinoin 0.025 %) at night + benzoyl peroxide 2.5–5 % AM. Add topical antibiotic (clindamycin 1 %) if inflammatory predominant (max 12 weeks).

Topical retinoid + benzoyl peroxide. Add oral antibiotic — doxycycline 100 mg OD or lymecycline 408 mg OD × 12 weeks max (resistance). Avoid topical + oral antibiotic combination (resistance). Always pair with benzoyl peroxide to reduce resistance.

Combined oral contraceptive — drospirenone-containing (Yasmin) or cyproterone-containing pills. Spironolactone 50–100 mg/day (off-label) — anti-androgen for adult female acne with hormonal pattern. Requires contraception (teratogenic).
Refer to dermatology. Oral isotretinoin 0.5 mg/kg/day × 16–24 weeks, cumulative 120–150 mg/kg. Strict pregnancy prevention programme. Lipid + LFT monitoring.
Treat active acne first. Microneedling, chemical peels, laser resurfacing, subcision, dermal filler for atrophic scars. Steroid injection for hypertrophic / keloid. Refer dermatology / plastics.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
presentation: Chronic relapsing pruritic inflammatory skin disorder — flexural distribution in older children + adults; facial + extensor in infants
Family or personal history of atopy (asthma, allergic rhinitis, food allergy)
Acute: erythema + papulovesicles + weeping + crusting. Chronic: lichenification + scaling + pigmentary change
Severity: mild (minor flares, easily controlled with emollients), moderate (significant pruritus + sleep disturbance + nuisance), severe (extensive + sleep loss + psychosocial impact)
redFlags: Eczema herpeticum (HSV superinfection) — sudden monomorphic vesicles + pustules + fever + lymphadenopathy → urgent IV aciclovir
Secondary bacterial infection (Staph aureus / MRSA) — golden crusting / impetigo features
Severe + refractory + failure of standard therapy → dermatology referral

diagnostics.test: Clinical diagnosis — UK Working Party Criteria
Allergy testing only if specific food triggers / contact dermatitis suspected
diagnostics.rationale: not routine — high false positives in atopic patients

management.detail: Greasy ointments (50:50 white soft paraffin/liquid paraffin) > creams > lotions. Minimum 250 g/week adult, 100 g/week child. Apply within 3 min of bathing. Use as soap substitute. Avoid aqueous cream (SLS irritant).

Mild (hydrocortisone 1 %) for face / flexures / infants. Moderate (clobetasone 0.05 %) for trunk + limbs in moderate flare. Potent (betamethasone valerate 0.1 %) for lichenified / severe trunk + limbs. Very potent (clobetasol 0.05 %) for severe palms/soles (≤ 2 weeks). Apply once daily until clear, then taper / maintenance 2× weekly (proactive therapy).
Tacrolimus 0.03 % (children) / 0.1 % (adults) BD, OR pimecrolimus 1 % BD. For face / flexures + steroid-sparing. ≥ 2 yrs. Common burning initially. UV avoidance.

Mild: topical fusidic acid 2 % × 1 week. Moderate-severe: flucloxacillin 500 mg every 6 h × 7 days. Eczema herpeticum: aciclovir 800 mg 5× daily PO (mild) or 10 mg/kg IV every 8 h (severe) + admit / ophthalmology if periocular.

Phototherapy (NB-UVB) first step. Oral immunosuppressants: ciclosporin 3–5 mg/kg/day (rapid effect, monitor renal + BP). Methotrexate 15 mg weekly. Azathioprine (TPMT activity first). Biologic: dupilumab 300 mg every 2 weeks SC. JAK inhibitors: upadacitinib, abrocitinib (specialist).

Avoid triggers (irritants, allergens, heat, stress). Cotton clothing. Manage sleep — sedating antihistamine (chlorphenamine) short-term. Eczema Action Plan + patient + family education. School / nursery liaison. Psychological impact assessment (depression, anxiety).

references.label: NICE CG57 Atopic Eczema in Children
Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (5th ed, 2022), Ministry of Health

title: Psoriasis
presentation: Chronic Th17-driven inflammatory skin disease

Plaque psoriasis (most common 80 %) — symmetrical erythematous well-demarcated silvery-scaled plaques on extensor surfaces, scalp, lower back, umbilicus, gluteal cleft, nails (pitting, onycholysis, oil-drop sign)
Guttate (post-streptococcal, young), inverse (flexural), pustular (palmoplantar / generalised), erythrodermic (severe extensive)
Comorbidities — psoriatic arthritis (30 %), metabolic syndrome, CVD, IBD, depression
Triggers — infection, stress, alcohol, smoking, drugs (β-blocker, lithium, ACEi, antimalarials, NSAID, withdrawal of steroid)
redFlags: Erythrodermic psoriasis — > 90 % body surface, systemic upset → admit + dermatology
Generalised pustular psoriasis (von Zumbusch) — fever + neutrophilia + admit
Suspected psoriatic arthritis — early dermatology / rheumatology referral
Mental health impact — high suicide rate

diagnostics.test: Clinical — Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding on scale removal), Koebner phenomenon
Joint screen — PEST (Psoriasis Epidemiology Screening Tool)

management.detail: Emollients liberally. Smoking + alcohol cessation. Weight loss if BMI > 25 (improves disease + comorbidity). Address mental health. Manage CV risk.

management.step: Topical therapy — first-line for limited plaque
management.detail: Potent topical corticosteroid (betamethasone valerate 0.1 %) + vitamin D analogue (calcipotriol 50 µg/g) — fixed combo OD or BD × 4 weeks. Coal tar / dithranol — older agents, less popular. Scalp: tar shampoo + topical steroid lotion.
Narrowband UVB (TL-01) — 3× weekly. PUVA (psoralen + UVA) for refractory. Skin cancer risk monitoring.

Methotrexate 10–25 mg weekly + folic acid. Acitretin 25–50 mg OD (teratogenic — strict contraception × 3 yrs after stopping in women). Ciclosporin 2.5–5 mg/kg/day (short courses). Apremilast (PDE4) 30 mg BD.

Anti-TNF (adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab). Anti-IL12/23 (ustekinumab). Anti-IL17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab — preferred for psoriasis-only). Anti-IL23 (guselkumab, risankizumab). Sequence depends on comorbidities + access.

Pregnancy: emollients + low-potency topical steroid + UVB acceptable. Stop methotrexate ≥ 3 months pre-conception. Acitretin × 3 yrs. Certolizumab pegol (no placental transfer) for severe. Erythrodermic / pustular flares: admit + ciclosporin + supportive.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Ulcerative colitis
presentation: Bloody diarrhoea + tenesmus + faecal urgency + abdominal cramping
Continuous colonic involvement from rectum proximally (rectum always involved)
Extent: proctitis (rectum only), left-sided (to splenic flexure), extensive (beyond splenic flexure)
Extra-intestinal: erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis, episcleritis, primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), seronegative arthritis
Severity (Truelove + Witts): mild < 4 stools/day, normal observations; severe ≥ 6 bloody + fever / tachycardia / anaemia / raised CRP
redFlags: Acute severe UC (Truelove + Witts severe) — admit; toxic megacolon risk
Toxic megacolon (transverse colon > 5.5 cm + systemic toxicity) — surgical emergency
Cancer surveillance after 8–10 yrs (colorectal cancer risk)

diagnostics.test: Stool — exclude infection (C. diff, Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, E. histolytica in SSA + travellers)
Bloods — FBC, CRP, ESR, U+E, LFT, albumin, ferritin, B12, folate, magnesium

diagnostics.rationale: definitive — continuous inflammation from rectum, crypt distortion + abscess + ulceration; rules out Crohn (which is patchy with skip lesions + granulomata)

management.detail: Topical 5-ASA (mesalazine suppository 1 g OD proctitis; enema 1 g OD left-sided) ± oral mesalazine 2.4–4.8 g/day. Add topical steroid (rectal hydrocortisone) if 5-ASA fails.
Oral mesalazine 4.8 g/day + topical mesalazine. Add oral prednisolone 40 mg taper × 8 weeks if no response in 2 weeks.

IV hydrocortisone 100 mg every 6 h (or methylprednisolone 60 mg/day) × 3 days. AXR + bloods + stool daily. Truelove + Witts on day 3 — if not responding (stool > 8/day OR CRP > 45 with > 3 stools), rescue with infliximab 5 mg/kg or ciclosporin 2 mg/kg/day IV. If no improvement at day 7 — colectomy.

5-ASA (mesalazine 1.5–3 g/day PO or topical) for proctitis / left-sided. Azathioprine / mercaptopurine if steroid-dependent or after ASUC. Biologics (anti-TNF, vedolizumab, ustekinumab, JAK inhibitors) for moderate-severe refractory / steroid-dependent.

management.step: Surgical — for failed medical / acute fulminant / dysplasia
management.detail: Subtotal colectomy + ileostomy (acute), followed by completion proctectomy + ileo-anal pouch (IPAA) for younger / motivated patients, OR ileostomy + Hartmann pouch / proctocolectomy in older / co-morbid.
Colonoscopy + chromoendoscopy / random biopsies every 1–5 years from 8–10 yrs from disease onset depending on risk. Concurrent PSC — annual surveillance from diagnosis.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Crohn disease
presentation: Chronic transmural inflammation anywhere mouth-to-anus; SKIP lesions
Diarrhoea (often non-bloody), abdominal pain (typically RIF), weight loss, fatigue, fever, growth failure in children
Perianal disease — fistula, abscess, skin tags (1/3 patients)
Complications: stricture, fistula, abscess, malabsorption, nutritional deficiency (B12 in terminal ileal disease)
Extra-intestinal — as UC + erythema nodosum + arthropathy
redFlags: Severe weight loss / failure to thrive (children)
Colorectal cancer risk in long-standing colonic disease

diagnostics.test: FBC, CRP, ESR, U+E, LFT, albumin, ferritin, B12, folate, vitamin D, magnesium, ZnO

diagnostics.rationale: skip lesions, deep ulcers, granulomata, terminal ileitis

management.step: Smoking cessation — most important modifiable factor
management.detail: Smoking doubles risk of relapse + halves benefit of medical therapy in Crohn. NOT a contributor in UC (opposite epidemiology).
Budesonide 9 mg OD × 8 weeks (low systemic AE — preferred over prednisolone for ileocaecal). Alternative: prednisolone 40 mg taper. 5-ASA limited benefit.
Prednisolone 40 mg taper × 8 weeks for induction. Initiate immunomodulator (azathioprine 2 mg/kg / mercaptopurine 1 mg/kg / methotrexate 25 mg weekly) or biologic for steroid-sparing maintenance.

Anti-TNF (infliximab 5 mg/kg, adalimumab 160-80-40) — first-line for severe / refractory / fistulising / perianal. Ustekinumab + vedolizumab alternatives. JAK inhibitors (upadacitinib) for moderate-severe. Combination of anti-TNF + immunomodulator (SONIC) — most effective.
MRI pelvis. Examination under anaesthesia. Drain abscess + seton drainage of fistula. Anti-TNF (infliximab) for fistulising disease. Antibiotics (ciprofloxacin + metronidazole) for sepsis.

management.step: Surgery — for stricture / fistula / abscess / failed medical / cancer
management.detail: Limited resection / strictureplasty. Recurrence at anastomosis common — endoscopic surveillance + post-op anti-TNF prophylaxis for high-risk.
Enteral nutrition (polymeric formula × 6–8 weeks) — effective induction in paediatric Crohn (CD-TREAT). B12 (terminal ileal disease / resection), vitamin D + Ca, iron, zinc. Dietitian input.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)
presentation: Heartburn (retrosternal burning, worse on lying / postprandially), acid regurgitation
Atypical — chronic cough, hoarseness, dental erosion, sore throat, non-cardiac chest pain
Complications: erosive oesophagitis, peptic stricture, Barrett oesophagus (10 % long-standing → adenocarcinoma risk 0.5 %/yr)
redFlags: Alarm features (ALARMS-55) — Anaemia, Loss of weight, Anorexia, Recent onset / progressive, Melaena, Swallowing difficulty (dysphagia), age > 55 with new symptoms → urgent OGD
Symptoms persisting despite full-dose PPI × 8 weeks

diagnostics.test: Empirical PPI trial × 4–8 weeks for typical symptoms without alarm features
OGD if alarm symptoms / failed PPI / new symptoms > 55
24-h pH-impedance + manometry (specialist) — for typical symptoms with normal OGD or atypical symptoms

management.detail: Weight loss if BMI > 25 (most effective single intervention). Avoid late evening meals (last meal ≥ 3 h before bed). Elevate head of bed 15 cm. Avoid triggers (fatty / spicy / caffeine / alcohol / chocolate / mint / citrus). Smoking cessation.
PPI (omeprazole 20 mg OD or pantoprazole 40 mg OD) before breakfast × 4–8 weeks. Alginate-antacid (Gaviscon) PRN for breakthrough. H2 blocker (famotidine 20 mg BD) alternative for mild.
Check adherence + timing (30 min before food). Increase to BD. Switch PPI. Add H2 blocker nocte for nocturnal symptoms. Refer for OGD + functional studies.
Step down to lowest effective PPI dose or alternate-day; PRN; or stop. Long-term PPI need: erosive oesophagitis grade C/D, Barrett, peptic stricture.

Surveillance OGD with biopsies every 3–5 years for non-dysplastic; every 6 months if low-grade dysplasia. Endoscopic eradication (radiofrequency ablation, EMR) for high-grade dysplasia / intramucosal cancer.

Fundoplication (Nissen / Toupet) — symptomatic young patients on lifelong PPI, after objective reflux on impedance study. Bariatric surgery (Roux-en-Y) — better for obese patients with GORD + obesity.
Lifestyle. Alginate-antacid first-line. Ranitidine (no longer available — NDMA recall) or famotidine. PPI (omeprazole most data) if essential.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Diabetic foot disease
presentation: Neuropathic ulcer (warm, painless, on weight-bearing area)
Ischaemic ulcer (cold, painful, distal — toes, heel)
Neuro-ischaemic (combination)
Charcot neuro-arthropathy — acute red hot swollen foot WITHOUT infection in neuropathic patient
Infection — cellulitis, deep tissue, osteomyelitis
redFlags: Osteomyelitis — bone exposed / probe-to-bone / non-healing > 4 weeks

diagnostics.test: Foot exam at every diabetes visit — inspection, monofilament, vibration, pedal pulses, ABPI
Wound assessment — TIME framework (Tissue, Infection, Moisture, Edge); University of Texas / Wagner classification
Bloods — FBC, CRP, HbA1c, U+E, lactate; cultures (deep tissue / bone)
Imaging — plain X-ray first (osteomyelitis, Charcot), MRI gold standard if suspicion + X-ray normal
Vascular — Doppler waveforms, ABPI (caution — calcified vessels falsely raise), toe pressures, CT angiography for revascularisation

management.step: Multidisciplinary foot team — refer ≤ 24 h for active ulcer
management.detail: Vascular + orthopaedic + diabetologist + podiatry + tissue viability + microbiology. Single point of contact for patient.

management.step: Offloading — cornerstone of neuropathic ulcer healing
management.detail: Total contact cast (gold standard for plantar ulcer) OR removable cast walker OR healing sandal. Reduce weight-bearing immediately at presentation. Counsel: 'every step delays healing'.
Daily dressings. Sharp debridement of necrotic / callus tissue (specialist). Negative pressure wound therapy for selected. Avoid foot soaking. Hydrogel for dry necrotic; absorbent for exudative.

Mild: oral flucloxacillin (or co-amoxiclav, doxycycline) × 7–14 days. Moderate: IV co-amoxiclav / piperacillin-tazobactam. Severe / sepsis: piperacillin-tazobactam / carbapenem ± vancomycin (MRSA). Osteomyelitis: prolonged 6 weeks (often surgical) — IV + oral targeted by culture.
Refer vascular urgently — angioplasty / bypass before wound will heal in ischaemic limb. Time-critical for limb salvage.

management.step: Charcot — total contact cast + non-weight-bearing × 3–6 months
management.detail: Acute swelling not infection. Refer foot team. Bisphosphonates controversial. Bracing long-term to prevent deformity.
HbA1c < 7 %. BP < 130/80. Statin. Smoking cessation. Iron + B12 + folate / D nutrition. Annual foot screen + education + appropriate footwear lifelong.

Required for: uncontrollable infection, gangrene, non-reconstructable ischaemia, intractable pain. Multidisciplinary decision. Pre-amputation: optimise wound + nutrition + comorbidities + psychology. Post: rehabilitation + prosthetic + contralateral foot protection.

references.label: Kenya National Clinical Guidelines for Management of Diabetes Mellitus, Ministry of Health

title: Diabetic retinopathy
presentation: Often asymptomatic until advanced — annual screening essential
Floaters, sudden vision loss (vitreous haemorrhage), gradual blurring (macular oedema)
Risk: duration of diabetes (most), HbA1c, BP, dyslipidaemia, pregnancy, ethnicity
Leading cause of blindness in working-age adults globally
redFlags: Sudden vision loss → vitreous haemorrhage / retinal detachment
Pregnancy — rapid progression risk; screen each trimester

diagnostics.test: Annual retinal screening — dilated fundus photography (mydriatic 2-field digital)
diagnostics.rationale: from diagnosis in T2DM; from 5 yrs duration in T1DM
macular oedema assessment + intravitreal therapy planning

management.detail: R0 (none), R1 (mild non-proliferative — micro-aneurysms), R2 (moderate-severe non-prolif), R3 (proliferative — neovascularisation). M0/M1 (maculopathy + / -).

Glycaemic control (HbA1c < 7 %; avoid rapid fall — paradoxical worsening). BP < 130/80 (ACEi/ARB). Lipids (statin + fenofibrate for diabetic maculopathy — FIELD/ACCORD). Smoking cessation. Aspirin in established CVD.
Annual screen + risk factor optimisation.

Macular oedema — intravitreal anti-VEGF (bevacizumab / ranibizumab / aflibercept) monthly initially, then PRN. Refractory — intravitreal steroid (dexamethasone implant) or laser. Proliferative — panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) + anti-VEGF.
Vitrectomy for non-clearing vitreous haemorrhage > 1 month, tractional retinal detachment, severe proliferative disease.
Screen pre-conception + each trimester + postpartum. Treat sight-threatening disease aggressively. Anti-VEGF generally avoided in pregnancy — laser preferred. Tight glycaemic control important.

references.label: Kenya National Clinical Guidelines for Management of Diabetes Mellitus, Ministry of Health

title: Breast cancer — diagnostic pathway + early management
presentation: New unilateral palpable breast lump (~90 % of presenting cancers); often painless
Skin changes — dimpling (peau d'orange), retraction, ulceration
Nipple changes — inversion, bloody / serous discharge, Paget disease (eczematous nipple)
Axillary lump
Inflammatory breast cancer — erythema + warm + oedematous breast without obvious mass
Risk factors: age, family history, BRCA1/2, prior chest wall radiation, ER+ exposures (early menarche, late menopause, late pregnancy, HRT)
Male breast cancer (1 % all breast cancers) — usually retroareolar lump
redFlags: Suspected inflammatory breast cancer — urgent referral (DO NOT trial antibiotics)
Suspected Paget disease of nipple — biopsy
Family history with BRCA — genetic counselling
Pregnancy / lactation — palpable lump still warrants triple assessment

diagnostics.test: Triple assessment in breast clinic — clinical exam + imaging + biopsy
diagnostics.rationale: definitive diagnosis pathway; refer 2-week wait if suspected cancer (UK)

diagnostics.test: Imaging — mammography ≥ 40 yrs / USS < 40 yrs / both for diagnostic
Core needle biopsy (or FNA if cystic)
Staging if invasive — CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± bone scan for ≥ stage IIB

management.step: Multidisciplinary team (MDT) — pathologist + radiologist + surgeon + oncologist + breast nurse + radiographer
management.detail: Decide neoadjuvant vs upfront surgery.

Breast-conserving with sentinel lymph node biopsy first-line for early-stage. Mastectomy for: tumour > 5 cm relative to breast, multifocal, contraindications to radiotherapy, patient choice, post-neoadjuvant non-response. Axillary clearance if positive sentinel + significant disease.

Premenopausal: tamoxifen 20 mg OD × 5–10 yrs OR ovarian suppression (goserelin / leuprorelin) + aromatase inhibitor. Postmenopausal: aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole 1 mg / letrozole 2.5 mg) × 5–10 yrs. Switch / extended therapy in selected.
Trastuzumab 12 months ± pertuzumab. Sequence: neoadjuvant chemo + HER2 → surgery → trastuzumab continuation. Cardiac monitoring.
Anthracycline-cyclophosphamide (AC) + taxane (paclitaxel / docetaxel). Decision based on size, grade, nodes, gene-expression (Oncotype DX / Mammaprint) for ER+ HER2-.
After lumpectomy. After mastectomy if: tumour > 5 cm, ≥ 4 nodes, positive margins.

Surgery + chemotherapy (after 1st trimester) acceptable. Avoid radiotherapy + tamoxifen + trastuzumab until postpartum. Diagnosis often delayed by physiological breast changes — high index of suspicion.

references.label: NICE NG101 Early + Locally Advanced Breast Cancer
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health

title: Prostate cancer — diagnostic + early management
presentation: Often asymptomatic — detected on PSA screening + DRE
LUTS (BPH symptoms also common in this age group)
Bony pain → metastases (axial skeleton)
Cord compression — late presentation, surgical emergency
Family history (paternal, fraternal — risk doubled), Black African / African-Caribbean (2× risk + earlier age + more aggressive), BRCA1/2
redFlags: Spinal cord compression — urgent MRI + dexamethasone

diagnostics.test: PSA — informed decision-making, especially men 50–70 (or 45 if Black African / family history)
diagnostics.rationale: counsel re false positives, over-diagnosis, biopsy risks; PSA > 3 ng/mL (50–69) or > 5 (70+) triggers referral
PIRADS scoring; mpMRI < 3 may avoid biopsy in some men

diagnostics.test: Transperineal MRI-targeted biopsy (preferred over transrectal — lower sepsis risk)
Staging — bone scan + CT pelvis ± PSMA PET for intermediate-high risk
Genetic counselling if family history / Ashkenazi Jewish / Black African / BRCA suspected
diagnostics.rationale: PARP inhibitor eligibility in advanced disease + family implications

management.detail: Low: PSA ≤ 10 + Gleason ≤ 6 + cT1c-T2a. Intermediate: PSA 10–20 or Gleason 7 or T2b. High: PSA > 20 or Gleason ≥ 8 or ≥ T2c. Very-high + metastatic.
PSA every 3 months, DRE annually, mpMRI annually, repeat biopsy at year 1 + then targeted. Treat if progression. Avoids over-treatment + side effects.
Radical prostatectomy (open / laparoscopic / robotic) OR external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) + brachytherapy boost + androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) × 6 months (intermediate) or 2–3 yrs (high).
ADT (leuprorelin / goserelin / degarelix) + intensification: docetaxel × 6 cycles OR abiraterone (with prednisolone) OR enzalutamide / apalutamide. Bisphosphonate / denosumab if bone metastases.
Abiraterone or enzalutamide or docetaxel or cabazitaxel or PARP inhibitor (olaparib for BRCA+). Radium-223 for bone-predominant. Palliative care input.

Spinal cord compression — dexamethasone + RT/surgery. Bone health — Ca + vit D + bisphosphonate / denosumab on ADT. Sexual + urinary side effects of treatment — patient counselling + ED / continence services.

references.label: Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health

title: Overactive bladder (OAB)
presentation: Urgency — sudden compelling desire to urinate, hard to defer
Frequency — > 8 voids/day
Nocturia — ≥ 2 wakings/night to void
± Urgency incontinence (urge incontinence)
Affects 10–15 % adults; increases with age
Triggers: caffeine, alcohol, fizzy drinks, bladder irritants, anxiety
redFlags: Haematuria — exclude bladder cancer (urgent cystoscopy + CT urogram)
Neurological cause — MS, spinal cord disease, Parkinson

diagnostics.rationale: fluid intake + voids + leakage + urgency episodes

diagnostics.test: Urodynamics — only in failed conservative / surgical decision

management.detail: Bladder training (timed voiding starting at shortest tolerated interval, gradually extend) × 6 weeks. Reduce caffeine + alcohol + fizzy drinks. Manage fluid intake (1.5–2 L/day, avoid evening). Pelvic floor exercises. Weight loss if overweight. Constipation management.

Oxybutynin IR 2.5–5 mg BD/TDS (cheap but anticholinergic burden), tolterodine 2–4 mg OD (lower CNS effect), solifenacin 5–10 mg OD (M3-selective), trospium (no CNS effect). Counsel re side effects + falls / cognition in elderly.
Mirabegron 25–50 mg OD — different mechanism, no anticholinergic effects. Avoid in uncontrolled HTN. Combination with antimuscarinic (combo studies).

Intravesical botulinum toxin A — 100 units injected at multiple sites; effective 6–9 months. Posterior tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS). Sacral neuromodulation (Interstim implant). Augmentation cystoplasty / urinary diversion (last resort).

Elderly: avoid oxybutynin (anticholinergic burden). Men with BPH: combine α-blocker (tamsulosin) with antimuscarinic. Mixed incontinence (stress + urge): treat predominant; weight loss + pelvic floor + duloxetine for stress component.

references.label: NICE NG123 Urinary Incontinence in Women
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Schizophrenia — chronic management
presentation: Positive symptoms — delusions, hallucinations, disorganised thinking, abnormal motor behaviour
Negative — flattened affect, alogia, avolition, anhedonia, asociality
Cognitive — attention, working memory, executive function
≥ 6 months total + ≥ 1 month active phase (DSM-5/ICD-11)
Onset typically late adolescence / early adulthood; men earlier than women
SSA — high stigma + treatment gap; mhGAP-supported community care models
redFlags: Acute agitation / violence risk to self or others
Command auditory hallucinations to harm self / others
First-episode psychosis (FEP) — Early Intervention service referral
Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (failure of 2 antipsychotics × 6 weeks each at adequate dose)

diagnostics.test: DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria — clinical assessment + collateral
Rule out organic — FBC, U+E, LFT, TFT, glucose, lipids, urine toxicology, syphilis, HIV, CT brain
diagnostics.rationale: rule out medical / drug-induced psychosis, esp. first episode

management.detail: Refer FEP to specialist Early Intervention service. Engage family + carers. Address substance use (cannabis, methamphetamine). Vocational + social support.

Atypical antipsychotic per patient preference + side-effect profile: aripiprazole (low metabolic + sedation), risperidone (effective + cheap), olanzapine (effective but metabolic + sedation high), quetiapine (sedation + sleep). Avoid haloperidol first-line in young patients (EPS). Start LOW, titrate slowly. Trial × 6 weeks at adequate dose before changing.
Switch antipsychotic if inadequate response × 6 weeks. Consider LAI (paliperidone palmitate, aripiprazole monohydrate) if non-adherent.
Clozapine — gold standard; clear evidence of superiority. Mandatory monitoring (FBC weekly × 18 weeks then 2-weekly × 1 yr then monthly). Cardiac + GI + metabolic screening.

Continue antipsychotic for ≥ 1–2 years after FEP, ≥ 5 years after recurrent episodes. Avoid abrupt discontinuation (relapse rate 60–80 % in 1 year). Address adherence — LAI for non-adherent / chaotic.

CBT for psychosis (CBTp), family interventions (reduces relapse 50 %), supported employment / education, art therapy, peer support, physical health monitoring (annual metabolic + CV risk + cancer screening), smoking cessation, dietary support.

Continue antipsychotic — relapse risk significant + neonatal effects manageable. Switch clozapine pre-pregnancy ideally (limited data, requires baby FBC monitoring). Plan delivery + postnatal support.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for the Management of Common Mental Disorders / Kenya-adapted WHO mhGAP (MOH)

title: Bipolar disorder
presentation: Bipolar I — ≥ 1 manic episode (often + depressive)
Bipolar II — ≥ 1 hypomanic + ≥ 1 major depressive; never manic
Cyclothymic — chronic milder variations
Mania: elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, flight of ideas, distractibility, risky behaviour, psychosis (severe)
Hypomania: same but milder + no psychosis + no severe functional impairment
Mixed features: simultaneous manic + depressive symptoms
Suicide risk 10–15× general population; highest in mixed + depressive phases
redFlags: Acute mania with psychosis — admit + sedation
Pregnancy — relapse risk + drug choice complex (avoid valproate, lamotrigine sensitive)
Postpartum — high relapse risk; consider prophylactic mood stabiliser

diagnostics.test: Mood diary + collateral history + Mood Disorder Questionnaire (MDQ)
Rule out medical — TFT, FBC, U+E, glucose, B12, folate, ANA, urine toxicology, CT/MRI if atypical / late-onset / focal neuro
Suicide risk assessment at every contact

management.detail: Severe / agitated: haloperidol 5 mg + lorazepam 1–2 mg IM (NOT olanzapine IM with parenteral BZD). Less severe: atypical (olanzapine 10–20 mg, risperidone 4–6 mg, quetiapine 600 mg, aripiprazole 15–30 mg) — first-line. Lithium 600–1200 mg/day titrated to level 0.6–1.0 mmol/L (slower onset 7–14 days). Valproate 750 mg/day → 1.5 g/day to level 50–125 mg/L. Hospitalisation for severe + safety concerns.

Quetiapine 300 mg OD. Lurasidone 20–120 mg OD. Olanzapine + fluoxetine combination (OFC). Lithium adjunct. CAUTION antidepressants alone — risk of mood switch + cycle acceleration; if used, always pair with mood stabiliser.

Lithium first-line (also reduces suicide + may slow brain ageing); levels 0.6–0.8 prevention, 0.8–1.0 active. Valproate second-line (AVOID in women of childbearing potential — Pregnancy Prevention). Lamotrigine — best for depressive-predominant bipolar II (slow titration to avoid SJS). Atypicals (quetiapine, olanzapine, aripiprazole-LAI).

Multidisciplinary perinatal mental health. Lithium continued (cardiac echo at 18–20 weeks) — D&C / cooling needed in labour to prevent neonatal toxicity. Quetiapine + olanzapine acceptable. Stop valproate ideally pre-conception. Lamotrigine continued with dose monitoring (clearance ↑ in pregnancy).

Sleep hygiene critical (sleep loss → mania trigger). Avoid alcohol + cannabis + stimulants. Psychoeducation. Family-focused therapy. CBT for relapse prevention. Suicide-safety planning. Annual metabolic + cardiac + thyroid + renal (if on lithium) screening.
Bipolar puerperal psychosis risk × 100. Restart / continue mood stabiliser immediately postpartum + close monitoring × 6 months. Plan support + sleep with partner / family.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for the Management of Common Mental Disorders / Kenya-adapted WHO mhGAP (MOH)

title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
presentation: Persistent inattention + hyperactivity-impulsivity > 6 months, present before age 12, in ≥ 2 settings, causing functional impairment
Inattentive — easily distracted, careless errors, difficulty sustaining attention, poor organisation, loses things
Hyperactive-impulsive — fidgeting, can't sit still, blurts answers, interrupts, restlessness
Combined — both
Adult ADHD — symptoms continue in 60 %; presents with chronic disorganisation, time management, relationship + employment issues, often co-morbid mood / anxiety / substance use
ASRS-V1.1 + DIVA-5 for adult diagnosis
redFlags: Stimulant misuse risk — drug + alcohol screen pre-prescribing
Cardiac history — pre-treatment ECG / cardiology if abnormality / FH sudden death
Co-morbid mood / anxiety / autism / tic disorder / substance use
Severe functional impairment at school / work / home

diagnostics.rationale: history from parents/teachers (children); adult — collateral from partner / family
NICE — psychiatrist / paediatrician / specialist nurse only diagnoses

diagnostics.test: Co-morbidity screen — depression, anxiety, autism, learning disability, substance use, tic disorder
Pre-stimulant baseline — BP, HR, weight, height, cardiac history + ECG if indicated

management.step: Children — psychosocial first; then medication if persistent + significantly impairing
management.detail: Parent + child training. ADHD-focused CBT / behavioural therapy. School support (Education Health Care Plan / 504). Diet + sleep hygiene + exercise. Medication if symptoms persist + impair.

Methylphenidate (Concerta XL 18–54 mg OD; Equasym XL; Medikinet XR) — stimulant, first-line. Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse 30–70 mg OD) — alternative stimulant. Atomoxetine (non-stimulant) for: substance-use risk, anxiety co-morbidity, tics, parental preference.
BP + HR + weight + height + sleep + appetite + mood + tics at every visit, weekly initially. Annual cardiac review. Drug holidays controversial (growth concerns) — individualise.

Specialist diagnosis (no GP independent). Methylphenidate / lisdexamfetamine + workplace adjustments. CBT. Coaching. Manage co-morbidities (depression, anxiety, substance use). Driving advice (improved with treatment).
Combine stimulant + non-stimulant. Try alternative stimulant. Treat comorbidities. Behavioural / coaching intervention. Sleep disorder treatment.

references.label: AAP Guidelines for the Diagnosis + Management of ADHD
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Acute coronary syndrome (NSTEMI / UA / STEMI)
presentation: Crushing central chest pain ± radiation to jaw / arm / back, > 20 min, not relieved by rest / GTN
Associated dyspnoea, diaphoresis, nausea / vomiting, syncope
Atypical in elderly, women, diabetes — silent MI common
Risk factors — HTN, smoking, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, family history, age, prior MI / stent / CABG
redFlags: STEMI — emergency PCI / fibrinolysis (see separate condition / rule)
Mechanical complication — VSD, papillary muscle rupture, free wall rupture

diagnostics.rationale: STEMI vs NSTEMI vs UA (no troponin rise or ECG change)

diagnostics.test: FBC + U+E + glucose + lipids + creatinine + LFT + INR

diagnostics.rationale: definitive — within 24 h for very high risk (haemodynamic instability, refractory pain, dynamic ECG, raised troponin); within 72 h for high risk

management.detail: Aspirin 300 mg PO chewed + clopidogrel 600 mg (or ticagrelor 180 mg loading). GTN SL spray if pain. Morphine 5–10 mg IV (if pain refractory). O₂ ONLY if SpO₂ < 90 %. ECG monitoring. IV access.
Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC OD (NSTEMI), OR enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD, OR unfractionated heparin (PCI-bound).
Aspirin 75 mg OD + ticagrelor 90 mg BD (or clopidogrel 75 mg OD if ticagrelor contraindicated). Continue post-PCI.

Immediate (< 2 h): instability / refractory pain / arrhythmia. Early (< 24 h): GRACE > 140 / dynamic ECG / raised troponin. Within 72 h: any positive troponin. Otherwise: invasive vs conservative based on stress test / CT angiography.

Aspirin 75 mg + (P2Y12 antagonist × 12 months). High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) + LDL < 1.4. ACEi (ramipril 2.5–10 mg) + cardio-selective β-blocker (bisoprolol 2.5–10 mg). MRA (eplerenone 25–50 mg) if LVEF ≤ 40 + diabetes/HF. SGLT2i / GLP-1 RA if diabetes + ASCVD. Cardiac rehabilitation.
Smoking cessation (varenicline OK after 1 week). DASH-Mediterranean diet. Exercise 150 min/week (cardiac rehab). Weight + BP + lipid optimisation. Influenza + pneumococcal vaccines.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Stable angina pectoris
presentation: Predictable retrosternal chest discomfort precipitated by exertion / cold / emotion, relieved by rest / GTN within 5 min
Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) class I–IV
Atypical in women, diabetes, elderly — fatigue, dyspnoea on exertion
Risk factors as ACS
redFlags: Crescendo / nocturnal / rest angina — unstable angina → emergency

diagnostics.test: CT coronary angiography (CTCA) — first-line in stable chest pain (NICE)
diagnostics.rationale: rules in/out CAD; reduces unnecessary invasive angiography

diagnostics.test: Functional testing (stress echo / SPECT / cardiac MRI) — alternative

diagnostics.rationale: if revascularisation considered + suspicion high after non-invasive

management.detail: Smoking cessation. Weight + BP < 130/80. Diabetes control. Exercise (after risk-stratified). Diet. Address mood + sleep apnoea.
β-blocker (bisoprolol 2.5–10 mg) AND/OR CCB (amlodipine 5–10 mg if β-blocker contraindicated). GTN PRN for breakthrough + before predictable exertion.

Long-acting nitrate (isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg OD — nitrate-free interval to avoid tolerance). Nicorandil 10–20 mg BD. Ivabradine 5–7.5 mg BD (only if HR > 70 + sinus rhythm + symptoms despite β-blocker). Ranolazine 500–1000 mg BD. Trimetazidine. Combine 2 from different classes.
Aspirin 75 mg OD. High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg). ACEi (ramipril) if LV dysfunction / diabetes / hypertension. SGLT2i if diabetes.

PCI for: persistent symptoms despite max medical therapy + significant stenosis on FFR/iFR (≤ 0.80) OR left main / proximal LAD disease. CABG for: multi-vessel disease + diabetes / LV dysfunction / complex anatomy (SYNTAX score > 22). Discussion at Heart Team.
All patients with new diagnosis + post-PCI / CABG. Improves quality of life + reduces mortality.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD)
presentation: Intermittent claudication — predictable calf / thigh / buttock pain on walking, relieved by rest within 10 min
Rutherford / Fontaine classification
Critical limb ischaemia (Fontaine III-IV) — rest pain (worse at night, relieved by hanging leg over bed) ± tissue loss (ulcer, gangrene)
Acute limb ischaemia — 6 Ps: pain, pallor, paraesthesia, pulseless, paralysis, perishingly cold
Risk factors: smoking (most), diabetes, HTN, dyslipidaemia, hyperhomocysteinaemia, family history
redFlags: Acute limb ischaemia — surgical emergency (6 h to limb salvage)
Critical limb ischaemia — rest pain / tissue loss
Diabetic foot ulcer with PAD (poor healing)
Atherosclerosis is generalised — concurrent IHD + stroke + AAA risk

diagnostics.rationale: 0.9–1.4 normal; 0.5–0.9 mild-moderate; < 0.5 critical; > 1.4 calcified (false reassurance — use toe pressures)

diagnostics.test: Duplex ultrasound + magnetic resonance angiography / CT angiography

diagnostics.rationale: before revascularisation; therapeutic angioplasty / stent at same time
