Stop DMT (most) before conception (DMT-specific wash-out period). Interferon + glatiramer relatively safe. Pregnancy relapse rate typically reduced; rebound in postpartum — restart DMT promptly. Breastfeeding compatible with some DMT (specialist guidance).

Before highly immunosuppressive DMT (anti-CD20, cladribine, natalizumab): hepatitis B, hepatitis C, TB, HIV, varicella. Influenza + COVID + pneumococcal annually. Avoid live vaccines on immunosuppressive DMT.
Multidisciplinary rehabilitation — physiotherapy, OT, SALT, neuropsychology. Exercise + cardiovascular health + smoking cessation + vitamin D + obesity management — modifies disease + symptoms.

references.label: ECTRIMS / EAN Guidelines on MS; ABN Treatment of MS; NICE NG220 MS

title: Motor neurone disease / amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (MND / ALS)
presentation: Combination of upper + lower motor neuron signs (without sensory loss).
Bulbar: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue fasciculation (10–25% present).
Limb-onset (75%): asymmetric distal weakness, wasting, fasciculation, hyperreflexia.
Cognitive / behavioural: 50% have mild cognitive impairment; 5–10% develop frontotemporal dementia overlap.
Progression typically 2–4 years to respiratory failure; ~10% slower progressors.
redFlags: Acute respiratory failure (FVC < 50%, orthopnoea, daytime sleepiness, morning headache) — advance NIV decision.
Severe dysphagia — aspiration risk; PEG decision.
Suspected reversible mimic (multifocal motor neuropathy, Lyme, HIV, syringomyelia, cervical spondylotic myelopathy).
FTD-MND overlap — early advance care planning + family support.

diagnostics.test: EMG + nerve conduction studies — denervation in multiple regions / segments; revised El Escorial / Awaji criteria.
Genetic testing (C9orf72, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS) for familial / younger onset.
diagnostics.rationale: Familial counselling + emerging treatments (tofersen for SOD1).
Respiratory monitoring; prognostic; guides NIV / PEG timing.

diagnostics.test: Cognitive screen (ECAS — Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen).

management.detail: Neurologist + nurse specialist + respiratory + dietitian + SALT + OT + physiotherapy + palliative care + neuropsychology + family + social work. Specialist clinic association with longer survival.
Riluzole 50 mg BD — extends survival 2–3 months. Edaravone IV 14-day cycles (off-label / limited approval). Tofersen (antisense oligonucleotide) for SOD1-associated. Stem-cell therapies emerging.

Discuss NIV (BiPAP) when FVC < 50% OR symptomatic (orthopnoea, morning headache, daytime sleepiness). NIV extends survival 6–12 months + improves QoL. Cough assist + mechanical insufflator-exsufflator for secretion management. Plan invasive ventilation discussion.
PEG when: > 10% weight loss, dysphagia, fatigue interferes with feeding, choking episodes. Earlier PEG (before respiratory decline) safer + better outcomes.

Spasticity: baclofen, tizanidine. Cramps: quinine sulfate 200–300 mg nocte. Sialorrhoea: atropine drops, hyoscine patch, glycopyrrolate, botulinum toxin to salivary glands, radiotherapy. Pseudobulbar affect: SSRI / dextromethorphan-quinidine.
Mobility aids → wheelchair (powered); environmental controls (eye-tracking, head-mouse); communication device (high-tech AAC); home adaptations.
Depression + anxiety common — SSRI + counselling. Cognitive support if FTD overlap. Carer well-being + respite + financial benefits.
Early conversations about ceiling of intervention, NIV / tracheostomy, place of death, voluntary assisted dying (where legal). Compassionate end-of-life care; hospice involvement.

references.label: NICE NG42 Motor neurone disease; American Academy of Neurology ALS Guideline; EFNS / ENN

title: Duchenne / Becker muscular dystrophy — comprehensive management
presentation: Duchenne: progressive proximal weakness from age 2–5; Gowers sign; calf pseudohypertrophy; loss of ambulation 9–14 years; respiratory failure + cardiomyopathy 20s.
Becker: milder later-onset (after age 16); ambulation often into adulthood.
X-linked recessive — dystrophin gene mutations.
Cardiac: dilated cardiomyopathy + conduction abnormalities — leading cause of death.
Cognitive impairment in 30% (less than IQ 70).
redFlags: Suspected cardiomyopathy — annual echo + ECG from age 6 (asymptomatic dysfunction common).
Long-bone fracture — common from corticosteroid-induced osteoporosis + falls.
Anaesthetic — malignant-hyperthermia-like risk + rhabdomyolysis with halogenated agents + suxamethonium.

diagnostics.test: Genetic testing — dystrophin gene MLPA + sequencing.
diagnostics.rationale: Confirmation + identifies amenable mutations for emerging therapies.

diagnostics.test: Muscle biopsy if genetic inconclusive — absent / reduced dystrophin on IHC.
Annual pulmonary function tests (sitting + supine FVC) once over 6 years.
Bone density DEXA; vitamin D + calcium.

management.detail: Pediatric neurologist + cardiologist + pulmonologist + orthopaedic surgeon + physiotherapist + OT + SALT + dietitian + endocrinologist + genetic counsellor + psychologist + social worker.

Deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day OR prednisolone 0.75 mg/kg/day; start before significant decline (age 4–5 in DMD). Slows progression + delays loss of ambulation + cardiomyopathy + respiratory decline. Monitor: weight, growth, BP, glucose, bone (DEXA, vitamin D, calcium), cataract (annual eye review), behaviour.
Start ACEi from age 10 OR at first sign of LV dysfunction; add beta-blocker. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist for advanced. Anticoagulate for thrombus / atrial fibrillation.

Nocturnal NIV for hypoventilation (FVC < 50% or symptomatic). Cough-assist + manual assist for secretion management. Influenza + pneumococcal vaccinations. Surveillance + spinal management to optimise restriction.

Eteplirsen (exon 51 skip), golodirsen (exon 53), casimersen (exon 45), viltolarsen (exon 53) — for amenable mutations. Ataluren for nonsense mutation DMD (some countries). Delandistrogene moxeparvovec (gene therapy) — emerging.
Ankle-foot orthoses, mobility devices, manual / powered wheelchair, standing frame. Scoliosis surveillance + spinal fusion (in non-ambulatory adolescent for severe progressive curve).

Steroid-induced complications: osteoporosis (vitamin D + bisphosphonate for fractures), short stature, delayed puberty (testosterone replacement), insulin resistance / T2DM, adrenal insufficiency (stress-dose steroids).
AVOID halogenated volatile anaesthetics + suxamethonium (rhabdomyolysis + cardiac arrest). Use TIVA propofol-based; experienced paediatric / neuromuscular anaesthetist.
Adult MDC follow-up after age 18. NIV / tracheostomy decisions. Advance care planning. Mental-health support + dating + employment + independent living considerations.
X-linked — female carriers may have manifesting Duchenne (cardiomyopathy / mild weakness) — screen + monitor. Prenatal + pre-implantation genetic diagnosis for future pregnancies.

references.label: DMD Care Considerations Working Group (Bushby et al. Lancet Neurology 2010, updated 2018)

title: Systemic amyloidosis — AL + ATTR
presentation: Multi-system + non-specific — often delayed diagnosis.

AL (light chain) amyloidosis: clonal plasma-cell light-chain deposition; cardiac (restrictive cardiomyopathy + heart failure), renal (nephrotic-range proteinuria + AKI), peripheral / autonomic neuropathy, hepatomegaly, periorbital purpura, macroglossia.

ATTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis: wild-type (age-related, elderly males, carpal tunnel + cardiomyopathy + spinal stenosis) OR hereditary (autosomal dominant + ethnicity-specific mutations) — neuropathy + cardiomyopathy.
AA (secondary) amyloidosis: chronic inflammation (RA, IBD, FMF, chronic infection) — predominantly renal.
redFlags: Heart failure with preserved EF + thickened heart on echo + low voltages on ECG — consider amyloid (especially elderly + Black ethnicity for ATTR-V122I).
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome + heart failure — ATTR wild-type.
Family history of cardiomyopathy / neuropathy — hereditary ATTR.

diagnostics.test: Tissue biopsy with Congo red staining — apple-green birefringence under polarised light.
diagnostics.rationale: Confirms amyloid; biopsy fat pad / minor salivary / suspected organ.

diagnostics.test: Immunohistochemistry + mass spectrometry of biopsy for typing (AL vs ATTR vs AA).
Serum + urine immunofixation + free light chains (AL screen).
Echocardiogram + cardiac MRI + cardiac biomarkers (BNP, troponin) + 99mTc-DPD / PYP scintigraphy for ATTR.
diagnostics.rationale: Cardiac involvement assessment; 99mTc-PYP > 1.5 specific for ATTR cardiomyopathy.

diagnostics.test: U&E, urine PCR / ACR, LFT, coagulation, FBC.

management.detail: Haematology + cardiology + nephrology + neurology + genetics. Specialist centres improve outcomes significantly.

Daratumumab-CyBorD (daratumumab + cyclophosphamide + bortezomib + dexamethasone) × 6 cycles — first-line per ANDROMEDA. Autologous stem-cell transplant in selected. Targeted to eliminate plasma-cell clone. Cardiac involvement determines prognosis + treatment intensity.

Tafamidis 61 mg or 80 mg daily — stabilises TTR; improves survival in cardiac ATTR. Patisiran (siRNA) IV every 3 weeks OR inotersen / vutrisiran SC — TTR-silencing for ATTR neuropathy. Treats both hereditary + wild-type ATTR.
Aggressive control of chronic disease (RA: methotrexate + biologic; FMF: colchicine; chronic infection: eradication). Eprodisate (where available).

Cautious diuretic (avoid hypotension); avoid digoxin (binds amyloid + arrhythmia risk); avoid ACEi if severe hypotension. Beta-blocker often poorly tolerated. Pacemaker for advanced conduction disease. Transplantation in selected centres.
Standard CKD management; dialysis when ESRD; renal transplant requires amyloid control.
Pain (gabapentin / pregabalin / duloxetine); orthostatic hypotension (midodrine, fludrocortisone); incontinence; sexual dysfunction; physiotherapy + occupational therapy.
First-degree relatives — TTR genetic + early monitoring.

references.label: BCSH Guidelines on Diagnosis and Management of AL Amyloidosis; ATTR-ACT trial; ANDROMEDA daratumumab

title: Cushing syndrome — diagnosis + treatment
presentation: Weight gain (central + buffalo hump + supraclavicular pad), moon face, plethora, purple striae > 1 cm, easy bruising, proximal myopathy, hirsutism, acne, menstrual irregularity, depression / psychosis / cognitive change, hypertension, glucose intolerance, osteoporosis, infection susceptibility.

Causes: ACTH-dependent — pituitary adenoma (Cushing disease, 70%), ectopic ACTH (small-cell lung cancer, carcinoid, others, 10%). ACTH-independent — adrenal adenoma / carcinoma / hyperplasia (20%). Exogenous (most common!): therapeutic glucocorticoid.
redFlags: Severe Cushing syndrome — random cortisol > 1000 nmol/L; high mortality untreated.
Ectopic ACTH from carcinoma — concurrent malignancy + rapid onset + hypokalaemia + hyperpigmentation.
Cushing crisis: severe hypokalaemia + hyperglycaemia + sepsis + thromboembolism.
Pregnancy + Cushing — high maternal + fetal mortality.

diagnostics.test: First confirm Cushing syndrome (≥ 2 of): 24-h urinary free cortisol × 2; late-night salivary cortisol × 2; 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test (cortisol > 50 nmol/L); midnight serum cortisol.
Plasma ACTH at 9 am — distinguishes ACTH-dependent (raised / normal) from independent (suppressed).
If ACTH-dependent: high-dose dexamethasone suppression test + CRH stimulation + pituitary MRI + petrosal sinus sampling.
diagnostics.rationale: Distinguish pituitary (Cushing disease) from ectopic ACTH.

diagnostics.test: If ACTH-independent: adrenal CT / MRI; adrenal vein sampling for bilateral disease.
Baseline + ongoing: BP, HbA1c, lipids, U&E (hypokalaemia), DEXA, FBC, screen for infection.

management.step: Treat the cause — surgery is mainstay
management.detail: Cushing disease: trans-sphenoidal pituitary adenomectomy — first-line (60–90% cure). Adrenal adenoma / carcinoma: adrenalectomy. Ectopic ACTH: resect source if possible; otherwise medical + bilateral adrenalectomy.

management.step: Medical therapy — bridge or for non-surgical cases
management.detail: Steroidogenesis inhibitors: ketoconazole 400–1200 mg/day (LFT monitoring), metyrapone 500–4000 mg/day (hypokalaemia, hirsutism), osilodrostat 4–60 mg/day (newer, more potent). Combinations for refractory. Mifepristone (glucocorticoid receptor antagonist) for hyperglycaemia / hypertension.
Adjunct after failed / partially successful surgery; works slowly (months-years); risk of panhypopituitarism.
Severe / refractory Cushing — bilateral adrenalectomy + lifelong glucocorticoid + mineralocorticoid replacement. Watch for Nelson syndrome (pituitary tumour growth after bilateral adrenalectomy).

Hypertension (often resistant — multiple agents); diabetes (insulin commonly needed); osteoporosis (calcium + vitamin D + bisphosphonate); hypokalaemia (K replacement + spironolactone); infection prophylaxis (PCP if severe lymphopenia); thromboprophylaxis (LMWH — high VTE risk).
Most patients become adrenally insufficient after curative surgery — replace hydrocortisone 15–20 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses (mimicking circadian) until HPA recovery (months to never).
Surgical treatment in 2nd trimester preferred; if medical needed, metyrapone preferred (limited data). Specialist multidisciplinary team.
Lifelong endocrine follow-up — recurrence in 15–25% of Cushing disease over 10 years; cortisol + clinical assessment annually; pituitary MRI periodically.

references.label: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline on the Diagnosis + Treatment of Cushing Syndrome (2008, updated)

title: Renal cell carcinoma — diagnosis + risk-stratified treatment
presentation: Often incidental finding on imaging; classic triad (haematuria + flank pain + palpable mass) in only 10%.
Constitutional: fever, weight loss, fatigue, anaemia.
Paraneoplastic: hypercalcaemia, polycythaemia, hypertension, Cushing-like, Stauffer (hepatic dysfunction without metastasis).
Subtypes: clear-cell (75%), papillary (15%), chromophobe, collecting-duct, sarcomatoid (high-grade).
Risk factors: smoking, obesity, hypertension, chronic dialysis, hereditary syndromes (VHL, hereditary papillary RCC, BHD, HLRCC).
redFlags: Suspected paraneoplastic features prompting renal evaluation.
Metastatic disease (lung, bone, liver, brain) at presentation.
Hereditary syndrome features — multiple / bilateral / young age + family history.
Vena cava tumour thrombus extension — high-risk surgery.

diagnostics.test: Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen + chest (or MRI for IVC thrombus extent).
FBC, U&E, creatinine, LFT, calcium, LDH, urinalysis.
Renal mass biopsy in selected — small tumour active surveillance candidate, unfit / metastatic patient.
Genetic counselling if young / family history.

management.detail: Urologist + oncologist + radiologist + pathologist.

management.step: Localised disease (T1–T2 N0) — partial vs radical nephrectomy
management.detail: Partial nephrectomy preferred for T1 (< 7 cm) — nephron-sparing, preserves long-term renal function. Radical nephrectomy for larger / centrally located. Open / laparoscopic / robotic per surgeon expertise.

management.step: Locally advanced (T3–T4) — radical nephrectomy ± lymphadenectomy ± thrombectomy
management.detail: Surgical resection with IVC thrombectomy if applicable. Specialist surgical centre.
Pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) for 12 months — based on KEYNOTE-564 trial showing DFS benefit in high-risk clear-cell RCC.

Risk-stratified by IMDC criteria. Favourable: ipilimumab-nivolumab OR cabozantinib + nivolumab OR pembrolizumab + axitinib / lenvatinib. Intermediate / poor: ipilimumab + nivolumab combination immunotherapy + TKI superior to single-agent. Cytoreductive nephrectomy for selected good-prognosis patients (CARMENA-defined).

management.step: Active surveillance for small renal mass (< 3 cm)
management.detail: Selected elderly / comorbid with small lesions — serial imaging every 6 months. Treat if growth > 0.5 cm/year or > 4 cm size.
Genetic counselling + screening; family screening; nephron-sparing surgery prioritised; bilateral surveillance imaging lifelong (VHL especially).

Years 1–2: CT chest + abdomen every 6 months. Years 3–5: annual. After 5 years: every 2 years × 5 more years. Stage-adapted intensity. Functional renal preservation. Survivorship — second-cancer risk.

references.label: EAU Guidelines on Renal Cell Carcinoma; NCCN Kidney Cancer; ASCO Guidelines
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Asthma in pregnancy — maintenance + acute management
presentation: Pregnant patient with pre-existing or new-onset asthma.
1/3 stable, 1/3 improve, 1/3 worsen during pregnancy.
Uncontrolled asthma harms more than medication exposure: pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, low birthweight, perinatal mortality.
Most acute exacerbations second trimester.
redFlags: Acute severe asthma in pregnancy — fetal hypoxia + maternal compromise.

diagnostics.test: Peak flow + spirometry monitoring (no fetal risk).
ACT or asthma control assessment at each visit.
Fetal monitoring (CTG, growth scans) during severe exacerbation.

management.detail: Most inhaled medications have established safety. DO NOT reduce / stop control medication during pregnancy. Counsel that uncontrolled asthma is more dangerous to fetus than medication.

Steps 1–5: ICS-formoterol (preferred MART), separate ICS + LABA, add LAMA, biologic for severe. Specific safety: budesonide best evidence + preferred ICS; salbutamol established; formoterol + salmeterol acceptable; LTRA (montelukast) acceptable; theophylline narrow window — monitor levels (lower in pregnancy).

Prednisolone 30–40 mg/day × 5 days — risk-benefit favours treatment of severe asthma over fetal exposure. Cleft palate small absolute risk first trimester (background ~0.1%, OR ~3 — absolute ~0.3%); use is justified for severe asthma.

Same algorithm as non-pregnant: O2 to SpO2 94–98% (target tighter than usual; fetal need); salbutamol via spacer or nebuliser; ipratropium; prednisolone 40 mg or hydrocortisone 100 mg IV; magnesium sulphate 2 g IV; IV salbutamol / aminophylline + intubation if severe. Continuous fetal monitoring; lateral tilt; obstetric input.

Omalizumab limited safety data — continue if benefit; pregnancy registries collecting data. Mepolizumab / dupilumab / benralizumab / tezepelumab — limited safety data; specialist decision; do not initiate new biologic in pregnancy unless severe + benefit > risk.

Continue asthma medication during labour. AVOID prostaglandin F2α (carboprost) for postpartum haemorrhage — bronchoconstrictor; use oxytocin / misoprostol / carboprost only if no alternative. NSAID for analgesia if not aspirin-sensitive.
All asthma medications compatible with breastfeeding. Postpartum check-up + asthma plan; uncontrolled asthma + new-mother is high-risk; community asthma nurse follow-up.
Written asthma action plan; trigger avoidance; inhaler technique check; flu + COVID + pertussis vaccination.

references.label: GINA 2024 Asthma in pregnancy; BTS / SIGN asthma; NAEPP Expert Panel Working Group
Kenya National Guidelines for Quality Obstetrics and Perinatal Care (EmONC), Ministry of Health

title: Anaphylaxis under anaesthesia / perioperative allergy
presentation: Sudden cardiovascular collapse + bronchospasm + skin / mucosal involvement during anaesthesia.
Common causes: muscle relaxant (rocuronium, suxamethonium most common globally), antibiotic (β-lactam, vancomycin), chlorhexidine, latex, blue dyes (patent blue, methylene blue), opioids, NSAIDs.
May be masked: surgical drapes obscure skin; muscle relaxant masks bronchospasm; vasodilator drugs given (anaesthetic agents) mask hypotension.
redFlags: Cardiac arrest under anaesthesia from anaphylaxis.
Operation cannot be delayed (emergency / life-saving) — adapt anaesthetic plan.

diagnostics.test: Recognise: sudden hypotension + tachycardia + reduced ETCO2 + raised airway pressure + skin / mucosal changes (when visible).
Mast-cell tryptase: take samples at 1–2 h + 6 h + 24 h post-event.
diagnostics.rationale: Confirm anaphylactic mechanism; baseline at 24 h (or > 6 weeks).

diagnostics.test: Document all drugs / latex / fluids / disinfectants / blood products administered with timing.
Specialist allergy referral within weeks — skin-prick + intradermal + IgE serology + drug-provocation testing.

management.step: Stop suspected trigger + 100% O2 + secure airway
management.detail: STOP infusion / drug. Increase FiO2 to 1.0. Reduce / stop volatile anaesthetic. Tilt head down. Communicate clearly with team.

management.step: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg (or IV in anaesthetised patient)
management.detail: Anaesthetised patient — IV adrenaline 50–100 microgram bolus titrated to response; INFUSION 1–10 microgram/min if persistent. IM 500 microgram into anterolateral thigh if no IV access.
Rapid resuscitation — anaphylaxis causes severe distributive shock + capillary leak; often need 4–6 L.

Vasopressin 1–2 units IV bolus then infusion. Methylene blue 1.5–2 mg/kg over 20 min for vasoplegic shock (caution serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs). Glucagon 1–2 mg IV if patient on beta-blocker.

management.step: Continue procedure if essential / safer than abandoning
management.detail: Avoid suspected trigger for remainder of operation; document on anaesthetic chart. Postpone elective surgery if possible.
Chlorphenamine 10 mg IV for skin manifestations; hydrocortisone 200 mg IV — no acute benefit; prevent biphasic reaction (limited evidence).
ICU / HDU 6–12 h for biphasic reaction (especially if hypotension / asthma). Inform patient + family of event.

Refer specialist allergy / anaesthetic-allergy clinic within 4–8 weeks. Skin testing for muscle relaxants, antibiotics, chlorhexidine, latex, opioids, propofol, blue dyes. Document confirmed allergen on medical records + allergy bracelet + give patient + GP letter for future operations.

references.label: AAGBI / RCoA Anaphylaxis Quick Reference Handbook (2021)
ASA / Anesthesia Patient Safety Foundation Anaphylaxis Guidelines

title: Sickle cell disease — comprehensive lifelong care
presentation: Inherited haemoglobinopathy — HbSS, HbSC, HbS-β-thalassaemia and other compound heterozygotes.
Newborn screening detects affected babies; symptoms emerge after age 6 months as fetal Hb falls.
Chronic haemolytic anaemia + recurrent vaso-occlusive complications.

Long-term complications: stroke (silent + overt), pulmonary hypertension, nephropathy, retinopathy, avascular necrosis, leg ulcers, priapism, splenic dysfunction, cholelithiasis, growth + puberty delay, cognitive impairment.
redFlags: Acute chest syndrome — see VOC pathway.
Stroke / TIA / cognitive change — TCD screening + transfusion programme.
Aplastic crisis (Parvovirus B19) — reticulocyte drop + falling Hb.
Splenic sequestration — sudden splenomegaly + falling Hb in young child.
Pregnancy + SCD — high-risk maternal + fetal monitoring.

diagnostics.test: Annual FBC + reticulocytes + LFT + U&E + UACR + LDH.

diagnostics.rationale: Stroke risk screening; intervention threshold > 200 cm/s middle cerebral artery.
TRV ≥ 2.5 m/s warrants right heart catheter.

diagnostics.test: Bone marrow / spine imaging if AVN suspected.

management.step: Patient + family education + comprehensive sickle programme
management.detail: Multidisciplinary specialist centre — haematology + paediatrics + adult medicine + obstetrics + transplant. Genetic counselling for family + partners. Disease education + crisis trigger avoidance.

Penicillin V prophylaxis from 3 months to at least 5 years (some continue lifelong post-splenectomy / severe disease). Pneumococcal conjugate + polysaccharide + meningococcal ACWY + B + Hib + annual influenza + COVID + hepatitis B vaccination. Travel-specific vaccines.

management.step: Hydroxyurea (hydroxycarbamide) — disease-modifying for ALL with HbSS / HbS-β-thalassaemia
management.detail: Start in infants from 9 months (BABY HUG); titrate to MTD or fixed dose 15–35 mg/kg/day. Reduces VOC, ACS, transfusion need, mortality. Monitor FBC every 2 weeks initially then every 2–3 months. Pregnancy: stop ≥ 3 months before conception.
L-glutamine (Endari) 0.3 g/kg BD; voxelotor 1500 mg daily (HbS polymerisation inhibitor); crizanlizumab (anti-P-selectin) IV monthly. Specialist initiation.

TCD ≥ 200 cm/s — start chronic transfusion programme (every 3–4 weeks; target HbS < 30%); continue indefinitely. Hydroxyurea + phlebotomy alternative once stable (TWiTCH trial). Allogeneic SCT curative for stroke-risk patients with matched donor.
Indications: stroke prevention, recurrent ACS, pre-operative, severe anaemia (Hb < 5), preconception. Iron chelation (deferasirox) when ferritin > 1000 / 2.5 g cumulative iron load.

management.step: Curative therapy — stem cell transplant + gene therapy
management.detail: Allogeneic HSCT (matched-sibling): curative; cures young patients with serious complications. Gene therapy — exa-cel (CRISPR / Cas9, BCL11A targeting) + lovotibeglogene autotemcel (lovo-cel, lentiviral gene addition) — recently approved for select patients ≥ 12 years (US, EU, UK).

Priapism > 4 h — see acute pathway. Avascular necrosis — joint preservation surgery, physiotherapy. Leg ulcers — compression + wound care. Cholelithiasis — laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic. Pulmonary hypertension — specialist PHT clinic. Nephropathy — ACE inhibitor for proteinuria; eGFR monitoring; dialysis / transplant for ESRD.

Preconception planning; hydroxyurea STOP 3 months pre; folate 5 mg/day; partner haemoglobinopathy testing; aspirin 75 mg from 12 weeks (pre-eclampsia prevention); regular high-risk obstetric monitoring; LMWH prophylaxis; transfusion programme for severe SCD.
Structured adolescent-adult transition clinic; mental health screening (depression + chronic pain coping); educational + vocational support; medication adherence support.

references.label: ASH Pocket Guide on SCD 2020; BSH 2018; STOP / SWiTCH / TWiTCH / SUSTAIN / RESHAPE trials
Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (5th ed, 2022), Ministry of Health
WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children

title: Cystic fibrosis — comprehensive management
presentation: Autosomal recessive CFTR gene mutations — most common F508del.
Newborn screening detects most cases (immunoreactive trypsinogen → second-tier DNA / further IRT → sweat test confirmation > 60 mmol/L Cl⁻).

Multi-system: progressive lung disease (bronchiectasis, chronic infection — S. aureus, H. influenzae, P. aeruginosa, B. cepacia, NTM), pancreatic insufficiency (steatorrhoea, FTT), CF-related diabetes (CFRD), distal intestinal obstruction (DIOS), male infertility (congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens — CBAVD), hepatobiliary disease (CFLD), osteopenia, sinus disease + nasal polyps.
Median predicted survival in well-resourced settings now > 50 years with modern care + CFTR modulators.
redFlags: Acute pulmonary exacerbation: increased cough, sputum, dyspnoea, weight loss, hypoxia, falling lung function.
Massive haemoptysis (> 240 mL in 24 h) — bronchial artery embolisation.
Distal intestinal obstruction syndrome (DIOS) — RIF mass + signs of obstruction.
Suspected CF-related liver disease (cirrhosis + variceal bleeding).
B. cepacia complex isolation — segregation + high mortality concern.
Lung transplantation eligibility (FEV1 < 30% predicted with declining trajectory).

diagnostics.test: Sweat test (chloride > 60 mmol/L) + CFTR genetic testing.
FEV1 + FVC at every clinic visit; CT chest at intervals; HRCT for structural disease.
Sputum culture + sensitivities (annual or more frequent + during exacerbations).
Annual oral glucose tolerance test from age 10 (CFRD screening).
Faecal elastase / 3-day faecal fat for pancreatic insufficiency.
DEXA from age 18 (or earlier if risk factors).
Annual nutritional + height / weight / BMI assessment.
diagnostics.rationale: Cornerstone outcome — BMI correlates with FEV1.

management.detail: CF consultant + nurse + physiotherapist + dietitian + pharmacist + social worker + psychologist; minimum quarterly review; annual comprehensive assessment.

management.step: CFTR modulator therapy — game-changer for eligible patients
management.detail: Ivacaftor (potentiator) for gating mutations (e.g. G551D). Lumacaftor/ivacaftor; tezacaftor/ivacaftor for homozygous F508del. Elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI, Trikafta/Kaftrio) — for ≥ 90% of CF patients with at least one F508del or eligible mutation. Dramatic improvement in FEV1, exacerbations, BMI, sweat chloride. Specialist initiation + monitoring.

Daily airway clearance physiotherapy (active cycle of breathing, positive expiratory pressure, oscillating PEP); nebulised hypertonic saline 7% (3–7 mL BD); inhaled mannitol; dornase alfa 2.5 mg daily (DNAse for thick mucus); exercise.

management.step: Inhaled antibiotics for chronic Pseudomonas colonisation
management.detail: Nebulised tobramycin (28 days on / 28 days off cycles), colistin, aztreonam. First isolation of Pseudomonas — eradication regimen (oral ciprofloxacin + nebulised tobramycin / colistin).
IV antibiotics (two anti-pseudomonal — e.g. ceftazidime / piperacillin-tazobactam + tobramycin) 10–14 days; intensified physiotherapy + nutrition support. Home IV antibiotic programmes.

Pancreatic enzyme replacement (Creon) at every meal + snack; weight-band dose + adjusted to stool fat / symptoms. Fat-soluble vitamin (ADEK) supplementation. High-energy diet (110–200% normal); supplemental high-calorie drinks; PEG feeding if BMI falling.
Insulin therapy preferred over oral agents (CFRD is unique pathophysiology). Basal-bolus regimen; monitor + treat hypoglycaemia. Avoid carbohydrate restriction (would worsen weight loss).
Ursodeoxycholic acid 15–20 mg/kg/day for cholestasis. Variceal screening + management. Liver transplantation for end-stage.
Refer when FEV1 < 30% predicted (or rapid decline); 6MWD < 400 m; pulmonary hypertension; recurrent severe exacerbations. Bilateral sequential transplant. 5-year survival ~60%.

Screen depression + anxiety annually (TIDES). Structured transition adolescent to adult. Fertility counselling — male infertility from CBAVD (assisted reproduction options); female fertility usually preserved but pregnancy plan + CFTR-modulator continuation in pregnancy (Trikafta safe + recommended).

references.label: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation Clinical Practice Guidelines (multiple); ECFS Standards of Care; UK CF Trust

title: Non-small cell lung cancer — molecular-guided treatment pathway
presentation: Cough, weight loss, haemoptysis, chest pain, breathlessness, recurrent pneumonia, paraneoplastic, asymptomatic incidental finding.
Histology: adenocarcinoma (50%), squamous cell (25%), large-cell, NOS.
Molecular drivers (adenocarcinoma): EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET ex14, RET, NTRK, HER2.
PD-L1 expression — guides immunotherapy.
redFlags: Brain metastases with raised ICP / seizures.

diagnostics.test: Contrast CT chest + abdomen + pelvis + brain MRI.
PET-CT for staging mediastinum + distant disease.
Tissue biopsy (bronchoscopy, EBUS-TBNA for mediastinum, CT-guided percutaneous, surgical) with HISTOLOGY + COMPREHENSIVE MOLECULAR PROFILING.
diagnostics.rationale: Driver identification mandatory for non-squamous; increasingly squamous too.

diagnostics.test: Liquid biopsy (ctDNA) — alternative or complementary, especially for resistance mutations.
diagnostics.rationale: Less invasive; sensitive for major drivers.

management.detail: Thoracic surgeon + radiation oncologist + medical oncologist + radiologist + pathologist + pulmonologist + specialist nurse.
Lobectomy (preferred) or sub-lobar (selected). Lymph node dissection. SBRT (stereotactic body radiotherapy) alternative if medically inoperable.
Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Atezolizumab (PD-L1 ≥ 1%) or pembrolizumab adjuvant. Osimertinib adjuvant × 3 years for EGFR-mutant resected stage IB-IIIA (ADAURA).

management.step: Stage III unresectable — concurrent chemoradiotherapy + durvalumab
management.detail: Concurrent chemo (cisplatin / carboplatin + etoposide / paclitaxel) + thoracic radiotherapy 60–66 Gy. Followed by durvalumab × 12 months (PACIFIC) — improves overall survival.

management.step: Stage IV — molecular-targeted FIRST in driver-positive
management.detail: EGFR mutation: osimertinib (1st line; FLAURA). ALK rearrangement: alectinib / brigatinib / lorlatinib (1st line; ALEX / CROWN). ROS1: entrectinib / crizotinib. BRAF V600E: dabrafenib + trametinib. KRAS G12C: sotorasib / adagrasib. MET ex14: capmatinib / tepotinib. RET fusion: selpercatinib / pralsetinib. NTRK: larotrectinib / entrectinib. HER2: trastuzumab deruxtecan.

PD-L1 ≥ 50%: pembrolizumab monotherapy (1st line; KEYNOTE-024). PD-L1 1–49%: pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-189 + KEYNOTE-407). PD-L1 < 1%: ipilimumab + nivolumab + 2 cycles chemotherapy (CheckMate 9LA) or chemotherapy + pembrolizumab.
Re-biopsy for resistance mutations (e.g. EGFR T790M / C797S / MET amplification / SCLC transformation). Switch / add appropriate next-generation TKI; re-biopsy informs salvage strategy.

Palliative radiotherapy for bone / brain metastases / haemoptysis / chest pain. Bisphosphonate / denosumab for bone metastases. Endobronchial stent / debridement for airway. Oxygen + opioid for dyspnoea. Pleural drainage / pleurodesis for effusion. Early specialist palliative care improves quality + survival (Temel NEJM 2010).

Cessation improves treatment outcomes + quality of life — at any stage. Survivorship: surveillance imaging (3–6 monthly years 1–2; annually years 3–5); psychological support; manage chronic complications.

references.label: ESMO + NCCN NSCLC guidelines; multiple molecular-targeted trials
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Chronic kidney disease G3–G5 — pre-dialysis management
presentation: Often asymptomatic until advanced; symptoms (fatigue, oedema, breathlessness, nausea, pruritus) develop at G4–5.
Causes: diabetes (#1), hypertension, glomerulonephritis, polycystic kidneys, interstitial / drug-induced, renovascular, obstructive.
Complications: anaemia, mineral + bone disease (CKD-MBD), metabolic acidosis, hyperkalaemia, malnutrition, cardiovascular disease, infection susceptibility.
redFlags: Rapidly progressive disease (eGFR drop > 5 mL/min/year) — refer nephrology.
Active urinary sediment (RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs) — biopsy candidate.
Approaching dialysis: G4 (eGFR < 30) — modality discussion + access planning.

diagnostics.test: eGFR + UACR every 6–12 months (more often if rapidly progressive).
FBC, U&E, calcium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D, bicarbonate, ferritin, transferrin saturation.
Hepatitis B / C / HIV (pre-dialysis / transplant workup).
Renal biopsy if active glomerulonephritis / unexplained.

management.step: Address underlying cause + modifiable risk factors
management.detail: Tight glycaemic control in diabetes (HbA1c ~7%); BP < 130/80 with ACE inhibitor or ARB (proteinuria) + SGLT2 inhibitor (now first-line addition in CKD with eGFR ≥ 20); avoid nephrotoxins (NSAID, contrast, aminoglycoside).

management.step: SGLT2 inhibitor — every CKD patient eligibility check
management.detail: Dapagliflozin or empagliflozin — eGFR ≥ 20–25 mL/min, with or without diabetes (DAPA-CKD + EMPA-KIDNEY). Slows decline + reduces CV events. Caution euglycaemic DKA in T2DM (sick-day rules).

management.step: Finerenone (non-steroidal MRA) for diabetic kidney disease
management.detail: 10–20 mg daily for T2DM + albuminuria — further cardio-renal protection on top of ACEi + SGLT2i (FIDELIO + FIGARO). Monitor K+.

management.step: ACEi / ARB — first-line for proteinuric CKD
management.detail: Titrate to maximum tolerated; tolerate K+ rise + creatinine rise up to 30% from baseline. Combine with SGLT2i. Avoid combining ACEi + ARB (no benefit, more harm).
First-line ACEi/ARB + SGLT2i. Add CCB then thiazide then spironolactone for resistant. Watch hyperkalaemia + AKI risk.

Target Hb 100–115 g/L (NOT higher — over-correction increases CV events). Iron repletion first: ferritin > 100, TSAT > 20%; IV iron preferred in CKD. ESA (epoetin / darbepoetin) when Hb < 100 + iron-replete. HIF-PHI (roxadustat) emerging oral alternative.

Hyperphosphataemia: dietary restriction + phosphate binder (calcium acetate / sevelamer / lanthanum). Vitamin D deficiency: cholecalciferol. Secondary hyperparathyroidism: alfacalcidol / paricalcitol; cinacalcet / etelcalcetide for resistant. Avoid high-Ca binders in advanced disease.
Oral sodium bicarbonate to maintain serum HCO3 ≥ 22 mmol/L — slows CKD progression + improves nutrition + bone health (UBI trial).
Patiromer or sodium zirconium cyclosilicate — enables continuation of ACEi/ARB at protective doses. Reduce K+ in diet.
Modality discussion (HD vs PD vs transplant first); vascular access (AVF preferred — 6+ months to mature) OR PD catheter; transplant referral pre-emptive; vaccination (HBV, pneumococcal, flu, COVID).
Elderly / multi-morbid: conservative kidney management (no dialysis) — symptom-focused; palliative team; advance care planning. Survival comparable in very elderly with comorbidities.

references.label: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline; KDIGO Diabetes in CKD 2022; DAPA-CKD + EMPA-KIDNEY + FIDELIO trials
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management of Common Conditions (MOH)

title: Atrial fibrillation — comprehensive AF Care Pathway
presentation: Irregular pulse; palpitations + breathlessness + fatigue + reduced exercise capacity; up to 1/3 asymptomatic.
Detection by routine ECG, ambulatory monitor (Holter, patch), implantable loop recorder, smartwatch.
Patterns: paroxysmal (< 7 days, self-terminating), persistent (> 7 days, cardioversion to restore), long-standing persistent, permanent.
Risk factors: age, hypertension, heart failure, valve disease, OSA, obesity, alcohol, hyperthyroidism, post-cardiac surgery, lung disease, sleep apnoea.
redFlags: Haemodynamically unstable (rapid ventricular response with hypotension / pulmonary oedema / cardiac arrest) — urgent cardioversion.
Pre-excitation syndrome (WPW) with AF — risk of degeneration to VF; avoid AV-nodal blockers.
Concurrent severe valve disease (mitral stenosis especially) — risk of LA appendage thrombus.

diagnostics.test: 12-lead ECG + ambulatory ECG monitoring (24 h–4 weeks).
TTE — LA size, LV function, valve disease.
Sleep study if OSA risk factors.
TOE if rhythm control without ≥ 3 weeks anticoagulation considered.
diagnostics.rationale: Exclude LA appendage thrombus before cardioversion.

management.detail: A — Anticoagulation / Avoid stroke. B — Better symptom management (rate + rhythm). C — Cardiovascular + Comorbidity optimisation.

CHA2DS2-VASc ≥ 2 (men) / ≥ 3 (women): apixaban 5 mg BD OR rivaroxaban 20 mg OD OR edoxaban 60 mg OD OR dabigatran 150 mg BD. Reduce dose per renal / age / weight criteria. Warfarin (INR 2.0–3.0) preferred for mechanical valve, severe mitral stenosis, antiphospholipid. CHA2DS2-VASc 1 (men) — discuss benefit. ZERO — no anticoagulation.

management.step: Rate control — first-line for asymptomatic / persistent
management.detail: β-blocker (bisoprolol, metoprolol) OR non-DHP CCB (diltiazem, verapamil — AVOID in HFrEF). Digoxin add-on / monotherapy for elderly / sedentary. Target HR < 110 (lenient) or < 80 (strict — if symptomatic / cardiomyopathy).

management.step: Rhythm control — for symptomatic / first onset / young / new-onset HF
management.detail: Cardioversion: pharmacological (amiodarone / flecainide IV) or DC (synchronised; 120–200 J biphasic). REQUIRES anticoagulation ≥ 3 weeks pre + 4 weeks post (or TOE-guided). Maintenance: flecainide (no structural HD), amiodarone (structural HD), dronedarone (caution HF), sotalol.

Indicated for symptomatic AF: paroxysmal / persistent that failed / not tolerating AAD; selected first-line for paroxysmal AF (HRS / EHRA / APHRS 2017 guidelines). Pulmonary-vein isolation; cryoballoon or radiofrequency. Recurrence 20–40% over 5 years; repeat ablation sometimes needed. EARLY ablation in HFrEF + AF improves outcomes (CASTLE-AF).
Alternative to lifelong anticoagulation in patients with high bleeding risk / contraindication. PROTECT-AF trial — non-inferior to warfarin.

Weight loss (10% reduction reduces AF burden — ARREST-AF). Sleep apnoea treatment (CPAP). Alcohol reduction (< 10 standard drinks/week). Blood pressure control. Exercise. Cardiometabolic optimisation.

management.step: Acute new-onset AF with rapid ventricular response
management.detail: Unstable: synchronised DC cardioversion. Stable: IV β-blocker (metoprolol 2.5–5 mg) OR diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg. Address precipitant (sepsis, PE, alcohol). Consider rhythm-control attempt < 48 h.

management.step: Anticoagulation reversal for bleeding / urgent surgery
management.detail: Dabigatran: idarucizumab 5 g IV. Apixaban / rivaroxaban: andexanet alfa OR 4-factor PCC 50 IU/kg. Warfarin: vitamin K + PCC.

references.label: ESC + ACC/AHA Atrial Fibrillation Guidelines (2023 + 2024 update); CASTLE-AF + EAST-AFNET 4 trials
Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Moderate-severe Crohn disease — biologic + advanced therapy pathway
presentation: Chronic relapsing transmural inflammation anywhere from mouth to anus; ileocolonic (~50%), ileal (~30%), colonic (~20%), perianal (~30%).
Diarrhoea (often non-bloody) + abdominal pain + weight loss + fatigue + extra-intestinal (uveitis, arthritis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, primary sclerosing cholangitis).
Complications: strictures, fistulas (perianal, enterocutaneous, enterovesical, enteroenteric), abscess, perforation.
Risk factors: smoking (worsens — strong association), family history, NSAID, antibiotic use, urban / hygienic environment.
redFlags: Concomitant abscess — must drain before / alongside immunosuppression.
Colon cancer / dysplasia surveillance (longstanding colonic disease).
Pregnancy + Crohn — biologics continue; flares can complicate.

diagnostics.test: Capsule endoscopy + MR enterography for small-bowel disease.
MRI pelvis for perianal disease (fistula characterisation).
FBC + CRP + albumin + ferritin + vitamin B12 + faecal calprotectin.
Stool studies — C. difficile + culture + ova / parasites + viral.
Hepatitis B + C + HIV + TB (interferon-gamma release assay + CXR) before biologic.

management.detail: Gastroenterologist + IBD nurse + dietitian + stoma nurse + colorectal surgeon + psychologist. Treat to deep remission (clinical + biochemical + endoscopic + radiological).
Single most modifiable factor; smoking doubles relapse + surgery rates.

management.step: Induction — biologics increasingly first-line for moderate-severe
management.detail: Anti-TNF (infliximab 5 mg/kg IV at 0/2/6 weeks then every 8 weeks; adalimumab 160 mg → 80 mg → 40 mg SC every 2 weeks) — first-line. Combination with thiopurine (azathioprine 2 mg/kg) improves outcomes for infliximab. Ustekinumab (IL-12/23) 6 mg/kg IV then 90 mg SC every 8 weeks. Vedolizumab (anti-α4β7 integrin) 300 mg IV at 0/2/6 then every 8 weeks. Risankizumab (anti-IL-23) emerging. Upadacitinib (JAK inhibitor) oral approved for moderate-severe.

Budesonide CIR 9 mg/day for ileal / right-colonic (less systemic effect). Prednisolone 30–40 mg/day for severe / extensive — taper over 8 weeks; combine with steroid-sparing immunomodulator. NEVER long-term.

Same biologic as induction; therapeutic drug monitoring (trough levels + anti-drug antibodies). Tighten / switch if loss of response. Target deep remission (mucosal healing) — improves long-term outcomes (CALM trial).

Resect localised ileocolonic disease — increasingly considered earlier as alternative to long-term medication (LIR!C trial). Drain abscess BEFORE immunosuppression. Stricture: balloon dilation OR resection. Fistula: combined surgical + biologic management. Stoma when needed.

Active disease worse than medication for mother + baby. Continue anti-TNF / vedolizumab / ustekinumab throughout pregnancy (FDA pregnancy registry data reassuring). Stop methotrexate 3 months pre-conception. Aim conception when in remission.

Vitamin / iron / B12 repletion as needed. Exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) in paediatric — first-line induction (no steroid). Calcium + vitamin D + DEXA. Live vaccines BEFORE biologic; killed vaccines safe on biologic.
Colonoscopy 8 years after colonic disease onset, then every 1–3 years per risk. Skin cancer surveillance on thiopurine + anti-TNF.

references.label: ECCO Guidelines on Crohn Disease (2024 update); AGA Clinical Practice Guidelines

title: Treatment-resistant depression — augmentation, ECT, novel therapies
presentation: Major depressive disorder unresponsive to ≥ 2 adequate antidepressant trials of adequate dose + duration (4–8 weeks each).
30% of MDD becomes treatment-resistant.
Often co-occurring: severe anxiety, suicidal ideation, chronic pain, substance use, personality issues, medical comorbidity (hypothyroidism, vitamin deficiency, sleep apnoea, anaemia).
Functional impairment: work, relationships, self-care; suicide risk persistently elevated.
redFlags: Active suicidal ideation with plan or intent — urgent psychiatric assessment + admission consideration.
Severe psychomotor retardation / catatonia / refusal to eat — urgent treatment (ECT).
Pregnancy + severe depression — risk-benefit; some antidepressants safe; ECT safe.
Bipolar depression masquerading as MDD — antidepressant monotherapy can precipitate mania.

diagnostics.test: Confirm diagnosis + treatment history (adequacy of trials).
Exclude bipolar (MDQ + family history + episodic mood elevation history).
diagnostics.rationale: Bipolar depression has different optimal treatment.

diagnostics.test: Exclude organic + iatrogenic contributors: TSH, B12, folate, vitamin D, FBC, U&E, glucose, sleep study, medication review.
PHQ-9 + suicide risk assessment at every visit.
Cognitive testing (Trail Making, Stroop) if cognitive symptoms.

management.detail: Ensure adequate dose × adequate duration (4–8 weeks at maximum tolerated). Check adherence + pharmacogenomics (CYP2D6 / CYP2C19) if available. Address common co-morbidities (sleep, alcohol, substances, hypothyroidism).
SSRI → SNRI (venlafaxine, duloxetine); OR mirtazapine (helpful for insomnia, low appetite); OR vortioxetine; OR bupropion (low energy / weight gain). Cross-taper to avoid discontinuation.

Lithium (target 0.4–0.8 mmol/L) — most evidence. Atypical antipsychotic (aripiprazole 2–10 mg, quetiapine XR 150–300 mg, olanzapine 2.5–10 mg). Liothyronine T3 25 microgram (well-evidenced). Combination antidepressants (SSRI + bupropion; SSRI + mirtazapine 'California rocket fuel').
Spravato 56–84 mg intranasal twice weekly × 4 weeks then weekly then every 2 weeks. Specialist clinic with monitoring (2 h post-dose for dissociation + BP). REMS programme.
0.5 mg/kg IV over 40 min × multiple sessions. Specialist centre. Rapid effect within hours; benefit duration variable.

Gold standard for severe TRD especially with psychotic features, catatonia, severe suicidality, refusing food + fluid. Bilateral or right unilateral; 6–12 sessions. Side effects: cognitive (usually transient retrograde amnesia). Maintenance ECT for relapsing severe.
Non-invasive; daily × 4–6 weeks; specialist centre. Lower response rate than ECT but better tolerated. Newer: Stanford accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (SAINT).
Surgical implantation for very chronic / treatment-refractory cases.

CBT, behavioural activation, interpersonal therapy, mindfulness-based cognitive therapy. Exercise (moderate-intensity, 150 min/week). Sleep hygiene + circadian rhythm. Social support. Light therapy for seasonal pattern.
Psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (FDA breakthrough designation; specialist trials). MDMA-assisted (PTSD primarily). Stay alert to evolving evidence.
Continue effective treatment 2+ years after response in TRD. Wellness recovery action plan. Family + peer support. Address chronic pain + substance use + sleep + occupational issues.

references.label: NICE NG222 Depression in adults; CANMAT TRD; STAR*D trial
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Adult ADHD — diagnosis + comprehensive management
presentation: DSM-5 criteria: ≥ 5 inattention OR hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms (out of 9 each), present in 2+ settings for ≥ 6 months, with functional impairment, onset of some symptoms before age 12 (relaxed in DSM-5).
Inattention: difficulty sustaining attention, organisation problems, easily distracted, forgetfulness, time-management problems.
Hyperactivity-impulsivity: restlessness, talking excessively, blurting out, difficulty waiting turn (less overt motor restlessness than in children).
Comorbid: anxiety (50%), depression (45%), substance use (40%), learning disability, sleep disorders (delayed sleep phase), eating disorders, autism spectrum disorder.
redFlags: Severe suicidality — particularly with comorbid depression.
Substance use disorder — preferred non-stimulant treatment.
Bipolar disorder — stimulant can worsen; stabilise mood first.
Cardiovascular history / structural heart disease — pre-treatment ECG + risk-benefit for stimulants.
Diversion / misuse concerns — long-acting + non-stimulant preferred.
Pregnancy + ADHD — stimulant safety data limited; non-pharmacological emphasis.

diagnostics.test: Comprehensive clinical interview by trained specialist (DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria).
Validated screening: ASRS (Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale), DIVA-5.
Differential / comorbidity screening: mood / anxiety questionnaires, substance use, autism spectrum.
Cognitive testing if learning disability suspected.
Baseline before stimulant: BP, pulse, weight, ECG (per local protocol — usually if cardiac risk).

management.detail: Patient + family education; organisational + time-management skills; environmental modifications (timers, calendars, white-noise headphones, designated workspace); coaching.

Methylphenidate (immediate-release start 5–10 mg BD-TDS titrate to 60 mg/day; long-acting OROS-methylphenidate 18–72 mg AM; lisdexamfetamine 30–70 mg AM; mixed amphetamine salts). Titrate to symptom control with minimal side effects. Monitor BP, pulse, weight, sleep, appetite, mood.

Atomoxetine 40–100 mg/day (target ~1.2 mg/kg) — selective NRI; takes 4–6 weeks for effect. Guanfacine ER 1–7 mg/day OR clonidine ER — alpha-2 agonist. Bupropion 150–300 mg/day (off-label). Preferred for substance-use disorder, tics, anxiety, cardiac risk.
Specialised adult-ADHD CBT (e.g. Safren protocol) — improves outcomes when combined with medication. ADHD coaching for organisation + time management.

Anxiety / depression first if severe (treat to remission then start ADHD medication). Substance use — stabilise + monitor; prefer long-acting / non-stimulant. Mood stabiliser for bipolar before stimulant.
Sleep hygiene + circadian-shifting strategies (often delayed sleep phase + cognitive function impact). Regular aerobic exercise (consistent evidence). Mediterranean / omega-3-rich diet. Mindfulness.
Disability-rights protections in many jurisdictions. Reasonable adjustments (flexible hours, quiet workspace, extended deadlines, recorded meetings). University: extended exam time, tutoring.
Annual review minimum. Adjust dose with life changes (school, work, relationships). Counsel re: misuse + diversion. ADHD persists in 70% to adulthood; identify + support comorbidities.

references.label: NICE NG87 ADHD; APA Diagnostic Criteria DSM-5; European Consensus on Adult ADHD
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) — evidence-based treatment
presentation: Exposure to actual / threatened death, serious injury, sexual violence — directly experienced, witnessed, learned about close family / friend, repeated occupational exposure (first responders, military).

Four symptom clusters (DSM-5): intrusion (flashbacks, nightmares, distressing memories); avoidance of trauma reminders; negative cognitions / mood (numbing, detachment, blame, anhedonia); arousal / reactivity (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, irritability, sleep disturbance, concentration).
Persistent > 1 month with significant distress / impairment.
Complex PTSD (ICD-11): additional features — affective dysregulation, negative self-concept, interpersonal difficulties — often from prolonged / interpersonal trauma.
redFlags: Pregnancy + PTSD — flashback during delivery; trauma-focused care.
Suspected dissociative identity disorder (severe / very early-trauma).

diagnostics.test: Clinical interview based on DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria.
Suicide risk + substance use + depression + anxiety screen.
Physical examination — chronic pain, sleep disorders, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular.
Differential: acute stress disorder (< 1 month), adjustment disorder, depression, borderline PD, dissociative disorders.

management.detail: Trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT) — including prolonged exposure therapy + cognitive processing therapy. Eye movement desensitisation + reprocessing (EMDR) — non-inferior to TF-CBT; useful for those who cannot tolerate prolonged exposure. 8–16 sessions over 3–4 months.

SSRI (sertraline, paroxetine FDA-approved for PTSD) OR SNRI (venlafaxine) — first-line. Titrate to maximum tolerated × 12 weeks. Continue ≥ 12 months in responders. Prazosin 2–15 mg nocte for nightmares + sleep disturbance (specialist evidence).
Worsen PTSD outcomes; impair fear extinction learning; high addiction risk in PTSD population. Reserve for very short-term acute crisis only.

management.step: Adjunctive antipsychotic for psychotic features / severe paranoia
management.detail: Quetiapine 25–200 mg / olanzapine 5–10 mg — selected refractory cases; off-label.
Sleep disturbance + nightmares often persistent. Sleep hygiene + prazosin (for nightmares) + image rehearsal therapy (IRT). Treat comorbid depression / anxiety / substance use IN PARALLEL.

Phase 1: stabilisation + safety + skills. Phase 2: trauma processing. Phase 3: integration + reconnection. Often longer + more relational + skills-focused than standard TF-CBT (e.g. STAIR, ISTSS treatment guidelines).
MDMA-assisted psychotherapy showed strong phase-3 evidence; FDA approval anticipated (currently under review). Psilocybin in trials. Specialist centres only.
Veterans + first-responder peer-support programmes. Family education + couples therapy. Trauma-informed care across all healthcare interactions.
Integrated treatment — concurrent psychotherapy + medication for both. Avoid sequential treatment (often poor outcomes); SSRI + naltrexone OR concurrent therapy programmes.
If no response — switch SSRI / try different therapy modality / refer specialist trauma centre. Consider ECT / TMS for severe + treatment-resistant (limited evidence in PTSD).

references.label: ISTSS Treatment Guidelines for PTSD (2018); NICE NG116 PTSD; VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for PTSD (2023)
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Menopause — hormone therapy decision pathway
presentation: Vasomotor symptoms (hot flushes, night sweats) — peak in first 3 years post-final menstrual period; ~25% persist > 10 years.
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency / recurrent UTI).
Mood + cognition: depression, anxiety, brain fog.
Sleep disturbance.
Long-term: bone loss (osteoporosis), cardiovascular risk increase.
Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI): menopause before age 40 — needs HRT until natural menopause age.
redFlags: Postmenopausal bleeding — exclude endometrial cancer (TVUS endometrial thickness > 4 mm → biopsy).
Suspected hormone-sensitive malignancy (breast, endometrial) — HRT contraindicated.
VTE history / thrombophilia — oral HRT contraindicated; transdermal acceptable.
Severe liver disease, active migraine with aura, uncontrolled hypertension.
Pregnancy still possible during perimenopause — contraception until 1 year amenorrhoea (or 2 if < 50).

diagnostics.test: Clinical diagnosis — VMS + amenorrhoea > 12 months in age-appropriate woman.
Premature ovarian insufficiency: FSH > 25 IU/L × 2 occasions 4 weeks apart, age < 40.
Baseline + ongoing: BP, BMI, lipids, glucose, mammography (per programme), cervical screen (per programme).
DEXA bone density (POI, fracture history, risk factors).

management.detail: Most healthy women < 60 / within 10 years of menopause: HRT benefits outweigh risks for moderate-severe VMS. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration consistent with goals (but no arbitrary stop date — review annually).

Combined HRT (oestrogen + progestogen) for women with uterus to protect endometrium. Oestrogen-only for hysterectomised women. Routes: oral (cheaper, easier), transdermal patch / gel (preferred for VTE risk, hypertension, migraine, hepatic). Micronised progesterone (Utrogestan) — preferred progestogen (cancer-neutral; sleep + mood benefits).

Vaginal oestrogen (cream / tablet / ring) — minimal systemic absorption; safe in most cancer survivors after specialist discussion. Non-hormonal lubricant + moisturiser. Pelvic floor exercises. Ospemifene oral SERM alternative.

SSRI / SNRI (paroxetine 10 mg, venlafaxine 37.5–75 mg, escitalopram 10 mg) — modest effect. Gabapentin 300–900 mg/day. Clonidine 100 microgram BD. NK3 receptor antagonist (fezolinetant 45 mg) — newer non-hormonal targeted therapy.
HRT + calcium 1000 mg + vitamin D 800 IU + weight-bearing exercise; bisphosphonate / denosumab / parathyroid hormone analogue if osteoporosis confirmed. POI patients especially benefit.
HRT until expected age of natural menopause (~51) at minimum — even if asymptomatic — to protect bones + cardiovascular + brain. Higher doses than late-menopause may be needed.

Breast cancer: small increase with combined HRT after ~5 years (1 extra per 1000 women-years on combined; smaller risk with micronised progesterone). VTE: oral HRT 2× background; transdermal no increase. CHD: small increase if HRT started > 10 years post-menopause; cardio-neutral or protective if started < 60. Stroke: small increase with oral, less transdermal.
Review benefits vs risks annually; lowest effective dose; consider step-down + non-HRT alternatives over time.
Refer for: POI, complex risk-benefit, persistent symptoms despite first-line HRT, cancer-survivor HRT, gender-affirming hormone management overlap.

references.label: NICE NG23 Menopause; BMS Recommendations; IMS Position Statements
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Severe atopic dermatitis — systemic + biologic pathway
presentation: Chronic itchy inflammatory skin disease; flexural pattern (cubital + popliteal) in adults; face / extensor in infants.
Severe: extensive BSA involvement, sleep disturbance, frequent infection, severe pruritus, failure to thrive (paediatric), depression / anxiety, impaired quality of life.
Comorbid atopy: asthma, allergic rhinitis, food allergy (especially infants).
Risk: filaggrin mutations, family history, environmental (climate, allergens, infection).
redFlags: Eczema herpeticum (widespread vesicles + fever + lymphadenopathy) — IV aciclovir emergency.
Secondary bacterial / viral infection (S. aureus most common).
Suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides) — atypical / adult-onset severe / treatment-resistant.
Severe paediatric — growth failure, school absence, family burden.
Suicidal ideation from chronic itch + sleep deprivation.

diagnostics.test: Clinical (Hanifin-Rajka or UK Working Party criteria).
EASI (Eczema Area + Severity Index) or POEM (Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure) — severity scoring.
Total + specific IgE if comorbid allergy / atopic march concerns.

diagnostics.rationale: Exclude differential (mycosis fungoides, contact dermatitis, psoriasis).

management.detail: Liberal emollient 2–4 times daily (250–500 g/week adult); cool-tepid baths with bath emollient; soap-free wash. Avoid triggers (irritants, allergens, heat, sweat, stress). Education + self-management.

Topical corticosteroid (mild — moderate — potent — very potent) tiered to severity + site; ≤ 2 weeks then taper. Topical calcineurin inhibitor (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) for face / flexures / chronic. Crisaborole. Wet wrap therapy for severe.
Narrowband UVB 3 times/week × 8–12 weeks — moderate-severe disease unresponsive to topical. Combination with TCS / TCI.

Ciclosporin 3–5 mg/kg/day (short-term — 1 year max — renal toxicity). Methotrexate 7.5–25 mg/week. Mycophenolate 1–3 g/day. Azathioprine 1–3 mg/kg/day (TPMT testing). All require monitoring; for severe + cannot use biologic / JAK.

management.step: Biologics — paradigm shift in severe AD
management.detail: Dupilumab (IL-4Rα) 600 mg SC then 300 mg every 2 weeks — first-line biologic; effective + safe (conjunctivitis common side effect). Tralokinumab (IL-13) 300 mg every 2 weeks. Lebrikizumab approved. Specialist initiation.

Upadacitinib 15–30 mg daily; abrocitinib 100–200 mg daily; baricitinib 2–4 mg daily — for severe AD. RAPID onset (days). Specialist initiation + monitoring (FBC, lipids, infection screen, malignancy risk). Boxed warnings re: VTE + cardiac (extrapolated from RA data).

S. aureus colonisation common: dilute bleach baths (1/4 cup per full bath) + nasal mupirocin if recurrent; topical / oral antibiotic for clinical infection. Eczema herpeticum: IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 h × 7–14 days.
Screen depression + anxiety + sleep impact. Refer paediatric psychology + family support for childhood AD. Eczema-specific patient education programmes.
Food allergy testing if specific reaction or severe paediatric. Aeroallergen avoidance if confirmed sensitivity. Hyposensitisation in selected dust-mite-sensitive.
Atopic march surveillance (asthma, allergic rhinitis). Childhood — adolescent — adult care continuity. Family education + adherence support.

references.label: NICE QS44 Atopic eczema in children; EuroGuiDerm Guideline on AD (2023); ATS Skin position paper on biologics
Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (5th ed, 2022), Ministry of Health

title: Acromegaly — diagnosis + treatment
presentation: Adults: insidious onset of soft-tissue overgrowth — enlarged hands, feet, jaw (prognathism), tongue (macroglossia), nose, lips, supraorbital ridges; spacing of teeth; dental malocclusion; increased shoe / glove / ring size.
Headache, visual field defects (bitemporal hemianopia from optic chiasm compression), galactorrhoea (prolactin co-secretion).
Complications: hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hyperhidrosis, sleep apnoea, cardiomyopathy + arrhythmia, colorectal polyps + cancer, osteoarthropathy, carpal tunnel.
Gigantism in children (before epiphyseal closure): excessive linear growth.
Cause: pituitary GH-secreting adenoma (95%) — usually macroadenoma at diagnosis due to delayed recognition.
redFlags: Visual deterioration — chiasmal compression; urgent neurosurgical review.

diagnostics.test: Oral glucose tolerance test with GH measurement at baseline + 30/60/90/120 min (failure of GH suppression < 0.4 microgram/L confirms acromegaly).
Full anterior pituitary hormone panel (PRL, TSH + freeT4, LH + FSH + testosterone / oestradiol, ACTH + cortisol).
ECG + echo + sleep study + colonoscopy + HbA1c + lipids + BP.
Genetic testing if young / family history (MEN1, AIP, FIPA).

management.detail: Endocrinologist + neurosurgeon + radiation oncologist + ophthalmologist + cardiologist.
Microsurgery via experienced pituitary neurosurgeon. Cure rate 60–90% for microadenomas, 30–50% for macroadenomas. Pre-operative somatostatin analogue may improve outcomes.

management.step: Medical therapy — when surgery insufficient / contraindicated / pre-op
management.detail: Somatostatin receptor ligand (octreotide LAR, lanreotide autogel) IM monthly — first-line medical. Pasireotide LAR (second-generation; better efficacy but hyperglycaemia). GH receptor antagonist (pegvisomant) daily SC — blocks GH peripheral action; titrate to IGF-1. Dopamine agonist (cabergoline) — modest benefit, useful for mild / mixed GH+PRL tumours.
Stereotactic radiosurgery (Gamma knife) for residual tumour after surgery; takes years for full effect. High rate of hypopituitarism over time.
Hydrocortisone / thyroxine / testosterone / oestrogen / growth hormone (selectively) per identified deficiencies.

BP control + diabetes management + sleep apnoea CPAP + cardiomyopathy management (often reverses with biochemical control). Colonoscopy at diagnosis + every 5 years (longer in well-controlled). Joint care (NSAID / physiotherapy / joint replacement).

Biochemical: random GH < 1 microgram/L; OGTT-suppressed GH < 0.4; age-normalised IGF-1. Clinical: symptom improvement + cardiovascular + metabolic + colonic complications addressed. Mortality returns to background when controlled.
Annual IGF-1 + symptom review + pituitary MRI (initially) + complications surveillance + colonoscopy.
Often improves during pregnancy; stop somatostatin analogues + pegvisomant during pregnancy if possible; monitor IGF-1 every trimester; specialist multidisciplinary care.

references.label: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline on Acromegaly (2014 update); Pituitary Society International Acromegaly Consensus

title: Graves disease — hyperthyroidism management
presentation: Autoimmune disease (TSH receptor stimulating antibodies — TRAb) causing diffuse goitre + hyperthyroidism.

Hyperthyroidism: weight loss + heat intolerance + sweating + tachycardia + tremor + irritability + insomnia + bowel frequency + menstrual changes + proximal myopathy + osteoporosis + atrial fibrillation.

Specific to Graves: diffuse symmetrical goitre + thyroid bruit; Graves ophthalmopathy (proptosis + diplopia + chemosis + optic neuropathy) — 25–50%; pretibial myxoedema (rare); thyroid acropachy (rare).
Female > male 5–10:1; peak 30–50 years.
redFlags: Severe ophthalmopathy with optic neuropathy / corneal exposure — vision-threatening.
Severe cardiac complications (AF, heart failure, thromboembolism).
Severe agranulocytosis on antithyroid drug (rare; sore throat / fever).
Pregnancy — risk of fetal hyper / hypothyroidism; specialist care.

diagnostics.rationale: Confirm Graves (vs toxic nodular or thyroiditis).

diagnostics.test: Thyroid USS (diffuse hypervascular goitre — Graves pattern).
Thyroid uptake scan (Tc-99m) — if needed; diffuse uptake in Graves; reduced in thyroiditis.
ECG, BMD if osteoporotic risk, mental-health screen.

management.detail: Propranolol 40 mg TDS-QDS OR atenolol 25–100 mg daily — controls tachycardia, tremor, anxiety. Continue until euthyroid.

Carbimazole 20–40 mg/day (or methimazole) — preferred outside USA. Propylthiouracil 200–400 mg/day TDS — preferred in 1st trimester pregnancy + thyroid storm. Continue 12–18 months; remission rate ~50% post-cessation; lower with goitre + persistently positive TRAb. Titrate dose with thyroid function tests every 4–6 weeks.
Counsel patient: ANY sore throat / fever — STOP drug + urgent FBC. Frequency ~0.3% — usually first 90 days.

I-131 oral — definitive ablation of thyroid; hypothyroidism in 80% within 1 year (then lifelong levothyroxine). Useful for: recurrent Graves after thionamide, large goitre, contraindication to surgery. AVOID during pregnancy + breastfeeding + within 6 months of conception. AVOID with severe ophthalmopathy (may worsen — pre-treat with steroid).

Indications: large goitre, suspicious nodule, refusal of RAI, severe ophthalmopathy, planning pregnancy soon, very high TRAb. Specialist endocrine surgeon. Post-op lifelong levothyroxine ± calcium / vitamin D (parathyroid risk).

Smoking cessation (single most important — smoking worsens). Lubricant eye drops; head elevation; sunglasses. Selenium 100 microgram BD × 6 months for mild active disease. Moderate-severe active: IV methylprednisolone 4.5–7.5 g over 12 weeks. Severe / vision-threatening: combine with teprotumumab (anti-IGF-1R) — proptosis-reducing; or orbital decompression surgery; rituximab as alternative.

PTU in 1st trimester (lower teratogenicity); switch to carbimazole in 2nd-3rd; lowest dose to maintain free T4 upper-normal range. Block-replace REGIMEN avoided (transplacental hypothyroidism). Specialist obstetric + endocrine care. Newborn — risk of TRAb transmission → fetal/neonatal Graves.
Annual TSH after stable euthyroid; remission monitoring 1 year after stopping ATD then annually. RAI / surgery: lifelong levothyroxine. Cardiovascular + bone surveillance long-term.

references.label: ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis + Management of Hyperthyroidism (2016)
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Breast cancer — comprehensive biomarker-guided treatment pathway
presentation: Lump (most common), nipple discharge, skin / nipple changes, axillary lymphadenopathy, metastatic (bone pain, breathlessness, hepatomegaly, neurology, pleural effusion).
Screen-detected (mammography programme).
Subtypes by biomarker: ER+ / PR+ / HER2- (luminal A — best prognosis); ER+ / HER2+ (luminal B); HER2-amplified; triple-negative (no targets — chemotherapy mainstay).
Male breast cancer (1%) — usually ER+; treated similarly.
Inflammatory breast cancer — erythema + peau d'orange + rapid course; T4d.
redFlags: Inflammatory or locally advanced (T3-4) at presentation — urgent multidisciplinary.
Metastatic at presentation (cord compression, brain mets, leptomeningeal, hepatic failure).
Pregnancy + breast cancer — preserve pregnancy where possible; modify chemotherapy choice.
Hereditary suspicion (BRCA / PALB2 / TP53) — young / triple-negative / family history.

diagnostics.test: Triple assessment: clinical + imaging (mammography + USS / MRI) + core biopsy.
Histology + biomarkers: ER, PR, HER2 (IHC + FISH for equivocal), Ki67, grade.
BRCA1/2 + PALB2 + TP53 + multi-gene panel for hereditary suspicion.
Staging: CT chest/abdomen, bone scan, MRI brain if neuro symptoms; PET-CT for selected.
Oncotype DX / MammaPrint / Endopredict for ER+ / HER2- node-negative early (chemotherapy decision aid).

management.step: Multidisciplinary tumour board for ALL cases
management.detail: Breast surgeon + oncologist + radiation oncologist + radiologist + pathologist + specialist nurse + plastic surgery + genetic counsellor.

Breast-conserving surgery + radiotherapy (equivalent survival to mastectomy for selected; better cosmesis). Mastectomy for: large tumour, multifocal, BRCA, patient choice, prior radiation. Axillary sentinel node biopsy ± ALND. Adjuvant therapy: chemotherapy + endocrine + targeted per subtype.

management.step: Neoadjuvant therapy — for downstaging + triple-negative / HER2+ / large ER+
management.detail: Triple-negative: anthracycline-taxane + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-522). HER2+: trastuzumab + pertuzumab + chemotherapy (TCHP). ER+: usually adjuvant (some neoadjuvant endocrine for elderly / locally advanced). Path complete response (pCR) is positive prognostic.

Pre-menopausal: tamoxifen 20 mg/day × 5–10 years (longer for higher-risk). Add ovarian function suppression (LHRH agonist or oophorectomy) for higher-risk young pre-menopausal (SOFT / TEXT). Post-menopausal: aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole / letrozole / exemestane) × 5 years; consider extended adjuvant. Switch protocols common (tamoxifen first then AI).
Abemaciclib × 2 years (monarchE) for high-risk early ER+/HER2- (4+ nodes, or 1–3 nodes with grade 3 / size ≥ 5 cm / Ki67 ≥ 20). Ribociclib also approved (NATALEE).
Trastuzumab × 1 year + chemotherapy. T-DM1 (Kadcyla) if residual disease post-neoadjuvant TCHP (KATHERINE). Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu) for metastatic / refractory.
Chemotherapy backbone (anthracycline + taxane); pembrolizumab × 1 year if neoadjuvant-given (KEYNOTE-522). Olaparib × 1 year for BRCA-mutated post-adjuvant (OlympiA).

ER+: endocrine + CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib / ribociclib / abemaciclib) first-line; PI3K inhibitor (alpelisib) for PIK3CA mutation; capivasertib for AKT-PI3K-PTEN-mutated. HER2+: trastuzumab + pertuzumab + taxane → T-DM1 → T-DXd → tucatinib + capecitabine + trastuzumab. Triple-negative: chemotherapy + pembrolizumab (PD-L1+) → sacituzumab govitecan (ASCENT) → talazoparib / olaparib (BRCA-mutant) → trastuzumab deruxtecan (HER2-low). Survival extending year-on-year with novel agents.

Bone-modifying agents (zoledronate or denosumab) for bone metastases. Radiotherapy for symptomatic bone, brain, spinal cord. Lymphoedema management. Menopausal symptom management. Fertility preservation pre-chemotherapy. Specialist palliative care + survivorship clinic.

Test for BRCA1/2 + PALB2 + multi-gene if criteria. Risk-reducing surgery for mutation carriers (mastectomy + salpingo-oophorectomy). Family screening; long-term cardiac + bone + cognitive monitoring; second-cancer surveillance.

references.label: ESMO + NCCN Breast Cancer Guidelines; St Gallen Consensus; multiple trial-defining regimens
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Multiple myeloma — diagnosis + treatment pathway
presentation: Clonal plasma-cell malignancy: CRAB criteria (hyperCalcaemia, Renal impairment, Anaemia, Bone lytic lesions).
Symptoms: bone pain (often back, ribs, long bones; pathological fracture), anaemia, infection (humoral immunosuppression), AKI, hyperviscosity, weight loss, fatigue.
Spectrum: MGUS → smouldering myeloma → symptomatic MM. SLiM-CRAB criteria (2014) lowered diagnostic threshold (BM clonal plasma cells ≥ 60%, FLC ratio ≥ 100, MRI > 1 focal lesion).
Subgroups: high-risk cytogenetics t(4;14), t(14;16), del(17p), gain(1q), TP53 mutations.
redFlags: Spinal cord compression — urgent MRI + radiotherapy.
AKI from cast nephropathy — preserve renal function with rapid disease reduction.
Plasma cell leukaemia (> 20% peripheral plasma cells or absolute > 2 × 10⁹/L) — aggressive.
Hyperviscosity syndrome (IgM MM variant) — emergency plasmapheresis.

diagnostics.test: Serum + urine immunofixation + serum free light chains (kappa : lambda ratio).
Bone marrow aspirate + trephine + FISH cytogenetics (for high-risk markers).
Whole-body low-dose CT / WB-MRI / PET-CT (preferred over skeletal survey).
FBC, U&E, calcium, LDH, beta-2-microglobulin, albumin (R-ISS staging).
Cardiac assessment + echo + NT-proBNP (cardiac amyloid screen).

management.step: Multidisciplinary haematology + clinical trial enrolment encouraged
management.detail: Specialist myeloma centre; clinical trials accelerate access to novel therapy.
Daratumumab + bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (Dara-VRd; 4 cycles) — current standard (PERSEUS / GRIFFIN). Other options: Dara-VTd, VRd (no transplant-modifying anti-CD38).
Melphalan 200 mg/m² conditioning + autologous SCT. Consolidation + maintenance daratumumab + lenalidomide. Significant survival benefit in eligible patients.

Daratumumab + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (Dara-Rd; MAIA) — first-line in transplant-ineligible. Daratumumab + bortezomib + melphalan + prednisolone (Dara-VMP) for fit elderly. Continue until progression.
Lenalidomide 10–15 mg daily until progression — standard after ASCT. Add daratumumab in high-risk + relapsed.

Sequential novel agents in proteasome / immunomodulatory / anti-CD38 / antibody-drug conjugates / BCMA-targeted. Lines of therapy: anti-CD38 + IMiD + PI combinations; carfilzomib; pomalidomide; elotuzumab; ixazomib oral. BCMA-targeted: belantamab mafodotin (ADC); teclistamab / talquetamab (bispecific T-cell engagers); idecabtagene vicleucel + ciltacabtagene autoleucel (CAR-T) for triple-class refractory. Allogeneic SCT in young / refractory.

Bone-modifying agent (zoledronate or denosumab) monthly initially; AVOID in severe renal failure (denosumab acceptable). Calcium + vitamin D. Radiotherapy for symptomatic / spinal cord compression / pathological fracture. Vertebroplasty / kyphoplasty for vertebral compression. Erythropoietin for symptomatic anaemia. Aciclovir prophylaxis (zoster). Anti-thrombotic prophylaxis (aspirin or LMWH per VTE risk). IVIG for recurrent infection. PJP + antifungal prophylaxis during chemotherapy. Vaccinations.
Aggressive hydration. Rapid disease control (bortezomib-based). Plasma exchange for severe cast nephropathy (controversial — selected centres). Avoid nephrotoxins.
MRD (minimal residual disease) monitoring increasingly used. Second cancers (lenalidomide + alkylating). Cardiovascular events. Bone health surveillance. Continue maintenance until progression.

references.label: IMWG criteria + guidelines; ESMO + NCCN Multiple Myeloma; PERSEUS + MAIA + GRIFFIN trials
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health

title: Kidney transplant — peri-operative + immunosuppression + long-term care
presentation: Patient with end-stage renal disease pre-/post-transplantation.
Pre-transplant: dialysis or pre-emptive; complete workup; living-donor or deceased-donor.
Post-transplant: acute (first year — rejection, infection, surgical complications); chronic (years — graft dysfunction, infection, malignancy, cardiovascular, metabolic).
Common immunosuppression: induction (basiliximab or anti-thymocyte globulin) + maintenance (calcineurin inhibitor + antimetabolite + steroid).
redFlags: Acute rejection: rapid creatinine rise; needs biopsy + treatment.
Severe infection — opportunistic (CMV, BK virus, PJP, fungal, TB, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease).
Cardiovascular event — leading cause of death.
Suspected renal artery / vein thrombosis acute post-op.
Recurrent disease (FSGS, MPGN, lupus nephritis, atypical HUS).

diagnostics.test: Serial creatinine + eGFR + urinalysis (early frequent; later weekly → monthly).
Tacrolimus / ciclosporin trough level + drug interactions.
BK virus PCR + CMV PCR + EBV PCR at intervals.
Allograft biopsy for unexplained renal dysfunction.
Annual cardiovascular review, lipid + glucose + BP + DEXA, skin / cancer surveillance.
Vaccination history + infection screen pre-transplant; family / donor screening.

management.detail: Cardiovascular fitness (CT angiography / cardiac catheter; coronary revascularisation if indicated). Cancer screening (age-appropriate). Infection screen (HBV, HCV, HIV, CMV, EBV, VZV, TB, syphilis, parasites per region). Vaccinations: all routine + influenza + pneumococcal + COVID + zoster + hepatitis B + HPV. Live vaccines must be given pre-transplant. Donor matching: ABO + HLA + crossmatch + DSA screening.
Heterotopic placement in iliac fossa. Reperfusion injury management. Vascular + ureteric complication surveillance. Early ambulation. DVT prophylaxis.
Basiliximab (IL-2 receptor) for low-risk; anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) for high-risk (HLA-mismatched, sensitised, repeat transplant, paediatric).

Calcineurin inhibitor (tacrolimus preferred over ciclosporin; trough 5–8 ng/mL after first year) + antimetabolite (mycophenolate mofetil 1 g BD or mycophenolic acid) + corticosteroid (prednisolone 5–10 mg/day; some centres minimise / withdraw). Sirolimus / everolimus (mTOR inhibitors) as steroid-sparing or for malignancy.
High-dose IV methylprednisolone 500 mg–1 g × 3 days. Anti-thymocyte globulin for steroid-resistant. Optimise maintenance regimen.
Plasma exchange + IVIG + rituximab + bortezomib (refractory). Increasingly recognised; specialist transplant unit.
