Co-trimoxazole for PJP × 6–12 months. CMV: ganciclovir / valganciclovir prophylaxis for donor +/recipient – × 6 months. Aciclovir for HSV/VZV. Antifungal selectively. Nystatin for oral candidiasis. Vaccine review.
Reduce immunosuppression on BK viraemia > 10⁴ copies/mL; convert tacrolimus to ciclosporin; IVIG or leflunomide for established nephropathy.
BP target < 130/80; statin (atorvastatin / pravastatin — interact with calcineurin inhibitor); ACE inhibitor / ARB; tight glycaemic control; weight + lifestyle.

Skin: annual dermatology + sun protection (very high SCC + BCC risk on immunosuppression). Cervical + breast + colorectal screening per general population. PTLD surveillance (EBV PCR; biopsy if suspicious).

Wait ≥ 1 year stable graft function. Convert mycophenolate to azathioprine 6 weeks pre-conception (teratogenic). Continue tacrolimus + steroid. Joint nephrology + obstetric care. Aspirin from 12 weeks (pre-eclampsia).

references.label: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Care of Kidney Transplant Recipient; UK Renal Association

title: Rheumatoid arthritis — early treat-to-target + biologic / targeted synthetic
presentation: Symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis — small joints of hands + feet predominantly; morning stiffness > 30 min; fatigue.

Extra-articular: rheumatoid nodules, sicca, pulmonary (ILD, pleural effusion), cardiovascular (accelerated atherosclerosis), Felty syndrome, vasculitis, scleritis, anaemia of chronic disease, lymphoma risk.
Lab: positive RF + anti-CCP (high specificity), raised CRP / ESR.
Imaging: erosions + joint space narrowing + bony oedema on MRI / USS (sub-clinical inflammation).
redFlags: Septic arthritis differential — sudden severe monoarticular swelling + fever — aspirate.
Felty syndrome (RA + splenomegaly + neutropenia) — infection risk.
Atlanto-axial instability — cervical instability + neuro symptoms.
Suspected lymphoma (DLBCL more common in RA).

diagnostics.test: USS / MRI hands + feet for early disease + subclinical synovitis.
FBC, U&E, LFT, hepatitis B + C, TB (IGRA + CXR), pregnancy test, varicella status — pre-biologic.
Pulmonary function tests + HRCT if respiratory symptoms.

management.detail: EULAR / ACR: early DMARD (within 3 months of symptom onset); target remission or low disease activity (DAS28 / CDAI); escalate if not at target by 3 months; specialist rheumatology team.

10–25 mg/week oral or SC (SC if oral poorly tolerated or BMI > 30). Folic acid 5 mg/week (different day). Reduces inflammation + erosions + extra-articular + cardiovascular. Combine with prednisolone bridge.
If MTX inadequate: add hydroxychloroquine 200–400 mg/day + sulfasalazine 1.5–3 g/day (triple therapy) — non-inferior to anti-TNF for many.

Anti-TNF (etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab, golimumab, certolizumab) — first-line biologic. Rituximab (anti-CD20) for refractory / RF+ / extra-articular. Abatacept (CTLA4-Ig). IL-6 inhibitor (tocilizumab + sarilumab). All require pre-biologic safety screen + ongoing surveillance.

Tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib, filgotinib — oral. ORAL Surveillance + post-marketing have shown increased cardiac + VTE + serious infection events in older RA patients with cardiovascular risk factors — restricted use in patients with these risks; counsel.
Bridging low-dose prednisolone 5–10 mg/day during DMARD titration; intra-articular steroid for joint flare. AVOID long-term high-dose (osteoporosis, cataracts, diabetes, infection).

Physiotherapy + occupational therapy + hand therapy; exercise (essential for joint health + cardiovascular); smoking cessation (smoking worsens + reduces biologic response); orthotics; joint protection.

Cardiovascular risk-modification (statins, BP control — RA accelerates atherosclerosis). Osteoporosis (vitamin D + calcium + bisphosphonate); infection prophylaxis (PCP if high-dose immunosuppression); vaccinations (avoid live during biologic; flu + pneumococcal annual). Cancer surveillance + skin checks.

MTX, leflunomide CONTRAINDICATED — stop ≥ 3 months pre-conception. Sulfasalazine + hydroxychloroquine + azathioprine compatible. Anti-TNF (especially certolizumab — no placental transfer) compatible in pregnancy. Rituximab requires 6-month washout. Most RA improves in pregnancy + flares postpartum — restart effective DMARD postpartum.
Joint replacement for refractory destructive disease (hip, knee, shoulder, ankle). Synovectomy. Tendon repair. Cervical spine surgery for instability.

references.label: EULAR + ACR Treat-to-Target Recommendations; NICE NG100 + TA225 RA biologic + targeted synthetic
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Ankylosing spondylitis / axial spondyloarthritis — treatment pathway
presentation: Chronic inflammatory back pain — insidious onset before age 45; > 3 months duration; morning stiffness > 30 min; improves with activity worsens with rest; alternating buttock pain.
Enthesitis (Achilles, plantar fascia, ribs); dactylitis; peripheral arthritis.
Extra-articular: anterior uveitis (acute unilateral; recurrent), psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease, aortic root involvement, IgA nephropathy.
HLA-B27 positive in 80–90% of AS; family history common.
Progressive spinal fusion → restrictive lung disease + fracture risk.
redFlags: New focal back pain or trauma — increased fracture risk in fused spine (low-energy fracture).
Cauda equina syndrome — rare late complication.
Severe acute anterior uveitis with vision loss.
Aortic regurgitation / heart block on ECG.

diagnostics.test: ASAS classification criteria (back pain ≥ 3 months + age < 45 + sacroiliitis on imaging + ≥ 1 SpA feature OR HLA-B27 + ≥ 2 SpA features).
X-ray sacroiliac joints (Modified New York criteria — radiographic AS).
diagnostics.rationale: Detect structural sacroiliitis (often takes years to develop).

diagnostics.test: MRI sacroiliac joints + spine for inflammatory bone oedema — earlier than X-ray.
CRP + ESR (often raised in active disease).
Pre-biologic: hepatitis B/C + HIV + TB + varicella + vaccine review.
Annual ophthalmology if uveitis history; cardiac assessment for aortitis; PFTs.

management.detail: Daily home exercise + supervised physiotherapy (improves function + reduces stiffness; SPINE trial). Posture training; avoid prolonged static positions; spinal mobility maintenance critical.
Continuous NSAID (e.g. naproxen 500 mg BD, etoricoxib 60–90 mg daily) — evidence for symptom + structural-progression benefit. Caution gastrointestinal + cardiovascular + renal risk.

management.step: Biologic therapy — for axial disease inadequate response to NSAID
management.detail: Anti-TNF first-line (etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab, golimumab, certolizumab) — dramatic symptom + radiographic improvement. IL-17 inhibitor (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) — alternative. Pre-biologic screen mandatory.
Upadacitinib (15 mg daily) and tofacitinib approved for AS; caution VTE + cardiac risk in older patients.
Methotrexate / sulfasalazine for peripheral disease (NOT effective for axial).
Topical steroid + cycloplegic (atropine 1%); urgent ophthalmology. Recurrence common; some biologics (adalimumab) reduce uveitis flares.

Counsel re: fracture risk (low-energy injury can cause spinal fracture in fused spine — neuro-surgical consult + careful imaging — CT or MRI; not just X-ray which may underestimate). Calcium + vitamin D + bisphosphonate if osteoporotic.
Fused cervical spine — difficult intubation; awake fibre-optic; alert anaesthetist.
Disease activity variable in pregnancy. NSAID + biologic management as per general; certolizumab preferred biologic for pregnancy. Postpartum flares common.
Rheumatology + ophthalmology + cardiology + respiratory + physiotherapy + occupational therapy + GP. Lifelong management.

references.label: ASAS-EULAR Recommendations for Management of Axial SpA (2022 update); ACR / SAA Guideline

title: Psoriatic arthritis — treat-to-target with biologics + targeted synthetic
presentation: Inflammatory arthritis in patient with psoriasis (90%; 10% precedes psoriasis); spectrum: oligoarticular asymmetric, polyarticular (RA-like), DIP-predominant, arthritis mutilans, axial / spondylitis-predominant.
Enthesitis + dactylitis ('sausage digit') common.
Nail changes (pitting, onycholysis); psoriasis often nail / scalp / hidden sites.
Often seronegative for RF + anti-CCP; HLA-B27 positive subset (axial-predominant).
Comorbidities: cardiovascular (accelerated), depression, metabolic syndrome, NAFLD, uveitis, IBD.

diagnostics.test: USS / MRI of inflamed joints for sub-clinical synovitis / enthesitis.
RF + anti-CCP usually negative (helps differential from RA).
MRI sacroiliac joints if axial involvement suspected.
Disease activity: DAPSA, PASDAS, PsAID (patient-reported); skin: PASI.

management.detail: Joint clinic for combined skin + joint + comorbidity; ophthalmology / gastroenterology for relevant comorbidity.

management.step: NSAIDs + targeted steroids for mild peripheral
management.detail: Intra-articular steroid injection; oral steroid avoided long-term (rebound psoriasis on withdrawal).
Methotrexate first-line (also treats skin) 15–25 mg/week. Sulfasalazine, leflunomide, ciclosporin alternatives. Not effective for axial / enthesitis-predominant.

management.step: Biologics — for inadequate response to DMARDs OR axial / enthesitis disease
management.detail: Anti-TNF (etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab, golimumab, certolizumab). IL-17 inhibitor (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab — also excellent skin). IL-23 inhibitor (guselkumab, risankizumab — excellent skin + dactylitis + entheses; less effective axial). IL-12/23 (ustekinumab).
Apremilast (PDE-4) oral; modest efficacy but well-tolerated for mild disease. JAK inhibitor (tofacitinib, upadacitinib) for refractory; caution VTE + cardiac in older.
Aim minimal disease activity (MDA); reassess at 3-month intervals; escalate if not achieving.
Cardiovascular risk-modification (statin, BP, lifestyle); depression screen + treatment; weight + metabolic syndrome; smoking cessation; alcohol moderation.
Most controlled with sulfasalazine / certolizumab in pregnancy. Stop methotrexate + JAK 3 months pre-conception. Postpartum flares common — restart biologic.
Patient + family psoriasis education; trigger management (stress, infection, smoking, alcohol); topical skin care; phototherapy adjuncts.

references.label: EULAR + GRAPPA Recommendations for PsA Management (2024 update); CASPAR criteria

title: Cerebral palsy — diagnosis + lifelong multidisciplinary care
presentation: Non-progressive motor disorder caused by lesion to developing brain (in utero / perinatal / early childhood).
Subtypes: spastic (most common: hemiplegia / diplegia / quadriplegia), dyskinetic (athetoid / dystonic), ataxic, mixed.
Severity: GMFCS I (walks without limitation) → V (transported, no head control).

Comorbidities: epilepsy (35%), intellectual disability (50% — variable), feeding / nutrition / GI (dysphagia, GERD), respiratory (aspiration, chronic), orthopaedic (contractures, hip dysplasia, scoliosis), visual / hearing impairment, communication, behaviour, sleep, pain.
Aetiology: prematurity / intraventricular haemorrhage / hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy / antenatal stroke / congenital infection / kernicterus / postnatal head injury / meningitis / metabolic.
redFlags: Progressive neurological signs — suggests alternative diagnosis (metabolic, neurodegenerative).
Hip dislocation / scoliosis progression — orthopaedic referral.
Respiratory failure from chronic aspiration or restrictive lung disease.
Severe pain — under-recognised in non-communicative CP.

diagnostics.test: MRI brain — identifies cause + pattern (PVL, basal ganglia, stroke, malformation).
Genetic + metabolic workup if atypical / progressive / family history.
Annual hip surveillance X-ray (especially GMFCS III–V) + spinal assessment.
EEG if seizures suspected; sleep study if disordered sleep / respiratory concern.

management.detail: Developmental paediatrician + neurologist + physiotherapist + occupational therapist + speech-language pathologist + orthopaedic surgeon + nutrition / dietitian + nurse specialist + social worker + family + community-based services.

Identify early (within 6 months of corrected age if possible) for early intervention. Specific therapies: constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) for unilateral CP; bimanual intensive therapy; goal-directed therapy.

Stretching + orthoses + functional rehabilitation (PT/OT). Oral antispasticity (baclofen, diazepam, tizanidine, dantrolene). Botulinum toxin injection — focal; effective + repeated every 3–6 months. Intrathecal baclofen pump for severe diffuse. Selective dorsal rhizotomy (selected GMFCS II–IV).

Hip surveillance + soft-tissue release / osteotomy for displacement. Single-event multilevel surgery (SEMLS) — combined procedures around age 8–12. Scoliosis surgery for progressive curves. Foot deformities + contractures.
Augmentative + alternative communication (AAC) — picture boards, switches, eye-gaze devices; speech therapy; functional communication training.
PEG feeding for severe dysphagia / aspiration / failure to thrive. Fundoplication for severe GERD. Anti-reflux + prokinetic medications. Monitor + treat constipation.
Standard antiepileptic per seizure type; ketogenic diet for refractory; vagus nerve stimulation.

Assess pain even in non-communicative; treat constipation, GERD, dental, musculoskeletal causes; analgesia (paracetamol, NSAID, gabapentin for neuropathic); botulinum toxin for spasticity-related pain.
Educational support + accommodations; respite care; carer support; financial benefits; community-based therapy; equipment + adaptations; transport.
Structured adolescent — adult transition. Continued multidisciplinary care into adulthood; address employment + relationships + sexuality + housing + ageing.

references.label: AACPDM Care Pathways; SCPE Surveillance of Cerebral Palsy in Europe; NICE NG62 Cerebral palsy
Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (5th ed, 2022), Ministry of Health

title: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) — lifelong multidisciplinary care
presentation: Trisomy 21 — most commonly free trisomy (95%), Robertsonian translocation (4%), mosaicism (1%).
Diagnostic features: facial morphology (epicanthal folds, flat nasal bridge, brachycephaly, short neck), hypotonia, single palmar crease, sandal gap, brushfield spots; karyotype confirms.

Increased risk: congenital heart disease (50% — AVSD most common), duodenal atresia, Hirschsprung, hearing impairment, vision impairment, hypothyroidism, atlanto-axial instability, leukaemia (transient + later ALL/AML), obstructive sleep apnoea, dementia (early-onset Alzheimer).
Median life expectancy now > 60 years.
redFlags: Newborn — diagnose cardiac lesion early (often pre-symptomatic; echo essential).
Severe feeding difficulty / failure to thrive.
Atlantoaxial subluxation — neurological symptoms, neck pain — urgent imaging.
Transient abnormal myelopoiesis (TAM) at birth — usually resolves but ~20% develop AML.
Acute leukaemia at any age — particularly ALL + AML.
Adult-onset cognitive decline — Alzheimer pathology near-universal by 50 (clinical dementia in 50% by 60).

diagnostics.test: Newborn: karyotype confirmation; echo + CXR + audiology + ophthalmology; TSH + FBC.
diagnostics.rationale: Baseline + early detection of congenital abnormalities.

diagnostics.test: First year: monthly weight + height + growth on DS-specific charts; cardiac follow-up; TSH 6-monthly.

Childhood: annual TSH + FBC + audiology + ophthalmology + dental; coeliac (~5% risk); diabetes screening from age 5; lateral cervical-spine X-ray (controversial — selectively); sleep study for OSA risk.
Adolescent + adult: BMI + lipids + diabetes (high risk); sleep apnoea; mental health + cognitive screening; gynaecological; thyroid + coeliac annually.
Suspected dementia: structured cognitive assessment (CAMDEX-DS); collateral history.

management.detail: Paediatrician + cardiology + ENT + ophthalmology + endocrinology + audiology + dental + physiotherapy + speech + occupational + nutrition + community paediatrics + adult medicine + family support / DSA. Coordinated transition into adulthood.
Echo at diagnosis + per CHD findings. Surgical correction of AVSD in first 6 months; other CHD per specific anatomy. Adult surveillance for late-onset valve / arrhythmia.

Identify + treat congenital GI (duodenal atresia, Hirschsprung, anal stenosis) in newborn. Feeding support; PEG if needed. Coeliac screening; obesity prevention from school-age. Constipation management.
Lifelong TSH monitoring (~10% develop hypothyroidism). Diabetes screening — increased risk. Growth charts. Pubertal review.

Cataract, refractive error (glasses), keratoconus, strabismus, blocked tear ducts — early ophthalmology essential. Conductive (otitis media — frequent) + sensorineural hearing loss — annual audiology + hearing aids.

Counsel about contact sports + general anaesthesia (head/neck positioning); urgent imaging if neurological symptoms. Lateral cervical X-ray in flexion/extension if planning contact sport — recent guidance moves away from routine screening.

Early intervention services. Educational support (often individualised education plan; some attend mainstream with support). Autism spectrum disorder overlap (~15–20%). ADHD common. Adult-onset depression / anxiety common.
High prevalence (50–80%). Polysomnography + CPAP / surgical (tonsillectomy + adenoidectomy).

Alzheimer pathology near-universal by 40; clinical dementia 50% by 60. Disease-modifying therapy (anti-amyloid mAbs) emerging for early symptomatic stage with confirmed amyloid pathology. Structured dementia care + family support; CAMDEX-DS cognitive screening from age 30.
Increased infection susceptibility — full vaccination including pneumococcal + influenza + COVID + RSV (for at-risk infants). Selective antibiotic prophylaxis after recurrent infection.
Most men infertile; most women fertile (50% pregnancy with trisomy 21 in offspring). Contraception + sexual education + relationship support.
Structured adolescent — adult transition clinic. Continued multidisciplinary care. Advance care planning + end-of-life — increasingly relevant as life expectancy approaches general population.

references.label: AAP / DSMIG-USA Health Supervision for Children + Adolescents with Down Syndrome (2022); Trisomy 21 Research Society
Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (5th ed, 2022), Ministry of Health

title: Autism spectrum disorder — diagnosis + lifelong support
presentation: Persistent deficits in social communication + interaction + restricted, repetitive behaviours / interests + sensory differences — DSM-5 / ICD-11.
Early signs: reduced eye contact, response to name, joint attention, pointing, pretend play; speech delay or regression.
Spectrum: mild (level 1) to substantial (level 3) support needs.
Co-occurring: intellectual disability (~30%); ADHD (~50%); anxiety (~40%); depression; epilepsy (~25%); sleep disorders; gastrointestinal; sensory processing differences.
Female autism often underdiagnosed (different presentation — internalising, social masking).
redFlags: Regression of previously acquired skills — exclude neurodegenerative.
Suicidal ideation / self-harm in adolescent + adult.
Suspected abuse (autistic individuals at increased risk).

diagnostics.test: Standardised diagnostic instruments: ADOS-2 (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule) + ADI-R (Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised).
Genetic testing (chromosomal microarray + Fragile-X + whole-exome) — increasingly first-line.
diagnostics.rationale: Identify cause + family + reproductive counselling; treatment-relevant for some conditions.

diagnostics.test: EEG if seizures suspected; MRI selectively.
Mental health + behavioural screen at intervals.

management.step: Early intervention — within 12 months of identification
management.detail: Naturalistic developmental behavioural interventions (NDBI), Early Start Denver Model, parent-mediated programmes (e.g. JASPER, ImPACT). Frequency + intensity individualised. Speech + occupational + behavioural therapy as needed.
Parent / carer education + training; sibling support; respite. Move from 'normalisation' to support of authentic autistic identity. Co-produced with autistic community.
Augmentative + alternative communication (AAC) for minimally verbal — picture boards, sign language, speech-generating devices; speech + language therapy.
Individualised education plan; sensory accommodations (quiet space, noise-cancelling headphones, breaks); visual schedules; transition support. Adult: workplace accommodations + supported employment.

ADHD: stimulant / atomoxetine. Anxiety: SSRI + CBT (modified). Sleep: melatonin (good evidence) + sleep hygiene. Epilepsy: standard antiepileptic. Aggression / severe behaviour: behavioural intervention first; risperidone / aripiprazole (FDA-approved for irritability — only after non-pharm).
Occupational therapy for sensory integration + environmental adaptations; sensory tools (weighted blanket, fidget items, dimmed lighting, quiet times).
Watch for motor / verbal slowing, withdrawal, refusal of food, repetitive movements; benzodiazepine (lorazepam challenge); ECT for severe.
Many adults diagnosed late — particularly women + minoritised. Validation + post-diagnostic support; peer community; mental health treatment; employment + relationships.
Autistic adults — 9× elevated suicide risk. Routine screening for depression, anxiety, suicidality. Adapted therapy (modified CBT, autism-aware therapists).
Adolescent — adult transition critical; healthcare + education + employment + housing + relationships + finances. Lifelong support; community participation; aged-care planning.

references.label: NICE CG170 + CG142 Autism; AAP Autism Practice Guidelines; ESCAP Autism Position
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Type 1 diabetes — insulin pump + continuous glucose monitoring
presentation: Established type 1 diabetes requiring intensive insulin regimen.
Modalities: multiple daily injection (MDI — basal-bolus); insulin pump (CSII); hybrid closed-loop (HCL) automated insulin delivery (AID) — increasingly first-line.
Monitoring: capillary glucose; continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) — flash (rtCGM intermittent scan) or real-time CGM.
Targets: time-in-range 70–180 mg/dL > 70%; time below range < 4% (< 70) and < 1% (< 54); HbA1c < 7%.
redFlags: Recurrent DKA — typically poor adherence / pump dysfunction.
Diabetic ketoacidosis under pump therapy — pump can fail silently (cannula blockage / kink).
Eating disorder + T1D (T1DM with eating disorder / diabulimia) — high mortality.

diagnostics.test: HbA1c + capillary / CGM time-in-range every 3 months.
Annual: U&E + ACR + lipids + retinal screening + foot examination + thyroid + coeliac (autoimmune association) + BP.
Mental health + eating disorder screen (especially adolescent + young adult).
Ketone testing kit (blood or urine) at home.

management.detail: Structured education (DAFNE for adults; carbohydrate counting for children); carbohydrate counting; insulin-to-carb ratio; correction factor; sick-day rules; hypoglycaemia education.
Basal-bolus: long-acting (glargine U100 / U300, degludec, detemir) + rapid-acting (lispro, aspart, glulisine) with each meal + correction. Adjust per CGM patterns.

Continuous SC infusion via pump; basal rate + meal-time bolus + correction. Indications: difficult-to-control on MDI, frequent hypoglycaemia, dawn phenomenon, occupational, lifestyle, planning pregnancy. NICE: HbA1c > 8.5% on MDI OR severe hypoglycaemia.

Pump + CGM + algorithm modulating basal (and increasingly bolus) automatically. Currently approved: Medtronic 770G/780G, Tandem t:slim X2 with Control-IQ, Omnipod 5, CamAPS FX (CGM-pump-app hybrid). Open-source DIY systems (Loop, AndroidAPS). Improved time-in-range + reduced hypoglycaemia + reduced burden.

management.step: CGM — increasingly first-line for ALL T1D
management.detail: Real-time CGM (Dexcom G6/G7, Medtronic Guardian) — alerts. Flash (Libre 2/3). Improved outcomes + reduced hypoglycaemia (DIAMOND + GOLD trials). Healthcare-system coverage expanding.
Glucagon nasal spray (Baqsimi) OR injection (1 mg IM/SC for adult, 0.5 mg < 25 kg); IV 10% dextrose. Newer: dasiglucagon ready-to-use auto-injector. Family + colleague training in glucagon use.

Preconception HbA1c < 6.5%; high-dose folic acid 5 mg; pre-pregnancy retinal screen; pump + CGM strongly recommended; tighter glucose targets in pregnancy (FGM/CGM time-in-range > 70% target 63–140 mg/dL pregnancy); regular obstetric high-risk care; aspirin from 12 weeks.
Pramlintide (amylin analog) for postprandial spikes. SGLT2 inhibitor + GLP-1 agonist — not approved as routine T1D adjunct due to DKA risk.

Annual screening: retinopathy (from 5 years post-diagnosis adults; from age 12+ adolescents), nephropathy (UACR), peripheral neuropathy + foot, autonomic neuropathy. Statin from age 40 (or earlier with high risk). ACEi for albuminuria. SGLT2i for adult T1D with CKD ± CV disease selectively per specialist.
Annual structured education refresher; carer / family support; mental-health screening (PHQ-9, GAD-7, eating disorder); adolescent — adult transition clinic; technology training.

references.label: ADA Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes (annual); ISPAD Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines for paediatric; NICE NG18 + NG17 T1DM
Kenya National Clinical Guidelines for Management of Diabetes Mellitus, Ministry of Health

title: Schizophrenia — maintenance treatment + long-acting injectable
presentation: Established schizophrenia / schizoaffective disorder — beyond acute phase.
Maintenance phase: relapse prevention + functional restoration + comorbidity management.

Common: positive symptoms (residual hallucinations, delusions, thought disorder), negative symptoms (avolition, alogia, anhedonia, social withdrawal), cognitive deficits (attention, memory, executive function), depression / suicide risk (10%), substance use comorbidity (50%), metabolic syndrome (often medication-induced), cardiovascular disease (life expectancy reduced 15–20 years).
Risk of relapse: 60% within 1 year off medication.
redFlags: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (rigidity + hyperthermia + autonomic) — emergency.
Cardiovascular event — metabolic + adverse drug effects.
Pregnancy — maintain treatment; fetal antipsychotic exposure / neonatal extrapyramidal symptoms.

diagnostics.test: Symptom monitoring (PANSS / BPRS or clinical interview).
Annual: BMI + waist + BP + lipids + glucose + HbA1c + ECG (QT).
Clozapine: weekly FBC × 18 weeks → 2-weekly → monthly + ECG + troponin + cardiac symptoms — agranulocytosis + myocarditis monitoring.
AIMS / Glazov scale for tardive dyskinesia screening every 6 months.

management.step: Antipsychotic maintenance — continue 2-5 years after first episode
management.detail: After first episode: 2 years minimum; multiple episodes: 5+ years or indefinite. Patient-centred shared decision-making. Atypical antipsychotic preferred over first-generation (less EPS / TD; though metabolic risk).

Aripiprazole maintena (4-weekly), risperidone Consta (2-weekly), paliperidone (4-weekly or 3-monthly Trinza or 6-monthly Hafyera), olanzapine pamoate (LAI). Significantly reduce relapse + rehospitalisation. Offer EARLY (after first episode), not after multiple relapses.

Definition: failure of 2 adequate antipsychotic trials. Clozapine is THE most effective antipsychotic + UNIQUELY effective for TRS + reduces suicidality. Side effects: agranulocytosis (monitoring), seizures, myocarditis, metabolic, hypersalivation, constipation (severe — fatal), sedation. Combine with sulpiride / risperidone if partial response.

EPS: anticholinergic (procyclidine), switch agent. Akathisia: propranolol / mirtazapine / switch. Tardive dyskinesia: VMAT-2 inhibitor (valbenazine / deutetrabenazine — newer evidence). NMS: stop antipsychotic + supportive + dantrolene / bromocriptine.
Healthy lifestyle programmes; metformin for antipsychotic-induced weight gain; statin + BP control; smoking cessation (very high prevalence).
Cognitive behavioural therapy for psychosis (CBTp); family interventions; social skills training; supported employment; cognitive remediation; peer support.
Depression: SSRI (some QTc + interactions). Anxiety: avoid benzodiazepine long-term. Substance use: integrated dual diagnosis treatment. PTSD: trauma-focused therapy.

Continue antipsychotic (relapse risk > medication risk in most cases). Some agents safer (olanzapine, quetiapine, aripiprazole); folate; specialist perinatal psychiatry. Neonatal extrapyramidal symptoms / sedation possible — neonatology aware.
Annual physical health check (often poor in standard psychiatric care). Smoking cessation. Dental. Adolescent-adult / adult-elderly care transitions. Family + carer support.
Co-produced crisis plan; advance statements; emergency contact + community team; named worker / care coordinator.

references.label: NICE CG178 Psychosis + schizophrenia in adults; APA Practice Guideline for Schizophrenia; Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Bipolar disorder — long-term maintenance + relapse prevention
presentation: Recurrent mood episodes — bipolar I (mania ± depression) or bipolar II (hypomania + depression).
Maintenance phase: euthymic but lifelong relapse risk; functional impairment; cognitive symptoms; comorbidities (anxiety 60%, substance use 40%, ADHD 20%, eating disorders, PTSD).
Suicide risk lifetime 15–20% (highest of all psychiatric disorders).
Cardiovascular + metabolic premature mortality.
redFlags: Mixed features (depression + hyperarousal / racing thoughts) — high suicide risk.
Switch to mania on antidepressant (avoid antidepressant monotherapy).
Pregnancy + bipolar — relapse risk + medication selection.

diagnostics.test: Lifetime mood pattern + family history (often delays diagnosis).
Mood charting + symptom rating (e.g. YMRS, MADRS).
Annual: BMI + lipids + glucose + thyroid + ECG + lithium levels (if on Li); U&E + creatinine + Ca (lithium effects).
Pregnancy test in women starting valproate.

management.step: Lithium — first-line for maintenance + acute mania + bipolar depression
management.detail: Target trough 0.6–0.8 mmol/L (some up to 1.0). Reduces relapse + suicide. Side effects: tremor, polydipsia / polyuria (nephrogenic DI), hypothyroidism, weight gain, cognitive, GI, renal toxicity (long-term). Monitor U&E + Ca + thyroid + lithium every 3–6 months. Avoid NSAID + thiazide + ACEi (raise levels).

500–2000 mg/day; trough 50–125 mg/L. AVOID in women of childbearing potential — major teratogen (10% NTD + behavioural). Pregnancy Prevention Programme required. Side effects: weight gain, alopecia, tremor, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, PCOS.
25 mg → 200 mg over 6 weeks (slow titration to avoid SJS). Best for depressive predominance. AVOID combining with valproate (increases lamotrigine levels markedly).

Quetiapine (mania + depression + maintenance), olanzapine, risperidone, aripiprazole, asenapine, lurasidone (bipolar depression), cariprazine (bipolar depression). LAI considered for non-adherent. Metabolic monitoring.
Risk of mania induction + rapid cycling. If used, combine with mood stabiliser; consider lithium-augmentation or atypical antipsychotic (quetiapine + lurasidone) for bipolar depression.

management.step: ECT for severe / refractory / catatonic / psychotic mania or depression
management.detail: Highly effective; safe in pregnancy + elderly + treatment-resistant.

CBT for bipolar; interpersonal social rhythm therapy (IPSRT); family-focused therapy; psychoeducation. Sleep hygiene + regular routine + circadian regulation. Exercise. Avoid alcohol + recreational drugs. Identify + manage early warning signs (mood diary, family early alert).
Anxiety, substance use, ADHD — careful selection avoiding mood destabilisation. Treat physical health proactively (CV, metabolic, thyroid).

Specialist perinatal psychiatry. Lithium relatively safe (avoid 1st trimester if possible; reduce dose in 3rd; postpartum LITHIUM PROPHYLAXIS reduces severe relapse). Valproate CONTRAINDICATED. Lamotrigine safer. ECT safe in pregnancy. Postpartum is highest-risk period for severe relapse / postpartum psychosis (50% recurrence).
Lithium has independent anti-suicidal effect. Means restriction. Crisis planning. Family involvement. Safety planning at every visit.
Comprehensive psychoeducation; mood charting; relapse prevention plan; peer support (Bipolar UK; DBSA). Workplace / educational accommodation.

references.label: NICE CG185 Bipolar Disorder; CANMAT-ISBD Bipolar Guidelines; APA Practice Guideline
Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Mental, Neurological and Substance Use Disorders (mhGAP adaptation), Ministry of Health

title: Prostate cancer — screening + risk-stratified treatment
presentation: Often asymptomatic; detected on PSA / DRE screening.
Local: LUTS (overlap with BPH), haematuria, haematospermia.
Advanced: bone pain (skeletal metastases — bone scan), pathological fracture, spinal cord compression, lymphoedema, anaemia, weight loss.
Risk factors: age, family history, BRCA1/2 + Lynch syndrome (increased risk + earlier onset + more aggressive), Black African heritage.
redFlags: Suspected spinal cord compression — urgent MRI + dexamethasone + radiotherapy.
Acute urinary retention from local disease.

diagnostics.test: Screening: PSA + digital rectal examination — discuss benefits/risks individualised; from age 50 (45 if Black or family history); STOP at age 70 / life expectancy < 10–15 years.
diagnostics.rationale: Detection of clinically significant prostate cancer; overdiagnosis remains concern.

diagnostics.test: Suspicious PSA: multiparametric MRI prostate (FIRST) — PI-RADS 3-5 for biopsy.
diagnostics.rationale: Avoids unnecessary biopsies; identifies clinically significant lesions.

diagnostics.test: MRI-guided / fusion biopsy of suspicious lesions; systematic biopsy.
Staging: MRI prostate + lymph nodes; PSMA-PET (preferred) or bone scan + CT (high risk).
Genetic testing if family history / metastatic / atypical histology / young.

management.detail: Urologist + oncologist + radiation oncologist + radiologist + pathologist.
Serial PSA + DRE + MRI ± repeat biopsy; treatment if progression. ProtecT trial — 10-year survival equivalent between active surveillance, surgery, radiation.

Radical prostatectomy (open / robotic) — younger / lower comorbidity. External beam radiotherapy + androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for high-risk. Brachytherapy (low-dose-rate + high-dose-rate) alternative. Pelvic lymph node dissection per risk.

management.step: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) — TRIPLET therapy
management.detail: ADT (GnRH agonist degarelix / leuprolide; or antagonist relugolix) + docetaxel + AR pathway inhibitor (abiraterone OR enzalutamide OR apalutamide OR darolutamide). Triplet superior to doublet (PEACE-1 + ARASENS).

management.step: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) — sequential novel agents
management.detail: ARSI (abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide); cabazitaxel; radium-223 for bone-metastatic; PARP inhibitor (olaparib, rucaparib, talazoparib) for BRCA-mutated; PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy (lutetium-177-PSMA — VISION trial); sipuleucel-T (limited use).

Zoledronate or denosumab monthly for bone metastases (reduce SREs). Vitamin D + calcium. Palliative radiotherapy. Spinal cord compression pathway. Pain management. Hot flushes (ADT) — venlafaxine / cyproterone.

Sexual function (PDE-5i, intracavernosal alprostadil, penile prosthesis); urinary continence; bone health (DEXA + bisphosphonate / denosumab on ADT); cardiovascular (ADT increases events); metabolic; depression. Survivorship clinic.
BRCA1/2 + multi-gene panel for family + treatment-defining (PARP inhibitor); cascade testing of first-degree relatives.

references.label: EAU + NCCN Prostate Cancer Guidelines; ProtecT trial; PEACE-1 + ARASENS + VISION trials
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Sustained ventricular tachycardia / ventricular fibrillation
presentation: Monomorphic VT: regular wide-QRS tachycardia > 100 bpm; sustained > 30 s or with haemodynamic instability.
Polymorphic VT: torsades de pointes — QT-prolongation-related (drugs, electrolyte, congenital LQTS); non-TdP polymorphic in ischaemia / heart failure.
VF: chaotic; pulseless; cardiac arrest.
Aetiology: structural heart disease (ischaemia/post-MI scar, cardiomyopathy), inherited channelopathy (LQTS, Brugada, CPVT), electrolyte (K+, Mg2+), drugs (QT-prolonging), idiopathic.
redFlags: Haemodynamic instability — IMMEDIATE DC cardioversion / defibrillation.
Recurrent VT / VF (electrical storm — ≥ 3 episodes in 24 h).
Brugada syndrome with VF — implantable defibrillator + family screen.
Post-MI new VT — risk for sudden death; refer EP.
Congenital LQTS with TdP — bradycardia + electrolyte + drug-trigger reversal.

diagnostics.rationale: Confirm rhythm + QT + Brugada / LQTS pattern.

diagnostics.test: U&E (K+, Mg2+, Ca2+), troponin, glucose, ABG.
Cardiac MRI — scar pattern (post-MI vs cardiomyopathy vs ARVC vs sarcoid).
Genetic testing for inherited (LQTS, CPVT, Brugada, HCM, ARVC).

management.step: Pulseless VT / VF — defibrillate IMMEDIATELY + ACLS
management.detail: Biphasic 150–200 J; continue CPR; adrenaline 1 mg every 3–5 min from 2nd shock; amiodarone 300 mg IV after 3 shocks (refractory). Identify + reverse causes (4 Hs + 4 Ts).

Unstable (hypotension / pulmonary oedema / chest pain / altered consciousness): synchronised DC cardioversion 100–200 J. Stable: IV amiodarone 150 mg bolus then 1 mg/min × 6 h then 0.5 mg/min × 18 h; OR procainamide 20 mg/min loading (preferred per recent evidence — PROCAMIO); OR sotalol IV (caution QT); OR lignocaine 1–1.5 mg/kg (older; preferred in MI context). Beta-blocker also useful.

Magnesium sulphate 2 g IV bolus + 2 g/h infusion. Correct K+ + Mg2+. Stop QT-prolonging drugs (list current medications; check Liverpool QT database). Isoprenaline / overdrive pacing to shorten QT if bradycardia-dependent.

Sedation (propofol / midazolam) + intubation reduces sympathetic drive. Amiodarone + beta-blocker. Stellate ganglion block for refractory. Catheter ablation (epicardial / endocardial). Mechanical circulatory support (ECMO, Impella) as bridge.

Treat ischaemia (revascularisation); correct electrolyte; stop QT-prolonging drug. Optimise heart failure therapy. Beta-blocker + ACE inhibitor / ARB + sacubitril-valsartan for HFrEF; SGLT2 inhibitor.

Secondary prevention: ICD for survivors of cardiac arrest, sustained VT with structural heart disease. Primary prevention: LVEF ≤ 35% on optimal HF therapy ≥ 3 months (post-MI ≥ 40 days); inherited channelopathy with high risk; HCM with high-risk features; ARVC; sarcoidosis with scar. Wearable cardioverter defibrillator (WCD, LifeVest) as bridge.
Idiopathic VT (outflow tract, fascicular) — often curative. Scar-related VT (post-MI, cardiomyopathy, ARVC) — substrate-based ablation; reduces ICD shocks + improves outcomes.

LQTS: beta-blocker (nadolol or propranolol); avoid QT-prolonging drugs; left cardiac sympathetic denervation for refractory. Brugada: ICD; quinidine to suppress; avoid febrile illness + offending drugs. CPVT: beta-blocker + flecainide; consider ICD; left cardiac sympathetic denervation. Family screening + cascade genetic testing.
Inherited channelopathy / cardiomyopathy — family screening of first-degree relatives with ECG + echo ± genetic testing. Lifestyle modification (avoid trigger sports for some).

references.label: ESC Guidelines for Management of Patients with Ventricular Arrhythmias + Prevention of Sudden Cardiac Death (2022); AHA/ACC/HRS VA-SCD
Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Infective endocarditis — comprehensive management
presentation: Fever + new / changing murmur + embolic phenomena + persistent bacteraemia.
Modified Duke criteria for diagnosis (major: blood cultures + endocardial involvement; minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic, microbiologic).

Common organisms: Staph aureus (most common; especially IV drug users + healthcare-associated), Streptococcus viridans (subacute on damaged native valves), Enterococcus (elderly + post-procedural), Coagulase-negative staph (prosthetic), HACEK (rare), culture-negative (5–15% — fastidious, prior antibiotic).
Risk: prior IE, prosthetic valve, congenital heart disease, structural valve disease, IV drug use, immunosuppression, indwelling line / pacemaker / ICD, recent dental / GI / GU procedure.
redFlags: Large mobile vegetation > 10 mm — high embolic risk.
Cerebral embolic event (35% have CNS complications) — caution timing of surgery.
Suspected prosthetic-valve IE — high mortality + complex management.
Right-sided IE in IVDU — septic pulmonary emboli.

diagnostics.test: Blood cultures × 3 sets from different sites + 30 min apart BEFORE antibiotic.
TTE first; TOE if TTE non-diagnostic / negative + clinical suspicion remains / prosthetic valve / complications suspected.
diagnostics.rationale: Identify vegetation + valve abnormality + perivalvular complications.

diagnostics.test: PET-CT for diagnostic uncertainty (prosthetic valve, CIED).
diagnostics.rationale: Adjunctive — increasingly important in 2023 ESC criteria.

diagnostics.test: FBC, CRP, ESR, U&E, urinalysis, fungal markers if culture-negative.
Dental + brain MRI + CT body for embolic search.
Bartonella, Coxiella, Brucella, Mycoplasma, Tropheryma whippelii serology for culture-negative.

management.detail: Cardiology + ID + cardiothoracic surgery + microbiology + neurology + radiology — joint care reduces mortality.

management.step: Empirical antibiotic ONLY after blood cultures
management.detail: Native valve / community: vancomycin + ceftriaxone OR ampicillin + gentamicin + flucloxacillin. Prosthetic valve / healthcare: vancomycin + gentamicin + rifampicin + cefepime. Adjust to identified organism.

Strep viridans / bovis (penicillin-susceptible): IV penicillin G 12–18 MU/24 h × 4 weeks (or 2 weeks combined with gentamicin). Staph aureus (MSSA): flucloxacillin 12 g/24 h × 4–6 weeks. MRSA: vancomycin OR daptomycin × 4–6 weeks. Enterococcus: ampicillin + gentamicin × 4–6 weeks (or ampicillin + ceftriaxone for HLAR). HACEK: ceftriaxone × 4–6 weeks. Prosthetic valve: 6 weeks + rifampicin.

Heart failure (acute severe regurgitation); uncontrolled infection (persistent bacteraemia, perivalvular extension, abscess, fungal/MDRO); embolism prevention (vegetation > 10 mm with prior embolism or > 15 mm); fungal endocarditis (always surgery).

Emergency (< 24 h): refractory heart failure, severe acute mitral / aortic regurgitation with shock. Urgent (within days): uncontrolled infection. Elective: large vegetation + healed embolic. Stroke complicates — re-image; usually safe to operate but multi-disciplinary decision per stroke type + size.
Complete device + lead extraction; antibiotics 4–6 weeks; new device after 14 days negative cultures + on opposite side / epicardial.
Mechanical valve IE: continue (stroke risk). Discontinue all anticoagulation in S. aureus IE with intracerebral haemorrhage / large embolic stroke.

Dental + IDU intervention; CIED hygiene; prophylactic antibiotic prior to high-risk dental procedures in IE-survivors / prosthetic / cyanotic CHD (per current restricted criteria). Echo follow-up; valve replacement surveillance.

Right-sided IE in IVDU (tricuspid): often medical only (uncomplicated MSSA); surgery for refractory / large vegetation. Culture-negative: empirical doxycycline + ceftriaxone for Coxiella / Bartonella; Bartonella PCR / serology.

references.label: ESC Guidelines for the Management of Endocarditis (2023); AHA/IDSA Endocarditis
Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy — diagnosis + risk stratification
presentation: Most common inherited cardiac disease (1 in 500).
Asymptomatic — often family screening / pre-participation.
Symptomatic: dyspnoea, chest pain, palpitations, syncope, sudden cardiac death.
Subtypes: obstructive HCM (~70% — LVOTO at rest or on provocation > 30 mmHg); non-obstructive HCM; apical HCM (Yamaguchi).
Risk: sudden death (especially adolescents + young adults), heart failure, atrial fibrillation, stroke, atypical chest pain, exercise limitation.
redFlags: Sustained / inducible ventricular tachycardia / aborted sudden death.
End-stage 'burnout' phase with LV dysfunction / dilation.
Atrial fibrillation in HCM — high stroke risk.
Family history of sudden death — screening + risk stratification.

diagnostics.test: ECG (LVH + repolarisation, deep narrow Q waves, T-wave inversion).
TTE — wall thickness ≥ 15 mm (or ≥ 13 mm with family history) without explanatory load; LVOTO at rest + Valsalva; systolic anterior motion of mitral valve.
Cardiac MRI — wall thickness measurement + LGE (scar — risk marker).
Holter monitoring 24–48 h for ventricular arrhythmia.
Exercise stress echocardiography for LVOTO + ambulatory BP.
diagnostics.rationale: Provocable obstruction + functional capacity + abnormal BP response.

diagnostics.test: Genetic testing (sarcomeric panel) + cascade family screening.
Calculate HCM Risk-SCD score (ESC) or ACC/AHA enhanced major risk markers.

management.detail: Avoid competitive / high-intensity sport (especially severe LVOTO, family SCD history, sustained arrhythmia). Moderate recreational exercise increasingly endorsed (LIVE-HCM, RESET-HCM trials). Smoking cessation. Maintain hydration.

management.step: Symptomatic LVOT obstruction — first-line beta-blocker / non-DHP CCB
management.detail: Bisoprolol or metoprolol up-titrated. Verapamil or diltiazem (caution — avoid in resting LVOT gradient > 100 mmHg). Avoid vasodilators (DHP CCB, ACE inhibitor, diuretic over-treatment, nitrates) — worsen LVOTO.

management.step: Mavacamten — disease-modifying for symptomatic obstructive HCM (NYHA II-III)
management.detail: Cardiac myosin inhibitor; 2.5–15 mg daily. REMS programme — echo monitoring (LVEF < 50% threshold for hold). EXPLORER-HCM + VALOR-HCM trials. Aficamten — newer alternative.

management.step: Septal reduction therapy for refractory symptomatic LVOTO
management.detail: Surgical septal myectomy (preferred, gold standard); alcohol septal ablation (for higher surgical risk). Specialist HCM centre.

Secondary prevention: SCD survivor, sustained VT. Primary prevention based on HCM Risk-SCD score (ESC > 6%) or ACC/AHA major risk markers (family SCD, massive LVH ≥ 30 mm, recent syncope, abnormal BP response, NSVT > 3 beats > 120 bpm, extensive LGE, LV aneurysm).
Anticoagulation — DOAC / warfarin (irrespective of CHA2DS2-VASc); HCM is independent stroke risk factor. Rhythm control preferred; catheter ablation often needed; amiodarone.
Standard heart-failure therapy; consider heart transplantation.

First-degree relatives — ECG + echocardiography every 5 years (or earlier with clinical concerns) starting at age 10–12; genetic testing if proband variant identified; positive carriers screened more frequently.

Most women tolerate pregnancy well; multidisciplinary care. Risk varies by symptoms + LV function + arrhythmia. Avoid vasodilators; continue beta-blocker. Vaginal delivery preferred for most; epidural cautious (gradient may rise).

references.label: ESC Guidelines for the Management of Cardiomyopathies (2023); ACC/AHA HCM Guideline (2024)

title: Marfan syndrome — aortic surveillance + multidisciplinary management
presentation: Autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder — FBN1 mutations.
Cardiovascular: aortic root dilation + dissection (leading cause of mortality), mitral valve prolapse + regurgitation, pulmonary artery dilation.
Ocular: ectopia lentis (lens dislocation — 60%), myopia, retinal detachment, early cataract.
Skeletal: tall stature, arachnodactyly, scoliosis, pectus excavatum / carinatum, joint hypermobility, dural ectasia, high-arched palate, dolichocephaly.
Pulmonary: pneumothorax, restrictive lung disease.
Skin: striae, hernias.
redFlags: New chest / back pain — exclude aortic dissection.
Aortic root > 50 mm or rapid growth (> 3 mm/year) — surgery indication.
Pregnancy + aortic root > 40 mm — high-risk; specialist care.
Acute lens dislocation with vision change.

diagnostics.test: Echo for aortic root dimension (Z-score for age + body surface area), MV prolapse + regurgitation, LV / RV function.
Cardiac MRI for aortic root + arch + descending; CT angio for full aorta.
diagnostics.rationale: Comprehensive aortic assessment; baseline + every 2–5 years.

diagnostics.test: Genetic testing — FBN1 sequence + deletion / duplication; multi-gene panel (TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2, TGFB3 for related disorders — Loeys-Dietz).
Spine + chest examination + DEXA + spirometry as needed.

management.detail: Cardiology + cardiothoracic surgery + ophthalmology + orthopaedics / spinal + genetics / counsellor + adult / paediatric medicine.

Beta-blocker (lifelong from diagnosis) — atenolol or losartan — reduces aortic dilation. ARB (losartan) — alternative or combined; AIMS / COMPARE trials. ACE inhibitor for hypertension. Avoid stimulants + vasoconstrictors.
AVOID isometric exercise + heavy weightlifting + contact / collision sports + competitive intense aerobic (especially if aortic root > 40 mm). Light-moderate aerobic acceptable. Smoking cessation.
Echo annually (more if rapid growth or > 40 mm); CT or MRI angio every 2–5 years for whole aorta. Children: more frequent depending on growth + family history.

Indications: aortic root diameter ≥ 50 mm in adults (45 mm if family history of dissection / rapid growth / planning pregnancy); 47 mm in children. Valve-sparing root replacement (David procedure) preferred over Bentall (composite mechanical + valve) if anatomy + experienced centre. Post-op lifelong follow-up + endocarditis prophylaxis.
Type A (ascending) — emergency surgery. Type B (descending) — medical first-line; TEVAR for complicated. Per aortic-dissection pathway.

Pre-conception counselling; assess aortic dimension; prophylactic root replacement if > 40 mm and planning. Continue beta-blocker through pregnancy; restrict activity; serial echo every 4–6 weeks. Vaginal delivery for stable; LSCS if dilation. Family-planning + 50% offspring inheritance.
Annual review; correct refractive error; lens dislocation may need surgery; retinal detachment risk.
Scoliosis bracing / surgery for progressive curves. Pectus repair for cosmetic / cardiopulmonary impact. Joint protection. Foot orthoses.
First-degree relatives — clinical + echo + slit-lamp ± genetic testing. Reproductive counselling — pre-implantation genetic diagnosis option.

references.label: Revised Ghent Nosology (Loeys et al. 2010); ESC/AHA aortic-disease guidelines; Marfan Foundation

title: Adult nephrotic syndrome — diagnosis + treatment by aetiology
presentation: Diagnostic triad: heavy proteinuria > 3.5 g/24 h + hypoalbuminaemia (< 30 g/L) + oedema (often pitting; periorbital + dependent).
Hyperlipidaemia + thrombotic risk (urinary loss of antithrombin) + infection susceptibility (urinary loss of IgG + complement).
Adult aetiology: membranous nephropathy (~30%), FSGS (~25%), minimal change disease (~10%), diabetic nephropathy, lupus nephritis, amyloidosis, MGUS / myeloma, secondary causes.
redFlags: Acute thrombosis (DVT, PE, renal vein thrombosis) — anticoagulation.
Severe oedema with pleural effusion + ascites.
AKI from intravascular volume depletion or contrast / drug.

diagnostics.test: Urinary protein-creatinine ratio (UPCR) or 24-h urine collection.

Serum albumin, U&E, lipids, FBC, fasting glucose / HbA1c, complement (C3 + C4), ANA + anti-dsDNA, anti-PLA2R + THSD7A (membranous), serum + urine immunofixation + light chains, hepatitis B + C + HIV + syphilis, ANCA.

diagnostics.rationale: Diagnose specific GN; treatment depends on pathology.

diagnostics.test: Renal USS + Doppler for renal vein thrombosis.
Cancer screen in older (especially anti-PLA2R-negative membranous).

management.detail: Salt restriction (< 100 mmol/day) + fluid restriction; loop diuretic (furosemide + thiazide / metolazone for refractory); ACEi/ARB to reduce proteinuria + protect renal function; statin for lipids; pneumococcal + influenza vaccination.
Anti-Xa or warfarin if serum albumin < 25 g/L AND additional risk factor (membranous nephropathy has highest VTE risk). Treat established VTE with full anticoagulation × at least 6 months.

First-line (high-risk per KDIGO): rituximab 1 g IV × 2 doses 2 weeks apart, OR ciclosporin / tacrolimus, OR Ponticelli regimen (alternating cyclophosphamide + steroid 6 months). Anti-PLA2R titre tracks response. Spontaneous remission in 30%.

management.step: Minimal change disease (more common in children but presents in adults)
management.detail: Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day × 16 weeks then taper. Steroid-resistant: ciclosporin, tacrolimus, mycophenolate, rituximab. Relapsing: long-term immunosuppression.

Primary: high-dose steroid × 6 months → ciclosporin / rituximab for steroid-resistant. Genetic causes — no benefit from immunosuppression; manage ACEi + supportive. Secondary FSGS (obesity, virus, drug, reflux): treat underlying.
Tight glycaemic + BP control + ACEi/ARB + SGLT2i + finerenone (foundational quartet; see CKD pathway). Avoid immunosuppression.
Per SLE flare pathway — MMF or cyclophosphamide + steroid + hydroxychloroquine + belimumab.
Per amyloidosis pathway — Dara-CyBorD for AL; treat plasma-cell dyscrasia.

management.step: Refractory / progressive disease — dialysis + transplant referral
management.detail: Manage as CKD progression; renal replacement therapy planning.

references.label: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Glomerular Diseases (2021)

title: IgA nephropathy — diagnosis + risk-stratified treatment
presentation: Most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide.

Visible (macroscopic) haematuria episodes — often within 1–3 days of URTI ('synpharyngitic'); microscopic haematuria + proteinuria most common presentation; hypertension; CKD progression in 25–30% over 20 years.
Rare presentations: rapidly progressive GN (crescentic), nephrotic syndrome, acute kidney injury.
Co-occurring: Henoch-Schönlein purpura (IgA vasculitis), inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease, chronic liver disease.
redFlags: Rapidly progressive GN (crescents > 25% on biopsy) — pulse steroid + cyclophosphamide.
Heavy proteinuria + high BP + reduced eGFR — high-risk progression.
Acute kidney injury during macroscopic haematuria episode (acute tubular obstruction).
MEST-C score on biopsy — Oxford classification (mesangial / endocapillary / segmental sclerosis / tubular atrophy / crescents).

diagnostics.test: UPCR + serum creatinine + eGFR + BP at every visit.
Renal biopsy with MEST-C scoring + immunofluorescence (mesangial IgA dominance).
Exclude secondary IgA: chronic liver disease (cirrhosis), HIV, IBD, coeliac, gluten enteropathy.

management.detail: ACEi/ARB titrated to maximum tolerated (reduces proteinuria + slows progression); BP target < 130/80 or lower in heavy proteinuria. SGLT2i for proteinuria > 1 g/day (DAPA-CKD + EMPA-KIDNEY).

management.step: High-risk patients (UPCR > 0.75 g/g despite ACEi optimisation × 3 months) — escalate
management.detail: Targeted-release budesonide (Nefecon, 16 mg/day × 9 months) — first-line per recent NefIgArd trial; gut-targeted reduces mucosal IgA. Combination with SGLT2i + RAS blockade.
PROTECT trial showed proteinuria reduction; FDA-approved for IgA nephropathy with high progression risk. Specialist initiation.
IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily × 3 days + cyclophosphamide × 3–6 months → maintenance azathioprine. Plasma exchange for severe / dialysis-dependent (selected centres).

management.step: Avoid blanket high-dose immunosuppression for stable disease
management.detail: TESTING + STOP-IgAN trials caution risk-benefit of conventional systemic steroids. Use targeted budesonide preferentially.
Some evidence for benefit in Japanese / Asian populations; not universally adopted. Consider in selected cases.
Treat underlying coeliac / IBD; manage chronic liver disease.
Some familial cases; counsel siblings about screening.
Pre-conception planning; switch ACEi to alternative; aspirin for pre-eclampsia prevention; close BP + proteinuria monitoring.

references.label: KDIGO Glomerular Diseases 2021; NefIgArd + PROTECT + DAPA-CKD trials

title: Acquired long QT syndrome + torsades de pointes
presentation: QT prolongation on ECG (QTc > 500 ms strongly increased risk; > 460 ms women / > 450 ms men borderline).
Torsades de pointes: polymorphic VT with twisting QRS axis on ECG; usually self-terminating but can degenerate to VF.

Causes: QT-prolonging drugs (antiarrhythmic IA + III, antibiotics — macrolides, fluoroquinolones, antifungals, antipsychotics, antidepressants, antiemetics, methadone), electrolyte derangements (hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, hypocalcaemia), bradyarrhythmia (pause-dependent), starvation / eating disorder, hypothermia, hypothyroidism.
Risk factors: female, age > 65, structural heart disease, prolonged baseline QT, concurrent QT-prolonging drugs, hepatic / renal impairment.
redFlags: Suicidal / accidental overdose of QT-prolonging drug.

diagnostics.test: 12-lead ECG — measure QT (Bazett or Fridericia correction).
Medication review against Liverpool QT database / CredibleMeds.
If TdP without obvious cause: consider congenital LQTS — genetic testing + family screen.

management.detail: Unsynchronised defibrillation 200 J biphasic.
2 g IV bolus over 1–2 min; repeat once; continue infusion 2 g/h until QTc < 500 ms + no further TdP. Effective even with normal Mg level.
K+ to 4.5–5.0 mmol/L (aggressive). Mg2+ to upper-normal. Ca2+ to normal.
Review medication list against Liverpool QT database. Switch to non-QT-prolonging alternatives. Counsel patient + record allergy / warning.

management.step: Bradycardia-dependent TdP — shorten QT by raising heart rate
management.detail: Transcutaneous pacing OR transvenous pacing (target HR 90–100); OR isoproterenol infusion 1–2 microgram/min IV (titrate to HR 90–100); useful while preparing pacing or as bridge.
Lignocaine 1–1.5 mg/kg IV. Mexiletine (oral; specialist). Phenytoin. Beta-blocker (esmolol) — controversial in acute TdP but useful prevention after stabilisation.
Treat hypothyroidism; correct hypothermia; treat starvation (anorexia / refeeding syndrome); reverse drug overdose.

ECG monitoring × 24–48 h after last episode. Counsel patient + family + GP about avoidable QT-prolonging drugs (provide list). Implantable defibrillator only if recurrent despite reversible-cause correction OR underlying severe substrate.

Beta-blocker (nadolol or propranolol — class IA recommendation); avoid QT-prolonging drugs lifelong; competitive sport restriction (some); cardiac MRI / EP study; left cardiac sympathetic denervation for refractory; ICD for high-risk.

references.label: ESC Ventricular Arrhythmia + SCD 2022; Liverpool QT Drug Database; CredibleMeds.org

title: Peripheral arterial disease — chronic management + limb salvage
presentation: Intermittent claudication — exercise-induced calf / thigh / buttock pain relieved by rest.
Critical / chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI): rest pain, non-healing ulcer, gangrene.
Risk factors: smoking, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, age, family history, CKD.
Often part of polyvascular disease — coronary + cerebrovascular involvement.
Diabetic foot complicates frequently.
redFlags: Critical limb-threatening ischaemia (rest pain, ulcer, gangrene) — refer urgently.
Suspected acute on chronic limb ischaemia.

diagnostics.test: Ankle-brachial pressure index (ABPI) — < 0.9 diagnostic; < 0.5 severe; > 1.4 incompressible (DM, ESRD) — use TBI.
Toe-brachial index (TBI) for incompressible arteries / diabetes.
Arterial duplex / CT angiography / MR angiography.
Fasting lipids + HbA1c + U&E + creatinine + BP + smoking status.

management.detail: Smoking cessation (single most important; counsel + pharmacotherapy). HbA1c < 7%. BP < 130/80 (ACEi / ARB first-line). Statin (high-intensity) regardless of baseline lipid (atorvastatin 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg).

Aspirin 75 mg OR clopidogrel 75 mg daily. Add low-dose rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD to aspirin (COMPASS, VOYAGER-PAD) — significant cardiovascular + limb benefit. Single antiplatelet for intermittent claudication if no symptomatic CAD.

management.step: Supervised exercise programme — first-line for claudication
management.detail: 30–60 min/week × 12 weeks supervised — improves walking distance ≥ 100%. Home-based programmes secondary.
Cilostazol 100 mg BD — improves walking distance; AVOID in heart failure. Naftidrofuryl 200 mg TDS alternative.

Urgent specialist vascular assessment. Endovascular revascularisation (angioplasty + stent) — first-line for most. Open surgical bypass for long lesions / multi-level / poor endo runoff (BASIL-2, BEST-CLI trials). Hybrid procedures. Amputation only when limb non-salvageable.
Specialist diabetic foot / wound clinic (see diabetic foot pathway). Offloading + debridement + antibiotic per infection severity.
Analgesia ladder for ischaemic rest pain; gabapentin for neuropathic component; spinal cord stimulator for refractory inoperable.
Annual ABPI + symptom + cardiovascular risk reassessment. Post-revascularisation: surveillance USS at 3, 6, 12 months. Lifelong antiplatelet + statin.

references.label: ESVS Guideline on Peripheral Arterial Diseases (2024); AHA/ACC Lower Extremity PAD; COMPASS + VOYAGER-PAD trials
Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
presentation: Symptoms + signs of heart failure (dyspnoea, fatigue, oedema) WITH LVEF ≥ 50%.
H2FPEF score (Heavy, hypertension, atrial Fibrillation, Pulmonary hypertension, Elderly, elevated Filling pressures) — diagnostic aid.
Comorbidities are central: hypertension (90%), obesity (40–80%), diabetes (40%), atrial fibrillation (40%), CKD, anaemia, COPD, sleep apnoea.
Increasing prevalence — now > 50% of HF cases.
redFlags: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response — precipitates flash pulmonary oedema.
Concurrent ischaemic heart disease + acute coronary syndrome.
Suspected cardiac amyloidosis (especially elderly + thickened ventricle + low voltages + carpal tunnel history).

diagnostics.test: Echocardiogram — preserved LVEF ≥ 50% + diastolic dysfunction (E/e' > 14, tricuspid regurgitation velocity > 2.8 m/s, LA volume index > 34 mL/m²).
BNP / NT-proBNP — elevated; thresholds vary by age + AF.
Cardiac MRI — when amyloid suspected (LGE + T1 mapping); HCM + sarcoidosis assessment.
Cardiopulmonary exercise testing if diagnosis uncertain.
Investigate amyloidosis: serum + urine immunofixation + free light chains; 99mTc-PYP / DPD bone scan for ATTR; abdominal fat pad biopsy.
Iron studies, thyroid, sleep study, OGTT, vitamin D.

management.step: SGLT2 inhibitor — first-line for ALL HFpEF
management.detail: Dapagliflozin OR empagliflozin 10 mg daily (DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved trials). Reduces HF hospitalisations + cardiovascular death. Effective regardless of diabetes status. Approved for HFpEF.
Spironolactone 25 mg daily (TOPCAT subgroup analysis showed benefit in patients with elevated BNP). Monitor K+ + creatinine.
Loop diuretic (furosemide, torsemide, bumetanide) titrated to euvolaemia. Thiazide adjunct for resistance. Aggressive diuresis can precipitate hypotension + AKI in HFpEF (more so than HFrEF).
BP < 130/80 — uncontrolled HTN drives HFpEF. ACEi / ARB / sacubitril-valsartan + CCB + thiazide; spironolactone. Loop diuretic also lowers BP via volume.
Rate or rhythm control per individual. Increasingly rhythm control favoured in HFpEF + AF (CABANA + EAST-AFNET 4 subgroups). Anticoagulation per CHA2DS2-VASc.
Caloric restriction + structured exercise — improves symptoms + quality of life (STEP-HFpEF trial — semaglutide also improves).

management.step: Treat sleep apnoea, anaemia, iron deficiency
management.detail: CPAP for moderate-severe OSA. Iron infusion for iron-deficiency (IRONMAN, AFFIRM-AHF — beneficial). Treat anaemia.
If ATTR cardiomyopathy: tafamidis 61 mg or 80 mg daily — improves survival. Patisiran / vutrisiran for ATTR neuropathy + cardiomyopathy.
Surgical pericardiectomy for severe constrictive disease.
Advanced HFpEF — symptom-focused; advance care planning; opioids + benzodiazepines for end-stage breathlessness.

references.label: ESC HF Guidelines 2021 (updated 2023); ACC/AHA/HFSA HF 2022 + 2023; DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved + STEP-HFpEF trials
Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Primary aldosteronism — diagnosis + treatment
presentation: Most common identifiable cause of secondary hypertension (~5–10% of all hypertension, > 20% of resistant hypertension).
Hypertension (often resistant; severe young-onset) ± hypokalaemia (now recognised majority normokalaemic) ± metabolic alkalosis.
Adrenal adenoma (Conn syndrome — ~30%) OR bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (~60%) OR familial / unilateral hyperplasia / aldosterone-producing carcinoma.
Long-term consequences: accelerated cardiovascular events (stroke, MI, AF, HF) + CKD + cognitive decline + DM — compared to essential hypertension.
redFlags: Familial cases — younger / inherited / cascade screening.
Concurrent secondary causes (renal artery stenosis, Cushing) — workup more complex.

diagnostics.rationale: Identifies primary aldosteronism — elevated ARR + plasma aldosterone ≥ 15 ng/dL is suggestive. Stop interfering drugs (MRA, spironolactone — 6 weeks; ACEi/ARB — 4 weeks; beta-blocker, NSAID, diuretic — modify timing) before testing. Use cautiously if cannot stop.

diagnostics.test: Confirmatory testing: saline suppression test (aldosterone > 5–10 ng/dL after 2 L NaCl) OR captopril challenge OR fludrocortisone suppression OR oral salt loading.

diagnostics.rationale: Identify adenoma vs bilateral hyperplasia vs carcinoma (size + heterogeneity).

diagnostics.test: Adrenal vein sampling — gold standard for lateralisation BEFORE surgery in unilateral cases.
diagnostics.rationale: Determines unilateral vs bilateral disease — guides surgery.

diagnostics.test: Genetic testing for familial hyperaldosteronism (KCNJ5, glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism).
diagnostics.rationale: Selected cases — < 20 years onset, family history.

management.detail: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy — biochemical cure 95%; hypertension cure / improvement 70–90%. Pre-op: control BP + correct hypokalaemia + spironolactone × 4 weeks. Post-op: monitor K+ (can become hyperkalaemic transiently); ongoing antihypertensive often needed.

Spironolactone 12.5–100 mg daily (titrate to BP + K+; gynaecomastia + menstrual irregularity common). Eplerenone 25–100 mg daily — selective MRA, fewer side effects (sexual + menstrual) but more expensive + ~50% potency of spironolactone. Finerenone (non-steroidal selective MRA) emerging.
ACEi / ARB + CCB + thiazide as standard. Combine with MRA. BP target < 130/80.
Oral KCl until MRA achieves normalisation. Replace urgently if severe (< 2.5).
Low sodium diet; weight management; alcohol moderation; statin per CV risk; smoking cessation.
Annual BP + electrolytes + cardiovascular assessment + adrenal imaging surveillance for adenoma residuum / contralateral disease.
Cascade screening of first-degree relatives + genetic counselling.
Avoid spironolactone (anti-androgen effects on fetus). Methyldopa / labetalol / nifedipine; restrict salt; postpone surgery to postpartum; specialist obstetric + endocrine care.

references.label: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline on the Case Detection, Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Aldosteronism (2016); ESC Hypertension 2024
Kenya National Guidelines for Cardiovascular Diseases Management, Ministry of Health

title: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)
presentation: Autosomal dominant inheritance — PKD1 (~85%, more severe) + PKD2 (~15%, milder, later onset). 50% of offspring affected.
Renal: cysts in kidneys (bilateral progression); flank pain, recurrent cyst infection / haemorrhage, urinary stones, hypertension (young-onset), progression to ESRD (median age 58 — PKD1; 79 — PKD2).

Extra-renal: hepatic cysts (asymptomatic to massive), pancreatic + splenic cysts (rare); intracranial aneurysms (10–12%, higher with family history of SAH); mitral valve prolapse; abdominal hernia; diverticulosis.
Diagnosis criteria (modified Ravine): age-dependent number of bilateral renal cysts + family history; genetic testing for atypical / sporadic.
redFlags: Acute severe flank pain — cyst haemorrhage or infection or stone or rarely cyst rupture.
New / severe headache — exclude intracranial aneurysm + SAH.
Hypertension young-onset (< 40 years) — often first manifestation.
Large polycystic liver causing symptomatic mass effect.

diagnostics.test: MRI for total kidney volume (TKV) calculation — disease progression marker.
diagnostics.rationale: Risk stratification + tolvaptan eligibility (Mayo Clinic imaging classification 1C–1E or PROPKD ≥ 6).

diagnostics.test: Genetic testing for: atypical presentation, sporadic, pre-implantation genetic diagnosis.
MR angiography intracranial — for screening in family history of SAH / aneurysm / occupational (e.g. pilot) / pre-major surgery / on tolvaptan / smokers.
Annual BP, urinalysis, creatinine + eGFR + UACR.

management.detail: ACEi / ARB first-line — target < 130/80 (HALT-PKD trial — lower target slows TKV growth in young adults). Combine with thiazide / CCB as needed. AVOID over-diuresis (cyst growth).

Vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist; 60 mg + 30 mg (titrate to 90 + 30) daily. Indicated for rapidly progressive ADPKD (Mayo class 1C–1E, PROPKD ≥ 6, eGFR > 30). Major side effects: polyuria (mandatory) + hepatotoxicity (LFT monthly × 18 months then 3-monthly; STOP if elevation). REPRISE + TEMPO trials demonstrated slowing of eGFR decline.
Adequate hydration (3–4 L/day — suppresses vasopressin). Low sodium diet. Caffeine moderation. Avoid NSAID (cyst haemorrhage + nephrotoxicity). Smoking cessation. Maintain healthy weight.
Paracetamol + opioid (cautious). Avoid NSAID. Cyst aspiration / sclerotherapy / surgical decortication for refractory severe pain. Nerve block.
Lipophilic antibiotics (ciprofloxacin, fluconazole, doxycycline) — penetrate cysts; 4–6 weeks. Drain if refractory. Distinguish from pyelonephritis.
More common in ADPKD; lithotripsy / ureteroscopy + dietary modification + hydration.
Screening every 5–10 years in high-risk (family history of SAH / smokers / pre-op / on tolvaptan). Coiling / clipping for > 7 mm / symptomatic / growing.
Conservative for most. Symptomatic large cyst: sclerotherapy, fenestration, segmental resection. Severe: liver transplant (rarely simultaneous with kidney).
Dialysis (PD acceptable despite intra-abdominal cysts) OR transplantation (preferred — often after native kidney removal for space / nephrectomy for refractory pain or infection).

Pre-conception counselling — 50% offspring; consider pre-implantation genetic diagnosis. Pregnancy increases pre-eclampsia + UTI risk. Stop tolvaptan + ACEi/ARB in pregnancy; manage BP with methyldopa / labetalol / nifedipine.
Cascade testing of first-degree relatives; pre-conception planning; offer pre-implantation genetic diagnosis for affected couples wanting unaffected child.

references.label: KDIGO Controversies Conference on ADPKD; HALT-PKD + TEMPO + REPRISE trials

title: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia — diagnosis + targeted therapy
presentation: Most common adult leukaemia — often asymptomatic; incidental lymphocytosis on FBC.
Symptomatic: fatigue, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, recurrent infection (hypogammaglobulinaemia), autoimmune cytopenia (AIHA, ITP), B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss).
Risk-stratified by genetics: TP53 mutation / del(17p), IGHV mutation status, complex karyotype, NOTCH1, SF3B1.
Increased risk: second malignancy, especially skin (annual surveillance), infection.
redFlags: Richter transformation (rapid lymph node growth + B-symptoms + extranodal disease) — biopsy mandatory.
Tumour lysis syndrome with first dose of venetoclax — high-risk patients.

diagnostics.test: FBC + blood film (mature lymphocytes + smudge cells) + flow cytometry (CD5+ + CD19+ + CD23+ + kappa or lambda restriction).
Bone marrow biopsy (selected — staging + cytopenia workup).
diagnostics.rationale: Helps when blood film inconclusive + assesses marrow involvement.

diagnostics.test: FISH for del(17p) + del(11q) + trisomy 12 + del(13q); TP53 + IGHV + NOTCH1 + SF3B1 mutation.
diagnostics.rationale: Risk-stratification + treatment selection — TP53 / del(17p) need targeted therapy.

diagnostics.test: Serum immunoglobulins + DAT (Coombs) + reticulocytes + LDH + haptoglobin.
CT chest + abdomen + pelvis for staging in symptomatic.
Hepatitis B + C + HIV screen pre-treatment.

management.detail: Most patients do NOT need treatment at diagnosis — RAI 0–II / Binet A asymptomatic disease can be observed for years. iwCLL 2018 criteria for treatment initiation.

Progressive marrow failure (anaemia / thrombocytopenia); massive / progressive symptomatic splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy; rapidly progressive lymphocytosis (doubling < 6 months); autoimmune cytopenia poorly responsive to standard therapy; B-symptoms.

BTK inhibitor: acalabrutinib (BTK selective, lower cardiac toxicity than ibrutinib), zanubrutinib, ibrutinib — continuous indefinite therapy. OR venetoclax (BCL2 inhibitor) + obinutuzumab (anti-CD20) — fixed duration 12 months (CLL14, CLL13 — superior PFS, undetectable MRD).

Venetoclax-based OR BTK inhibitor — only options effective (chemoimmunotherapy ineffective). Lifelong BTK inhibitor OR fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab; consider allogeneic stem cell transplant in fit selected.
FCR (fludarabine + cyclophosphamide + rituximab) for fit IGHV-mutated only (no role in TP53-mutated); reserved for resource-limited / specific scenarios. Bendamustine + rituximab for older.

5-week dose ramp-up (20 mg → 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 mg/day) with aggressive TLS prophylaxis (rasburicase or allopurinol, hyperhydration, K+/phosphate/Ca monitoring); inpatient initiation for high TLS risk.

Vaccinations pre-treatment: pneumococcal + flu + COVID + zoster RZV. Aciclovir + co-trimoxazole prophylaxis on chemoimmunotherapy / BTK inhibitor. IVIG for recurrent infections + severe hypogammaglobulinaemia (IgG < 4). Erythropoietin if symptomatic anaemia.
AIHA: prednisolone 1 mg/kg + rituximab; severe — IVIG / splenectomy. ITP: prednisolone + rituximab + thrombopoietin-receptor agonist.
Biopsy mandatory — DLBCL most common; R-CHOP ± targeted; allogeneic SCT for fit; outcomes worse than de novo DLBCL.
Annual dermatology + skin self-exam (BCC + SCC + melanoma elevated); age-appropriate cancer screening; CT surveillance per disease + treatment.

references.label: iwCLL Guidelines 2018; ESMO + NCCN CLL Guidelines; CLL14 + CLL13 + ELEVATE-TN + ALLIANCE trials
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Chronic myeloid leukaemia — BCR-ABL TKI management
presentation: Chronic phase (90% at diagnosis): often asymptomatic; raised WBC (often very high) + left-shifted myeloid maturation + basophilia + splenomegaly.
Accelerated / blast phase: rapid progression — anaemia, thrombocytopenia, basophilia, new chromosomal abnormalities, splenomegaly, B-symptoms.
Defined by Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) — BCR-ABL1 fusion gene + tyrosine kinase activity.
TKI revolutionised: median survival now > 20 years; many achieve treatment-free remission.
redFlags: Accelerated / blast crisis at presentation — urgent.
T315I mutation — resistant to most TKIs.
TKI-related complications: pleural effusion (dasatinib), arterial events (nilotinib, ponatinib).

diagnostics.test: FBC + blood film + bone marrow aspirate + biopsy + cytogenetics (Philadelphia chromosome).
BCR-ABL1 fusion confirmation by FISH + quantitative PCR (international standard — IS).
ABL kinase domain mutation analysis if resistant disease (e.g. T315I).
Baseline: BP, ECG (QTc), lipids, glucose, ophthalmology, dermatology + dental for nilotinib + ponatinib.

management.detail: Imatinib 400 mg daily (lowest cost; longest experience; generic; less efficacious than 2nd-gen) OR dasatinib 100 mg daily (faster MMR; pleural effusion + pulmonary HT) OR nilotinib 300 mg BD (faster MMR; cardiovascular events + hyperglycaemia) OR bosutinib 400 mg daily (gastrointestinal). Risk-adapt by ELTS score + comorbidities.
Baseline + 3 + 6 + 12 months then every 3 months until major molecular response (MMR = BCR-ABL ≤ 0.1% IS); then every 6 months. Targets: MR^3 (MMR) by 12 months; deeper MR^4 + MR^4.5 over time.

Resistance — check adherence first; ABL kinase mutation analysis; switch to alternate-generation TKI. T315I — ponatinib OR asciminib (allosteric inhibitor) OR olverembatinib. Allogeneic stem cell transplant for multi-TKI-resistant / blast crisis.
Allosteric inhibitor of BCR-ABL; effective even in T315I (at higher dose 200 mg BD); better tolerated than ATP-competitive TKIs. Increasing first-line consideration.
TKI + chemotherapy (AML-like for myeloid blast; ALL-like for lymphoid blast) → allogeneic stem cell transplant if responding + fit + donor available. Prognosis remains poor.
Eligibility: chronic phase only, MR^4 + sustained ≥ 2 years on TKI ≥ 5 years. Monitor closely after stopping; 40–50% maintain TFR; restart TKI if loss of MMR.

Imatinib: oedema, GI, muscle cramps, hepatic — supportive. Dasatinib: pleural effusion (diuretic + steroid + hold), pulmonary HT (irreversible — discontinue), GI bleed. Nilotinib: hyperglycaemia, peripheral arterial disease, pancreatitis, QTc prolongation. Ponatinib: cardiovascular events (highest), hypertension. Hepatic + cardiac monitoring.

TKIs are teratogenic. Achieve stable MMR for ≥ 2 years before considering pregnancy; stop TKI before conception (some restart trimester 2 with interferon as bridge); restart TKI postpartum (no breastfeeding on TKI). Sperm banking for men; fertility-preservation discussions.
Routine vaccinations safe on TKI; avoid live in immunocompromised. Aciclovir / antifungal prophylaxis selectively.

references.label: ELN Recommendations for Treatment of CML (2020); ESMO + NCCN CML Guidelines
Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Sarcoidosis — diagnosis + multisystem management
presentation: Multisystem granulomatous disease of unknown aetiology — non-caseating granulomas.
Pulmonary (90%): bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy + reticulonodular infiltrates; cough + dyspnoea.
Lofgren syndrome (acute): erythema nodosum + bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy + arthralgia + fever — usually self-limiting + excellent prognosis.

Extra-pulmonary: skin (erythema nodosum, lupus pernio, papules), uveitis (often anterior), cardiac (conduction block, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, cardiomyopathy), neurosarcoidosis (cranial nerve palsy, meningitis, intracranial mass, peripheral neuropathy), hepatic + splenic granulomas, hypercalcaemia (vitamin D activation), kidneys, parotid (Heerfordt syndrome).
Risk: female, age 20–40, Black > White, family history.
