title: Age-related macular degeneration — anti-VEGF era
population: Leading cause of irreversible vision loss in elderly developed countries; SSA: less prevalent but rising with ageing. Age > 50, smoking, family history, fair skin, hypertension, oxidative stress.
presentation: Gradual central vision loss + distortion (metamorphopsia — straight lines appear wavy on Amsler grid). Dry AMD (90%): drusen + RPE changes; slow progression to geographic atrophy. Wet (neovascular) AMD (10%): choroidal neovascularisation + sudden vision distortion / loss; rapidly progressive.
redFlags: SUDDEN central vision loss / new distortion — wet AMD until proven otherwise — URGENT ophthalmology (anti-VEGF works best early)
Hereditary macular dystrophy (younger onset, family history) — different management; genetic counselling
Central serous chorioretinopathy (younger, often male, steroid-related)
Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (more common Asian / African ancestry)
diagnostics: Visual acuity + Amsler grid
Slit-lamp + dilated fundoscopy — drusen + RPE changes (dry) + haemorrhage + exudate (wet)
OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY (OCT) — gold standard for diagnosis + monitoring (subretinal fluid, intraretinal fluid, pigment epithelial detachment in wet AMD)
OCT-ANGIOGRAPHY — non-invasive visualisation of choroidal neovascularisation
Fluorescein angiography (classic) — leakage from CNV
Indocyanine green (ICG) angiography — polypoidal CV (more common SSA/Asian)
Macular pigment optical density (MPOD) — supplementation guidance
Genetic testing for advanced AMD risk (ARMS2, CFH)
management: DRY AMD:
No anti-VEGF benefit (different pathology)

AREDS2 supplements (vitamin C 500 mg + vitamin E 400 IU + lutein 10 mg + zeaxanthin 2 mg + zinc 80 mg + copper 2 mg) — reduce progression of intermediate-advanced dry AMD by 25% (AREDS + AREDS2 trials)
No β-carotene (lung cancer risk in smokers — replaced with lutein/zeaxanthin in AREDS2)
Smoking cessation (single most modifiable RF)
Healthy diet (Mediterranean, fish, leafy greens)
UV protection
PEGCETACOPLAN (Syfovre, FDA 2023) + AVACINCAPTAD PEGOL (Izervay, FDA 2023) — anti-C3/C5 complement inhibitors — first treatments for GEOGRAPHIC ATROPHY (advanced dry AMD); slow progression
Cataract surgery if coexisting (improves vision; no AMD worsening)
Low-vision rehabilitation
WET (NEOVASCULAR) AMD — anti-VEGF revolutionised management:
Intravitreal anti-VEGF — FIRST-LINE:
RANIBIZUMAB (Lucentis) — monthly or PRN/treat-and-extend
AFLIBERCEPT (Eylea) — every 8 weeks after loading; or treat-and-extend; higher-dose 8 mg every 12-16 weeks (PHOTON / PULSAR — newer)
BEVACIZUMAB (Avastin) — off-label, much cheaper, equivalent in CATT + IVAN trials; widely used SSA + low-cost settings
FARICIMAB (Vabysmo, FDA 2022) — anti-VEGF + anti-Ang2; longer durability (TENAYA + LUCERNE)
BROLUCIZUMAB (Beovu) — small molecule; intraocular inflammation concerns
Loading 3 monthly injections then maintenance
Monitoring with OCT every visit
Treat-and-extend protocol (extend interval by 2 weeks if dry)
Port Delivery System (PDS — SUSVIMO) — refillable ranibizumab implant
Photodynamic therapy (verteporfin) — selected (PCV)
Laser photocoagulation (rarely used now)
ADJUNCTS:
Visual rehabilitation + low-vision aids (magnifiers, lighting, reading aids)
Audiobooks + assistive technology
Address depression (visual loss + social isolation common)
Driving + occupational counselling
POLYPOIDAL CHOROIDAL VASCULOPATHY (PCV) — common SSA + Asian ancestry:
Anti-VEGF + ICG-guided photodynamic therapy
Aflibercept + faricimab effective monotherapy
FOLLOW-UP:
Wet AMD: every 4-8 weeks (treat-and-extend)
Dry intermediate-advanced: every 6-12 months
Self-monitoring with Amsler grid (alert for new distortion)
Annual visual acuity
Fellow eye risk (50% at 5 years)
POPULATION + SSA:
Less common but emerging burden
Bevacizumab access via WHO + advocacy (Lucentis vs Avastin equivalence — CATT + IVAN)
Smoking cessation public health
Mediterranean diet + AREDS2 supplements where affordable
Ophthalmology + retina specialist access expanding
Kenya National Eye Health Plan + IAPB World Report on Vision

OAKS + DERBY pegcetacoplan + Izervay avacincaptad geographic atrophy

title: Retinal detachment — sudden vision loss emergency
population: Sight-threatening emergency. RF: myopia (especially high > -6.0 D), age > 50, lens surgery, trauma, family history, lattice degeneration, vitreoretinal disease.
presentation: Sudden onset photopsia (flashes — vitreoretinal traction) + floaters (vitreous haemorrhage / pigment / collagen) + curtain / shadow ascending across visual field + central vision loss when macula involves. Rhegmatogenous (most common — break in retina), tractional (DM, retinopathy of prematurity, sickle cell), exudative (serous — VKH, choroidal mass, malignant HT, eclampsia).
redFlags: MACULA-ON detachment — VISION-PRESERVING — URGENT surgery (within 24h ideal)
MACULA-OFF detachment > 7 days — vision recovery limited even with successful re-attachment
Acute posterior vitreous detachment with retinal tear — laser photocoagulation prophylaxis prevents progression
Suspected ocular trauma + retinal detachment — full trauma workup
Suspected choroidal mass causing exudative (melanoma) — ocular oncology
diagnostics: Urgent OPHTHALMOLOGY referral SAME DAY
Visual acuity
Slit-lamp + DILATED FUNDOSCOPY — bullous elevation of retina + visible breaks (rhegmatogenous)
Indirect ophthalmoscopy + scleral indentation (specialist)
B-scan ULTRASOUND if dense vitreous haemorrhage prevents fundus view
OCT macula (macula on vs off)
Fluorescein angiography (selected — rule out exudative)

Differential diagnosis: vitreous haemorrhage alone, posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) without retinal break, central retinal artery / vein occlusion, retinal migraine, neuro-ophthalmic, occipital stroke
management: PRE-OPERATIVE:
Strict bed rest with positioning (head dependent for inferior detachment, etc.)
Avoid Valsalva + bending + heavy lifting
Antiemetic if nausea (avoid Valsalva from vomiting)
Same-day surgical evaluation
SURGICAL OPTIONS:
LASER RETINOPEXY / CRYOPEXY — for retinal break / tear / hole without detachment (prophylactic) — in-office quick
PNEUMATIC RETINOPEXY — gas bubble injection + laser/cryo; selected (single superior break, fresh detachment)
SCLERAL BUCKLE — silicone band sutured to sclera, indents wall to relieve traction; classic technique; useful in young / phakic patients
PARS PLANA VITRECTOMY (PPV) — removes vitreous + laser + gas / oil tamponade; most modern + versatile; combine with cataract surgery (phacovitrectomy) in older patients
Combined PPV + scleral buckle for complex
Re-detachment management with redo surgery or silicone oil
POST-OPERATIVE:
Strict positioning (face-down or specific) for 7-14 days for gas/oil tamponade
Avoid air travel + altitude with intraocular gas (expansion → high IOP)
Topical antibiotic + steroid drops
Activity restrictions
Review at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month
VISUAL OUTCOMES:
Macula-on detachment: > 90% retain near-normal vision with prompt surgery
Macula-off detachment: visual recovery limited (50% achieve 6/12 at best, < 10% to 6/6); time-dependent
Re-detachment rate 5-15%; second procedure usually successful
PROPHYLAXIS:
Acute symptomatic PVD with retinal tear → laser photocoagulation prevents progression to detachment
High-risk asymptomatic lattice / breaks — selective laser
TRACTIONAL DETACHMENT (DM-PDR, ROP, sickle cell):
Vitrectomy + membrane peeling + anti-VEGF + laser
Address underlying disease
EXUDATIVE / SEROUS DETACHMENT:
Treat underlying (VKH steroid; choroidal mass; malignant HTN; eclampsia)
Often resolves with cause treatment
POPULATION + SSA:
Major vision-threatening emergency
Limited vitreoretinal surgery access
Train + scale-up ophthalmic services
Awareness of warning symptoms (flashes/floaters/curtain) + immediate referral
Kenya — KNH + Lions SightFirst + regional centres
Sickle cell retinopathy / proliferative DR access

title: Hearing loss — newborn screening + age-related + sudden + ototoxic
population: WHO 2024: > 1.5 billion globally with hearing loss; 466 million disabling. Major contributor to dementia (Lancet Commission 2024 — leading modifiable RF). SSA: underdiagnosed; congenital + childhood + age-related + ototoxic.
presentation: Subtle vs sudden. Categories: conductive (CHL — outer/middle ear), sensorineural (SNHL — cochlea/nerve), mixed. Onset (sudden = SSNHL = emergency vs chronic). Bilateral vs unilateral. Symptoms — difficulty understanding speech, increased volume, tinnitus, vertigo, otalgia, otorrhoea.
redFlags: SUDDEN sensorineural hearing loss (within 72h) — EMERGENCY (steroid window — refer ENT urgent for audiogram + treatment within days)
Bilateral hearing loss in newborn / infant (not passed newborn screen) — urgent paediatric audiology + intervention
Unilateral with vertigo + tinnitus — vestibular schwannoma; MRI
Recent ototoxic drug exposure (aminoglycoside, cisplatin, loop diuretic, NSAIDs) — review + audiogram
Hearing loss + facial nerve palsy / vertigo / Bell's palsy — herpes zoster oticus (Ramsay-Hunt) — acyclovir + steroid
Severe / profound bilateral — cochlear implant evaluation
Congenital infection (TORCH — CMV most common congenital SNHL cause; rubella, syphilis, toxo, herpes)
diagnostics: NEWBORN SCREENING — otoacoustic emissions (OAE) + automated auditory brainstem response (AABR) — universal in HIC; advocacy in SSA
Audiology evaluation:
Pure-tone audiometry (PTA) — air + bone conduction
Speech audiometry — speech reception threshold + word recognition
Tympanometry + acoustic reflexes
OAE + ABR for newborns / non-cooperative
WHO grading: mild (26-40 dB), moderate (41-55), moderately severe (56-70), severe (71-90), profound (> 90)
Workup by type:
CHL: otoscopy (cerumen, infection, perforation, otitis media with effusion), Weber + Rinne tuning fork tests
SNHL: audiogram pattern + age + history; consider MRI internal auditory meatus for unilateral SNHL or asymmetric (vestibular schwannoma)
Genetic testing for congenital SNHL (GJB2 connexin 26)
TORCH screen for congenital infection
Ototoxic drug review (aminoglycoside, cisplatin, loop diuretic at high dose, NSAIDs chronic, aspirin overdose, vancomycin, erythromycin)
Comorbidity: cardiovascular, diabetes, smoking, OSA
management: CONGENITAL / NEWBORN SCREENING POSITIVE:
Confirmatory audiology within 1 month
Intervention by 6 months (1-3-6 rule — screen by 1 month, diagnose by 3 months, intervene by 6 months) — best language + cognitive outcomes
Hearing aids early
Cochlear implant evaluation if severe-profound bilateral
Early sign language (Kenya Sign Language) + early intervention services
Address aetiology (CMV — ganciclovir / valganciclovir for symptomatic CMV — improves hearing outcomes; Standard 6-month course)
AGE-RELATED HEARING LOSS (presbycusis):
HEARING AIDS — single most effective intervention
Bilateral fitting preferred
Digital + behind-the-ear / in-ear / receiver-in-canal
Bluetooth + smartphone integration
Audiology fitting + counselling + follow-up
Over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids — newer (FDA 2022) for mild-moderate; lower cost
HEARING AIDS REDUCE DEMENTIA RISK (Lancet Commission 2024 — 8% reduction; ACHIEVE trial 2023 — 48% reduction in cognitive decline over 3 years in high-risk older adults)
Address concomitant tinnitus (separate)
Assistive listening devices (TV streamers, telephone amplifiers)
Captioning + speech-reading lessons
Family + caregiver education on communication
SUDDEN SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS (SSNHL):
EMERGENCY — refer ENT within 1-2 weeks for best outcome
HIGH-DOSE ORAL CORTICOSTEROID: prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day × 7-14 days, taper
INTRATYMPANIC STEROID (dexamethasone) — alternative or salvage; injection in office
MRI internal auditory meatus to rule out retrocochlear pathology
Hyperbaric oxygen — limited evidence
Anti-viral acyclovir (for suspected viral — limited evidence)
Audiogram follow-up at 2 + 6 months
~ 1/3 recover spontaneously, 1/3 partial, 1/3 permanent
CONDUCTIVE HEARING LOSS:
Cerumen impaction: drops + irrigation (avoid in perforated TM)
Otitis media with effusion (separate): observation; grommets if persistent + hearing loss > 25 dB > 3 mo
Tympanic membrane perforation: monitor; tympanoplasty for chronic
Otosclerosis: stapedectomy / hearing aid
Chronic suppurative otitis media: treat infection + surgery for chronic disease
OTOTOXICITY PREVENTION:
Minimise aminoglycoside duration + dose (use shortest course + once-daily where appropriate)
Audiogram baseline + serial in patients on aminoglycoside / cisplatin / vancomycin > 5-7 days
Patient education on early symptoms (high-frequency loss first; tinnitus warning)
Genetic testing for aminoglycoside hypersensitivity (m.1555A>G — common cause familial deafness in Kenya / SSA + Asia)
Avoid concurrent ototoxics where possible
RAMSAY-HUNT SYNDROME (herpes zoster oticus):
Acyclovir / valacyclovir + prednisolone × 7-14 days
Eye care + facial nerve protection
Audiology + ENT + neurology
COCHLEAR IMPLANT:
Severe-profound bilateral SNHL not adequately benefiting from hearing aids
Adult + paediatric criteria
Comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation
Audiologic + speech-language + psychological + surgical
Post-implant rehabilitation critical
TINNITUS (often coexists):
Identify aetiology (hearing loss, vascular, structural)
CBT, tinnitus retraining therapy, sound therapy
Hearing aid (often improves tinnitus)
Treat depression
POPULATION + SSA:
WHO World Hearing Report 2021
Universal newborn screening rollout
Affordable hearing aid access (WHO Preferred Product Profile)
Address barriers (cost, stigma, distance, training)
Train ear care + audiology + ENT + surgical hearing implant
Address ototoxic drug use (aminoglycoside, cisplatin) — judicious
Kenya National Eye + Hearing Health Plan
Sound-Hearing Africa (advocacy)

ACHIEVE JAMA Internal Medicine 2023 (hearing aid + cognitive decline reduction)

title: Uveitis — anterior + posterior + masquerade workup
population: Anterior uveitis most common (75%) — HLA-B27 associated 50%, idiopathic 30%; posterior + intermediate + panuveitis less common but vision-threatening. SSA: infectious causes prominent (TB, syphilis, toxoplasmosis, HIV, herpes).
presentation: Anterior: red painful eye + photophobia + decreased vision + circumcorneal redness + small irregular pupil + keratic precipitates + cells + flare in anterior chamber. Posterior: floaters + decreased vision + retinal/choroidal infiltrates + vitritis + macular oedema; less pain. Intermediate: vitreous cells + 'snowbanks' + macular oedema.
redFlags: Suspected infectious cause (TB, syphilis, toxoplasmosis, herpes, HIV-related) — DO NOT treat with steroid alone — empirical anti-infective if high suspicion + workup
Hypopyon (white cells in anterior chamber level) — severe uveitis OR endophthalmitis
Behcet's disease (Asian / Mediterranean / Turkish; oral + genital ulcers + uveitis + erythema nodosum) — needs systemic immunomodulation
Sympathetic ophthalmia (post-trauma / surgery in other eye — bilateral granulomatous uveitis)
VKH syndrome (Asian + dark-skinned; meningoencephalitis features + skin/hair depigmentation + uveitis)
Masquerade syndrome (lymphoma, leukaemia, retinitis pigmentosa, retinoblastoma in children)
diagnostics: Slit-lamp — anterior chamber cells + flare + KPs + iris nodules + posterior synechiae
Visual acuity + IOP + dilated fundoscopy
OCT macula (oedema), OCT-A, fluorescein/ICG angiography for posterior
Workup by clinical features + systemic associations:
HLA-B27 + spondyloarthropathy + IBD + psoriasis (anterior recurrent)
ACE + chest X-ray + CT (sarcoidosis)
ANA, ANCA, RF, CCP (autoimmune)
TB IGRA + chest X-ray (essential SSA + endemic)
RPR/VDRL + TPPA (syphilis — always test in any uveitis — 'the great mimic')
HIV testing
Toxoplasma serology + PCR vitreous (focal posterior chorioretinitis)
HSV / VZV / CMV PCR vitreous (selected)
Lyme (where endemic)
Bartonella (cat-scratch)
Aqueous / vitreous sampling for PCR + cytology + culture (selected severe + atypical)
management: ANTERIOR UVEITIS:
TOPICAL STEROID — prednisolone acetate 1% — frequent dosing (every 1-2 hours initially, taper over weeks)
CYCLOPLEGIC — cyclopentolate 1% TID or homatropine — prevents synechiae + reduces ciliary muscle spasm pain
Treat cause (HLA-B27 anti-inflammatory if associated; infectious-specific if identified)
Topical NSAID adjunct (ketorolac, nepafenac, bromfenac)
IOP monitoring (steroid-induced glaucoma risk)
Follow-up 1-2 weeks then taper
INTERMEDIATE + POSTERIOR + PANUVEITIS:
Systemic CORTICOSTEROID (prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day starting, taper over months)
Periocular steroid injection (subtenon or intravitreal — depo-medrol, triamcinolone, dexamethasone implant Ozurdex)
Intravitreal fluocinolone (Iluvien, Retisert) — chronic non-infectious
Steroid-sparing IMMUNOMODULATORS:
Methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate — first-line steroid-sparing
Ciclosporin, tacrolimus — calcineurin inhibitors
ADALIMUMAB (anti-TNF) — first biologic FDA-approved for non-infectious posterior + intermediate + panuveitis (VISUAL-I + VISUAL-II trials)
Infliximab, tocilizumab (anti-IL-6)
Rituximab for refractory
INFECTIOUS UVEITIS — treat infection FIRST (steroid cautious + after anti-infective):
TB UVEITIS: 4-drug ATT × 6-9 months + steroid
SYPHILIS: aqueous penicillin G IV × 10-14 days + lumbar puncture (neurosyphilis features common)
TOXOPLASMA RETINOCHOROIDITIS: pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + folinic acid × 4-6 weeks + prednisolone for active vision-threatening; cotrimoxazole alternative; HIV — chronic suppression
HSV/VZV ANTERIOR (Posner-Schlossman, herpetic): valacyclovir 1 g TDS × 7-14 days; chronic suppression for recurrent
CMV RETINITIS (HIV/immunocompromised): ganciclovir IV + maintenance + intravitreal; valganciclovir oral; foscarnet alternative
TOXOCARA: albendazole + steroid for vision-threatening
ENDOPHTHALMITIS (intraocular bacterial / fungal infection — separate emergency): intravitreal antibiotics + vitrectomy
BEHCET'S DISEASE UVEITIS:
Often severe + recurrent
Adalimumab + infliximab
Corticosteroid + colchicine + AZA + ciclosporin + alemtuzumab (refractory)
Address mucocutaneous + vascular + GI features
VKH SYNDROME:
Aggressive systemic corticosteroid + immunosuppression early
Often bilateral + vision-threatening
SYMPATHETIC OPHTHALMIA:
Post-trauma / surgery — fellow eye involvement
Aggressive systemic immunosuppression
Consider enucleation of severely damaged eye if no vision (prevents sympathetic in fellow)
MASQUERADE SYNDROME:
Suspect chronic / atypical / unresponsive to steroid
Vitrectomy + cytology + flow cytometry
Imaging (MRI brain — CNS lymphoma)
Refer haematology / oncology
COMPLICATIONS:
Cataract (steroid + inflammation)
Glaucoma (inflammation + steroid)
Cystoid macular oedema
Posterior synechiae
Band keratopathy
Hypotony
Vision loss
Phthisis bulbi end-stage
POPULATION + SSA:
TB + syphilis + HIV + toxoplasmosis common causes — workup essential
HIV + opportunistic infection (CMV) considerations
Access to ophthalmology + biologic limited
Train + scale-up uveitis specialists

title: Systemic lupus erythematosus — EULAR 2024 modern algorithm
population: Female predominance 9:1; peak 15-44 yr; African + Asian + Hispanic ancestry — higher prevalence + earlier onset + more severe (lupus nephritis, neuropsychiatric).
presentation: Multi-system: fatigue + malar rash + photosensitivity + oral ulcers + arthritis + serositis + nephritis + neuropsych + cytopenias + Raynaud's. Highly variable. Flares + remissions.
redFlags: Lupus nephritis (proteinuria/haematuria) — biopsy + class III/IV/V triple-therapy
Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) — fever + cytopenias + ferritin > 10,000
Pregnancy + high-risk antibodies (anti-Ro/La, lupus anticoagulant) — congenital heart block
diagnostics: ACR/EULAR 2019 classification (ANA + ≥ 10 points domains)
ANA + anti-dsDNA + anti-Sm + anti-Ro/La + complement C3/C4 + APL antibodies (LA + aCL + anti-β2GP1)
FBC + UEC + LFT + urinalysis + UPCR/UACR + ESR/CRP (often ESR-CRP dissociation)
Lupus nephritis suspected — renal biopsy ESSENTIAL (Class I-VI ISN/RPS 2018)
NPSLE — MRI brain + LP if indicated
Echocardiogram if serositis or APL
Disease activity: SLEDAI-2K or BILAG; damage: SDI
management: EULAR 2024 (Lancet Rheumatol) + ACR 2024:
FOUNDATIONS for everyone:
HYDROXYCHLOROQUINE 5 mg/kg/d (max 400 mg) — disease activity, flare prevention, cardiovascular, mortality benefit; annual eye exam (retinal toxicity)
Sun protection + smoking cessation + vitamin D + cardiovascular RF management
Vaccines (live contraindicated on immunosuppression — pneumococcal + influenza + COVID + HPV + zoster recombinant)
TARGET: Lupus Low Disease Activity State (LLDAS) → REMISSION on minimal pred (≤ 5 mg)
MILD-MODERATE FLARE (skin/joints):
Optimise HCQ + topical steroid + NSAID short course + low-dose pred 5-10 mg
Steroid-sparing: methotrexate 15-25 mg/wk + folic acid
Biologic: BELIMUMAB (BLISS trials) IV/SC for refractory + skin/joint disease
MODERATE-SEVERE (no organ-threat):
Pred 0.5 mg/kg/d short course + taper to ≤ 5 mg
Azathioprine 2-2.5 mg/kg or MMF 2-3 g/d
BELIMUMAB add-on; ANIFROLUMAB (Saphnelo) anti-IFN-α refractory skin + joints
LUPUS NEPHRITIS class III/IV/V (organ-threatening):
Induction: MMF 2-3 g/d OR cyclophosphamide (Euro-lupus 500 mg q2wk × 6) + steroid (PRED 0.5 mg/kg/d short — Belimumab BLISS-LN add-on + voclosporin AURORA)
TRIPLE THERAPY: MMF/CYC + steroid + BELIMUMAB or VOCLOSPORIN (AURORA-1/2 — first oral CNI approved for LN)
Maintenance: MMF (1-2 g/d) or AZA × 3-5 yr
Refractory: rituximab (off-label) or anifrolumab; CAR-T cells emerging (Mougiakakos NEJM 2021 + Lancet 2024 — small trials of CD19 CAR-T promising remission)
ACE-i/ARB + BP target < 130/80 + cardiovascular RF
NEUROPSYCHIATRIC SLE: high-dose steroid + cyclophosphamide; rituximab
PREGNANCY:
HCQ throughout pregnancy + low-dose aspirin from week 12 (pre-eclampsia)
Plan conception during 6-12 mo remission
Anti-Ro+/La+ — monitor fetal echo wk 16-26 (congenital heart block)
APS+ + lupus — therapeutic anticoagulation + LMWH; pre-eclampsia surveillance
Stop teratogenic: MMF/MTX/CYC pre-conception; AZA + tacrolimus + ciclosporin pregnancy-compatible
ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID SYNDROME co-existence:
Lifelong warfarin (INR 2-3) post-thrombosis; triple-positive higher target
Catastrophic APS — anticoagulation + steroid + IVIG + PLEX + rituximab + eculizumab
MAS: high-dose steroid + ciclosporin/anakinra; emapalumab
SSA: lupus more common + severe + LN; access to MMF + belimumab + rituximab limited — CYC still useful; advocate biosimilar access; train rheumatology + nephrology

references.label: EULAR 2024 Recommendations for SLE Lancet Rheumatology

title: Rheumatoid arthritis — treat-to-target with biologics and JAK inhibitors
population: Female 3:1; peak 40-60 yr; 1% population; smoking + HLA-DRB1 shared epitope + RF/anti-CCP increase risk.
presentation: Symmetric small-joint polyarthritis + morning stiffness > 30 min + MCP/PIP/wrist + extra-articular (nodules, ILD, vasculitis, scleritis, Sjögren). Damage early — window of opportunity within 12 wk.
redFlags: Septic arthritis on a chronic arthritis — joint aspiration
diagnostics: ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria — joint count + serology + APR + duration ≥ 6 wk; ≥ 6 = definite RA
Rheumatoid factor (RF) + ANTI-CCP (more specific) + ESR + CRP + FBC + UEC + LFT
Hand + foot X-rays baseline + 1 yr (erosions, JSN); MSK ultrasound (synovitis, erosions); MRI early disease
Pre-biologic screen: TB (IGRA + CXR), HBV/HCV, HIV, varicella IgG, JC virus if rituximab
Disease activity: DAS28-CRP or CDAI/SDAI; target ≤ 3.2 LDA / ≤ 2.6 remission
management: EULAR 2023 + ACR 2021 + NICE NG100:
EARLY treat-to-target — start csDMARD within weeks; review monthly; escalate if not at target by 3 mo
PHASE I — csDMARD ± short bridge steroid:
METHOTREXATE 15-25 mg/wk PO/SC + folic acid 5 mg/wk (DRUG OF CHOICE; SC if PO intolerant)
Sulfasalazine 2-3 g/d OR hydroxychloroquine OR leflunomide if MTX contraindicated/intolerant
Triple therapy (MTX + SSZ + HCQ) viable + cheap alternative to biologic (RACAT NEJM 2013)
Bridge steroid pred 7.5-10 mg/d × 3 mo TAPER (not chronic)
PHASE II — add biologic / JAKi (if not at target at 3-6 mo despite csDMARD):
TNF INHIBITOR first-line biologic: etanercept / adalimumab / infliximab / golimumab / certolizumab; PRE-SCREEN TB + HBV; biosimilars cost-effective
ALTERNATIVE biologic: tocilizumab (IL-6R), abatacept (CTLA-4), rituximab (CD20 — refractory + RF/CCP+)
JAK INHIBITOR oral: tofacitinib / baricitinib / upadacitinib — BLACK BOX MACE + thromboembolism + cancer over TNFi if > 65 yr or smoker (ORAL Surveillance) — use after TNFi or in cautious patient
PHASE III — switch class if no response after 3 mo of biologic/JAKi
DOSE-TAPERING when in sustained remission > 6 mo (consider step-down, not stop)

FOUNDATIONS: smoking cessation + vaccination (pneumococcal + influenza + COVID + zoster recombinant; live contraindicated) + cardiovascular RF + bone health (DEXA + ca + vit D + bisphosphonate on steroid) + dental health + PT/OT
EXTRA-ARTICULAR:
RA-ILD: MTX continue (no clear harm); abatacept or rituximab if progressive; pirfenidone/nintedanib INBUILD progressive fibrosis
Vasculitis: cyclophosphamide or rituximab
Felty: G-CSF + MTX or rituximab
PREGNANCY:
STOP MTX + leflunomide pre-conception (washout); STOP JAKi pre-conception
Compatible: HCQ + SSZ + AZA + ciclosporin/tacrolimus + low-dose pred + certolizumab (minimal placental transfer) and other TNFi second/third trimester
Plan during low activity; close monitoring
SSA: csDMARD MTX widely available + cost-effective; biosimilar TNFi access advocacy; MSK ultrasound training; integrate primary care + rheumatology referral

title: ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA / MPA / EGPA) — induction + maintenance
population: Rare — 20/million; peak 65-74 yr; GPA / MPA / EGPA spectrum.
presentation: Multisystem: ENT (saddle nose, sinusitis, otitis), pulmonary (haemoptysis, pulmonary haemorrhage, ILD), renal (RPGN with crescentic GN), skin (purpura), neuro (mononeuritis multiplex). EGPA — asthma + eosinophilia + cardiomyopathy. Constitutional — fever + weight loss.
redFlags: RPGN — rising creatinine + active urine sediment — biopsy + treat WITHIN DAYS
Diffuse alveolar haemorrhage — haemoptysis + falling Hb + diffuse CXR — emergency PLEX + steroid + immunosuppression
diagnostics: ANCA: c-ANCA / PR3 (GPA); p-ANCA / MPO (MPA + EGPA); 10% ANCA-negative
FBC + UEC + LFT + urinalysis + UPCR + ESR + CRP + complement (usually normal) + cryo + Hep B/C + HIV + ANA + anti-GBM (overlap)
TISSUE BIOPSY for diagnosis — kidney (RPGN with pauci-immune crescentic GN), nasal/sinus, lung, nerve, skin
CT chest (nodules, ground-glass, cavities); CT sinus; nerve conduction studies
EGPA — IgE + eosinophil count + cardiac MRI; ANCA-positive 40% only
Disease activity: BVAS; damage: VDI
management: EULAR 2024 + ACR 2021 + KDIGO 2024:
INDUCTION (severe — organ-threatening):
RITUXIMAB 375 mg/m² × 4 wk OR 1 g × 2 doses (preferred — RAVE/RITUXVAS — non-inferior to CYC + better in relapses; safer fertility/cancer)
OR CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE pulse 15 mg/kg q2-3 wk (CYCLOPS) × 6-10 doses (cheaper, still used SSA)
+ PREDNISOLONE 1 mg/kg/d (max 60-80 mg) TAPER per PEXIVAS (low-dose pred steroid-sparing regimen — same efficacy + less infection NEJM 2020)
+ AVACOPAN (Tavneos — C5a receptor antagonist) ADVOCATE NEJM 2021 — steroid-sparing alternative
Plasma exchange — selective: anti-GBM/AAV overlap, severe pulmonary haemorrhage, severe creatinine > 500 + dialysis-requiring (PEXIVAS — no overall benefit; selective)
INDUCTION (limited / non-organ-threatening):
Methotrexate + pred (NORAM); or rituximab
MAINTENANCE (6-24 mo post-induction → 4 yr):
RITUXIMAB 500 mg q6mo × 4-5 yr (MAINRITSAN — superior to AZA)
OR azathioprine 2 mg/kg/d × 4 yr
Wean pred ≤ 5 mg
Stop maintenance + monitor for relapse
RELAPSE: rituximab + steroid pulse
EGPA-SPECIFIC: severe — same induction; MEPOLIZUMAB (anti-IL5) added — MIRRA NEJM 2017 — for relapsing/refractory + steroid-dependent (asthma component)
ANCILLARIES:
TB + HBV + HIV screen + treat latent before immunosuppression
PJP prophylaxis cotrimoxazole 480 mg TDS while on steroid > 20 mg + immunosuppressed
Vaccination (no live) — pneumococcal, influenza, COVID, zoster recombinant
Cardiovascular RF; bone health (steroid)
Fertility — sperm/ovum cryopreserve if CYC option
Cancer surveillance long-term (esp. bladder if cumulative CYC; UPDATED — pulse CYC + reduced cumulative dose lowers risk)
Trimethoprim/sulfa long-term considered in localised GPA (Stegeman NEJM 1996 — reduces relapse)
ANCA-GBM OVERLAP: triple therapy — PLEX + CYC/rituximab + steroid
SSA: limited access to rituximab — CYC backbone; train nephrology/rheumatology; biopsy capacity essential; biosimilar advocacy.

references.label: PEXIVAS plasma exchange + low-dose steroid NEJM 2020

title: Axial spondyloarthritis — NSAID + TNFi / IL-17i / JAKi for refractory
population: Male 3:1; onset < 45 yr; HLA-B27 + (90% AS).
presentation: Inflammatory back pain > 3 mo + morning stiffness + improves with activity + buttock pain + enthesitis + uveitis + IBD + psoriasis. Restricted spinal movement, reduced chest expansion.
redFlags: Spinal fracture even minor trauma (ankylosed spine — fragile)
diagnostics: ASAS criteria axial SpA: back pain + radiographic OR MRI sacroiliitis + ≥ 1 SpA feature
X-ray SI joints + lumbar; MRI SI joints (early sacroiliitis — bone marrow oedema)
HLA-B27 (supportive not diagnostic)
CRP / ESR (often raised); FBC + UEC
Eye exam if uveitis history; cardiac echo if conduction concerns
BASDAI / ASDAS-CRP disease activity
Screen IBD (calprotectin if symptoms); psoriasis exam
management: ASAS-EULAR 2022 + ACR 2019:
PHYSIOTHERAPY + EXERCISE backbone (postural + spine extension + aerobic) + smoking cessation
PHASE I — NSAID continuous (not PRN) — naproxen 500 mg BD or celecoxib 200 mg BD × 2-4 wk trial (continuous suppresses radiographic progression)
PHASE II — if persistent active disease (ASDAS ≥ 2.1 or BASDAI ≥ 4) despite 2 NSAID trials, START BIOLOGIC:
TNF INHIBITOR (etanercept / adalimumab / infliximab / golimumab / certolizumab) — pre-screen TB/HBV/HIV; biosimilars
IL-17 INHIBITOR alternative (secukinumab / ixekizumab / bimekizumab) — equally effective; avoid in IBD overlap (worsens)
PHASE III — switch class if no response 3-4 mo
PHASE IV — JAK INHIBITOR (upadacitinib SELECT-AXIS-1/2; tofacitinib) for refractory — BLACK BOX MACE/VTE/cancer per ORAL Surveillance
PERIPHERAL ARTHRITIS — sulfasalazine 2-3 g/d (no role in axial); enthesitis — local steroid injection (limited)
ANTERIOR UVEITIS — topical steroid + mydriatic; recurrent — adalimumab (better than secukinumab)
IBD overlap — TNFi monoclonal antibody (adalimumab/infliximab) — NOT etanercept (poor IBD), NOT IL-17
PSORIASIS overlap — IL-17 or TNFi; avoid in IBD overlap
CARDIAC (AR + conduction) — echo + ECG surveillance
OSTEOPOROSIS — DEXA + bisphosphonate (high fracture risk in ankylosed spine)
SPINE FRACTURE — even minor trauma — full spine imaging (MRI > CT); surgical referral if unstable / cord risk
Vaccine (no live) pneumococcal + influenza + COVID + zoster recombinant
Pregnancy: stop MTX/leflunomide; SSZ/HCQ OK; certolizumab safest TNFi (low placental transfer); other TNFi acceptable 1st-2nd trimester
SSA: NSAID + physio backbone affordable; biosimilar TNFi advocacy; integrate eye + spine + rheumatology

title: Gout — treat acute + lifelong ULT to target urate < 360 (or < 300 tophaceous)
population: Male predominance; > 2% adults; metabolic syndrome + CKD + thiazide + alcohol + purines + obesity + heart failure.
presentation: Acute monoarthritis (1st MTP — podagra, knee, ankle, midfoot) with severe pain + redness + swelling overnight; mimics septic arthritis. Tophi over time on ears, fingers, olecranon. Polyarticular flare possible.
redFlags: Septic arthritis — fever + raised WCC/CRP + joint aspirate culture; can co-exist
Tophaceous gout with erosive joint destruction
Severe SCAR — allopurinol DRESS (HLA-B*58:01 — Han Chinese, Korean, Thai — TEST before allopurinol in those populations + SSA emerging data)
diagnostics: Joint aspiration GOLD STANDARD — negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals on polarised microscopy
Serum urate (often normal during acute attack — repeat 2 wk after settles)
UEC + FBC + glucose + lipids + cardiovascular RF; renal US if stones
Dual-energy CT — sensitive for tophi if diagnosis uncertain
X-ray — erosive changes overhanging edges chronic
Exclude septic arthritis if any doubt — aspirate + Gram stain + culture
management: ACR 2020 + EULAR 2016 (update 2024) + BSR 2017:
ACUTE FLARE (start within 24h):
NSAID — naproxen 500 mg BD or indomethacin or diclofenac × 5-7 d (avoid in CKD, peptic ulcer, anticoag)
OR COLCHICINE 1 mg stat then 0.5 mg 1h later, then 0.5 mg BD-TDS × 3-5 d (renal dose-adjust + statin interaction + grapefruit + macrolide CYP3A4)
OR ORAL PREDNISOLONE 30-40 mg × 5 d (DM-friendly; HF caution; alternative if NSAID + colchicine contraindicated)
Intra-articular steroid (single joint) if injectable
IL-1 INHIBITOR canakinumab/anakinra refractory + multiple comorbidities (NSAID + colchicine + steroid all contraindicated)
Ice + rest + elevate
CONTINUE ULT if already on — DO NOT stop
URATE-LOWERING THERAPY (ULT) lifelong — START after first flare or per indications:
Indications: > 1 flare/yr, tophi, X-ray damage, CKD ≥ stage 2, urolithiasis
ALLOPURINOL FIRST-LINE — start 100 mg/d (50 mg/d if CKD) titrate every 2-4 wk up to 300-900 mg/d to TARGET urate < 360 μmol/L (< 6 mg/dL) — or < 300 if tophi
HLA-B*58:01 TEST before allopurinol in Han Chinese / Korean / Thai (allopurinol-DRESS); use febuxostat alternative
FEBUXOSTAT 2nd-line (80-120 mg/d) — cardiovascular caution post-CARES (NEJM 2018) but newer FAST trial (Lancet 2020) shows non-inferior
Uricosuric: probenecid (avoid in CKD or stones), benzbromarone, lesinurad (combined with XOI)
Pegloticase IV (refractory tophaceous gout — short-term)
PROPHYLAXIS during ULT initiation: colchicine 0.5 mg OD/BD (or low NSAID/pred) × 3-6 mo (flares paradoxically increase as urate mobilises tophi)
Continue ULT lifelong — do NOT stop after target reached
LIFESTYLE: reduce alcohol (esp. beer), reduce purines (offal/red meat/seafood), avoid fructose drinks, weight loss, hydration, dairy/coffee may reduce, treat metabolic syndrome
CARDIOVASCULAR + CKD RF management (gout + uric acid CV risk marker)
SWITCH THIAZIDE/loop to losartan/CCB (losartan mild uricosuric)
PSEUDOGOUT (CPPD) differential — positively birefringent rhomboid crystals; NSAID/colchicine/steroid
SSA: allopurinol widely available + cheap; education on lifelong ULT + adherence (perceived 'only when painful'); cardiovascular RF integrated.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions (Levels 4–6 Hospitals), Ministry of Health

title: Polymyalgia rheumatica + giant cell arteritis — steroid + tocilizumab for refractory/relapsing GCA
population: Age > 50 (peak 70s); female 2:1; northern European ancestry highest but global. PMR + GCA overlap (40-60% co-occur).
presentation: PMR — bilateral shoulder + hip-girdle pain + morning stiffness > 45 min + functional impairment + raised ESR/CRP + > 50 yr. GCA — new headache + jaw claudication + scalp tenderness + visual symptoms (amaurosis/diplopia) + temporal artery abnormal + constitutional. PMR symptoms in 40% GCA.
redFlags: VISION LOSS — GCA — IMMEDIATE high-dose IV steroid (delay = permanent)
Severe constitutional + atypical features — workup myeloma / cancer / infection
diagnostics: PMR — clinical + ESR/CRP raised + > 50 yr + ACR/EULAR 2012 criteria; exclude RA + myositis + thyroid + statin myopathy
GCA — temporal artery BIOPSY ≥ 1 cm length (gold standard but skip lesions); HALO SIGN on ultrasound (vascular imaging — TABUL/Hauser); MRI/CT/PET-CT large-vessel (aortitis)
Anti-CCP/RF + CK + TSH + protein electrophoresis + glucose + lipids + bone profile (steroid bone risk)
FBC + UEC + LFT baseline (steroid + tocilizumab monitoring)
Pre-tocilizumab: TB/HBV/HCV screen; lipids (raises); LFT baseline
management: BSR 2020 + ACR/VF 2021 + EULAR 2024:
PMR — prednisolone 12.5-25 mg/d × 2-4 wk → reduce by 2.5 mg/2-4 wk to 10 mg/d × 4-6 wk → reduce 1 mg/4-8 wk → off by 1-2 yr; relapse common — return to last effective dose + slower taper
PMR steroid-sparing — methotrexate 7.5-15 mg/wk for relapsing or steroid-dependent; tocilizumab if refractory (less evidence than GCA)
GCA — START HIGH-DOSE STEROID IMMEDIATELY on clinical suspicion (do NOT wait for biopsy):
No visual involvement: pred 40-60 mg/d × 4 wk then taper
Visual loss / threatened: METHYLPRED IV 500-1000 mg/d × 3 d THEN pred 60 mg/d (some delay biopsy 1-2 wk — still high yield)
Continue 12-24 mo taper based on response + ESR/CRP
Aspirin 75-100 mg/d (cerebrovascular protection) + PPI

TOCILIZUMAB 162 mg SC weekly (or 8 mg/kg IV q4 wk) — GiACTA NEJM 2017 — steroid-sparing in new-onset + relapsing GCA, reduces flares + cumulative steroid; SC available; relapse on tapering steroid → add tocilizumab
Alternative: methotrexate (modest steroid-sparing); abatacept under study
AVOID rapid steroid taper — high relapse
STEROID ADJUNCTS (long-term):
Bone — DEXA + calcium + vit D + bisphosphonate (alendronate 70 mg/wk) if FRAX > 10% major or age > 70
PJP prophylaxis cotrim if on > 20 mg pred + immunomodulator
GI — PPI cover
BP + glucose + lipids monitoring (steroid)
Vaccines (no live) — pneumococcal + influenza + COVID + zoster recombinant
AORTIC SURVEILLANCE — annual chest imaging GCA (LV-GCA + aneurysm risk)
BIOPSY-NEGATIVE / FAST-LANE: clinical suspicion + halo on US + response to steroid — treat as GCA
SSA: prednisolone + aspirin + bisphosphonate widely available + cheap; tocilizumab access advocacy; train rheumatology + vascular US.

title: Sickle cell disease — modern multimodal (HU + voxelotor + crizanlizumab + transplant + gene therapy)
population: Sub-Saharan Africa highest burden (300,000 births/yr; Nigeria + DRC + Ghana + Tanzania + Kenya); Mediterranean/Middle East; Indian; diaspora. Newborn screening rolled out — Kenya/Tanzania universal in select counties.
presentation: Vaso-occlusive painful crises (children + adults), acute chest syndrome, stroke, splenic sequestration (children), aplastic crisis (parvovirus B19), priapism, chronic haemolytic anaemia, pulmonary HTN, leg ulcers, AVN hip + shoulder, retinopathy, nephropathy, gallstones.
redFlags: Acute chest syndrome (CXR infiltrate + fever/respiratory/chest pain) — exchange transfusion + antibiotics + bronchodilator
Stroke / TIA — exchange transfusion + chronic transfusion / hydroxyurea
Splenic sequestration (rapid spleen enlargement + Hb drop) — children — transfuse + splenectomy after recurrent
diagnostics: Newborn screen (HPLC / IEF) — universal goal SSA + WHO World Sickle Cell Day
Hb electrophoresis / HPLC + DNA confirmation
FBC + reticulocyte + LDH + bilirubin + LFT + UEC + UPCR + vit D + ferritin + folate
Transcranial Doppler (TCD) — annual screen children 2-16 yr — > 200 cm/s = primary stroke risk — start chronic transfusion (STOP trial)
Annual review — echo (PHT), urinalysis (proteinuria), retinopathy screen, DEXA, dental
Vaccinations + functional asplenia precautions
Genetic counselling + family screening
management: BSH 2018/2021 + ASH 2020 + WHO + Kenya SCD guidelines:
FOUNDATIONS for ALL:
PENICILLIN PROPHYLAXIS to age 5 (pen V 125 mg BD < 3 yr, 250 mg BD 3-5 yr) — landmark — reduces pneumococcal sepsis 84% (PROPS NEJM 1986); continue longer if splenectomised
VACCINATIONS — pneumococcal (PCV13 + PPV23 boosters), Hib, meningococcal ACWY + B, influenza annual, COVID, hepatitis B, malaria where endemic
FOLIC ACID 5 mg/d lifelong (haemolysis)
HYDRATION + avoid extremes temperature + altitude + dehydration
Education + family + caregiver + crisis plan
MALARIA prophylaxis + bed nets (SSA — malaria devastating in SCD)
DISEASE-MODIFYING:

HYDROXYUREA (HU) — start AGE 9 mo per BABY-HUG (NEJM 2011); 20-35 mg/kg/d titrated; reduces VOC + ACS + transfusions + mortality (LaSHS); SSA — REACH NEJM 2019 proved safety + efficacy SSA + reduced malaria; UNIVERSAL OFFER — Kenya / Tanzania scaling — landmark accessible therapy
L-GLUTAMINE 5-15 g BD (Endari FDA 2017) — reduces VOC; access limited
VOXELOTOR (Oxbryta) 1500 mg/d — HOPE NEJM 2019 — increases Hb + reduces haemolysis (FDA 2019; withdrawn 2024 worldwide due to adverse events — RE-EVALUATING — check current guidance)
CRIZANLIZUMAB (Adakveo) anti-P-selectin 5 mg/kg IV monthly — SUSTAIN NEJM 2017 — reduces VOC; status under review after STAND results (mixed)
Chronic transfusion programme (with chelation — deferasirox/deferoxamine) for stroke / abnormal TCD / recurrent ACS / severe disease
ACUTE VOC:
Pain — opioid PCA (morphine — NOT pethidine — neurotoxic) + paracetamol + NSAID (caution renal) + non-pharm (heat, distraction, hydration); avoid IV fluids excess (overhydration → ACS)
Oxygen if hypoxic, incentive spirometer
Screen for trigger — infection / dehydration / cold / stress
Antibiotics if any fever
Early discharge planning
ACUTE CHEST SYNDROME:
Broad-spectrum antibiotic (ceftriaxone + macrolide) + bronchodilator + simple transfusion early; EXCHANGE transfusion if severe/progressive
Incentive spirometer + pain control + oxygen
STROKE:
Exchange transfusion within 6-12h (target HbS < 30%)
Chronic transfusion or hydroxyurea (TWiTCH non-inferior NEJM 2016)
Primary prevention — TCD screening + transfuse if > 200 cm/s
PRIAPISM: > 4h — aspirate + adrenaline irrigation; urology
CURATIVE:
ALLOGENEIC HSCT — matched sibling donor (best outcomes children); haplo or MUD selected

GENE THERAPY — exa-cel (CASGEVY — CRISPR-Cas9 BCL11A, FDA Dec 2023) + lovo-cel (Lyfgenia — lentivirus, FDA Dec 2023) — eligible severe disease; cost + access challenges (esp SSA — advocacy + price reduction + transfer of tech essential)
PREGNANCY: multidisciplinary; folate; LMWH prophylaxis; pain crises common; transfusion threshold; prevention pre-eclampsia + IUGR
SSA SCALE-UP PRIORITIES:
Universal newborn screening (Kenya pilot + Tanzania + Nigeria scaling)
Penicillin + hydroxyurea + vaccines + malaria prevention — affordable + lifesaving
TCD machines + chronic transfusion programmes with safe blood + chelation
Specialised SCD clinics + comprehensive care + multidisciplinary
Mortality reduction through basic interventions before gene therapy access
Advocacy — gene therapy + voxelotor + crizanlizumab access + price negotiation (WHO PPP-style)
