title: Massive haemorrhage / transfusion protocol — 1:1:1 + TXA + ROTEM-guided
population: Active major haemorrhage: trauma, postpartum haemorrhage, GI bleed, surgical, ruptured AAA, ectopic, obstetric. > 10 units RBC in 24 h or > 4 units in 1 h = massive transfusion.
presentation: Active bleeding + haemorrhagic shock (tachycardia, hypotension late, lactate, base deficit, low Hb, coagulopathy). Trauma triad — hypothermia + acidosis + coagulopathy.
redFlags: DAMAGE control surgery / interventional radiology + resuscitation — not delayed
Pregnancy-related haemorrhage — uterotonic ladder + early O- if unmatched (Rh sensitisation concerns secondary)
Anticoagulation reversal — vit K + PCC + idarucizumab / andexanet
diagnostics: POC: Hb (HemoCue), lactate, base deficit, ABG, ionised Ca
Coagulation: INR, APTT, fibrinogen (target > 1.5 — 2 g/L PPH), platelets (target > 50 — > 100 if CNS/multitrauma), ROTEM/TEG viscoelastic (rapid + functional clot assessment) — IF AVAILABLE
Cross-match + group + screen — initially uncrossmatched O- emergency
FBC + UEC + LFT + glucose + cardiac enzymes selectively
Imaging: FAST / CT trauma / endoscopy / angio
management: European Trauma 2023 + UK NICE + ATLS + WHO + AAGBI:
ACTIVATE MTP — clear team role + lab + porter pathway; institutional protocol
DAMAGE CONTROL — control bleeding source FIRST (surgery / IR / endoscopy / tourniquet / packing); haemostasis trumps fluid
TRANSFUSION RATIOS (empirical until labs):
RBC : FFP : platelets — 1 : 1 : 1 (PROPPR JAMA 2015 — trend benefit + standardised in trauma)
PPH protocol — similar approach + cryoprecipitate early for fibrinogen
Massive haemorrhage pack 1: 4-6 RBC + 4-6 FFP + 1 platelet pool
Massive haemorrhage pack 2: add cryoprecipitate 2 pools
TRANEXAMIC ACID:
TRAUMA: 1 g IV over 10 min then 1 g over 8 h — WITHIN 3 H (CRASH-2 Lancet 2010 + CRASH-3 head injury 2019)
PPH: 1 g IV over 10 min repeat in 30 min if bleeding; effective within 3 h (WOMAN Lancet 2017)
GI bleed: HALT-IT Lancet 2020 — NO benefit + harm signal — DO NOT USE
FIBRINOGEN: cryoprecipitate (each pool ~ 2 g fibrinogen — 4 pools = ~ 8 g) or fibrinogen concentrate; target > 1.5-2 g/L PPH > 2 g/L
CALCIUM: monitor ionised; replace IV calcium chloride 1 g per 4 units RBC (citrate binds; hypocalcaemia worsens coagulopathy + cardiac contractility)
PREVENT TRAUMA TRIAD:
Warm (Bair Hugger, warmed fluids/blood, warm room)
Correct acidosis — restore perfusion + treat cause
Permissive hypotension in trauma without head injury (SBP 90 / palpable radial) until source control
REVERSAL of anticoagulation:
Warfarin: vitamin K 10 mg IV + 4-factor PCC (Beriplex / Octaplex) 25-50 IU/kg by INR
Dabigatran: idarucizumab 5 g IV
Xa inhibitor (apixaban/rivaroxaban): andexanet alfa (cost + access limited) or 4F-PCC 50 IU/kg
Heparin: protamine sulphate (1 mg per 100 units in last 2-3 h)
Antiplatelet — usually NOT specific reversal; platelets if life-threatening
ANTI-FIBRINOLYTIC if hyperfibrinolysis on ROTEM — TXA
FACTOR VIIa (NovoSeven) — generally NOT routine; consider salvage refractory haemorrhage
DIC: treat underlying + replace components (FFP + cryo + platelets)
OBSTETRIC: uterotonics ladder (oxytocin → ergometrine → carboprost → misoprostol) + B-Lynch / balloon / hysterectomy + interventional radiology embolisation
DEBRIEF + audit + simulation training

SSA: Kenya KNBTS + facility-level MTP development; blood supply chain + voluntary donation + safe blood; train teams + simulation; cost of factor concentrate + TXA + tranexamic access for primary postpartum advocacy.

title: Difficult airway management — DAS adult + paediatric algorithms + front-of-neck access
population: Any patient requiring tracheal intubation; high-risk anatomy (obesity, beard, restricted neck, mandibular hypoplasia, OSA, trauma, oedema, burns, pregnancy, paediatric), emergency setting.
presentation: Inability to mask ventilate or intubate; planned vs unplanned difficulty; awake fibreoptic vs RSI vs front-of-neck access.
redFlags: Cannot Intubate Cannot Oxygenate (CICO) — emergency front-of-neck access (eFONA) — IMMEDIATELY
Failed mask ventilation + paralysed patient → escalate immediately
Anatomy distortion (Ludwig's angina, anaphylaxis, burns, trauma) — anticipate + awake fibreoptic
Paediatric — different anatomy + reserve + algorithm (DAS Paeds 2024)
diagnostics: Airway assessment: Mallampati + thyromental distance + neck movement + mouth opening + Wilson + LEMON; OBESE; HOBBIT for emergency
POC ultrasound airway + cricothyroid membrane identification (CICO marking)
Plan A/B/C/D in advance per DAS
Equipment ready: videolaryngoscope, supraglottic airway, scalpel-bougie-tube for FONA, capnography
management: Difficult Airway Society (DAS) 2015 Adult + DAS Paediatric 2024 + ASA + NAP4:
PRE-OXYGENATE 3-5 min 100% O2 + denitrogenate (4 vital capacity breaths if rushed); apnoeic oxygenation NHF (high-flow nasal O2) 60 L/min reduces desat in difficult patients
PLAN A — TRACHEAL INTUBATION (max 3 attempts):
Optimal head/neck position (sniffing or ramped if obese)
Cricoid pressure controversial — release if obscuring view
VIDEOLARYNGOSCOPY first-line (C-MAC / Glidescope / McGrath) — improves Cormack-Lehane grade
Bougie introduction; size 7-8 ETT for adult; cuff up + capnography MANDATORY confirmation

Drugs: induction + neuromuscular blocker (suxamethonium 1-1.5 mg/kg or rocuronium 1-1.2 mg/kg high-dose for RSI — rocuronium preferred increasing; sugammadex 16 mg/kg reversal if failed RSI within 3 min)
PLAN B — SUPRAGLOTTIC AIRWAY (max 3 attempts):
Second-generation SGA (i-gel / LMA Proseal) — oxygenation + ventilation + drainage port; consider intubating through (Fastrach)
Decide: wake patient (elective) or proceed surgery via SGA (urgent) or proceed to Plan C
PLAN C — FACE MASK VENTILATION:
2-person 2-handed; oral + nasal airway adjuncts; muscle relaxant if not given (may improve)
Wake patient if possible
PLAN D — CICO — FRONT-OF-NECK ACCESS (eFONA) — EMERGENCY:
Declare CICO loudly
SCALPEL-BOUGIE-TUBE (DAS 2015 recommended adult): horizontal stab cricothyroid membrane → bougie → 6.0 ETT → confirm capnography + bilateral air entry
Pre-identified cricothyroid membrane (US in difficult anatomy)
Cannula cricothyroidotomy + jet ventilation alternative (paediatric < 8 yr first-line; risk barotrauma)
Convert to formal tracheostomy when stable
AWAKE FIBREOPTIC INTUBATION:
Anticipated difficult — distorted anatomy, fixed reduced opening, severe burns, neck mass, severe OSA, unstable c-spine, anaphylactic oedema, Ludwig's
Topical anaesthesia + minimal sedation (target alert + cooperative)
Awake VL emerging alternative
PAEDIATRIC (DAS Paeds 2024):
Different anatomy (large head + tongue + epiglottis, anterior larynx)
Higher O2 consumption + lower reserve → rapid desaturation
Familiar paediatric algorithm + appropriately sized equipment + skilled help
Front-of-neck — cannula cricothyroidotomy + jet < 8 yr
EXTUBATION + post-extubation: DAS Extubation 2012 — high-risk extubation plan (laryngeal mask exchange, airway exchange catheter, surgical airway ready)
DOCUMENTATION + ALERT (anaesthesia chart + medical alert bracelet) + difficult airway letter to patient and GP and future hospitals
AUDIT + simulation training + critical incident review (NAP4 lessons)
SSA: scalpel-bougie-tube + supraglottic airways + videolaryngoscope access expanding; train + simulation; cricothyroid US + difficult airway carts.

title: Stillbirth + perinatal loss — respectful care + bereavement + cause workup + follow-up
population: Stillbirth (≥ 28 wk WHO international / ≥ 24 wk UK / ≥ 20 wk US). 2 million stillbirths globally/year, 75% in SSA + South Asia. Neonatal death first 28 days. Miscarriage < 24 wk. Termination for fetal anomaly.
presentation: Antepartum (most — silent) or intrapartum loss. Family at acute grief + traumatic event + risk of subsequent pregnancy anxiety, PTSD, depression, marital distress.
redFlags: Maternal infection / sepsis with intrauterine death
Pre-eclampsia / abruption / cord accident causes — manage maternal
Coagulopathy from prolonged retained dead fetus
diagnostics: Confirm fetal death (ultrasound by 2 clinicians; auscultation alone insufficient)

Maternal workup: FBC + coag + UEC + LFT + glucose + HbA1c + thyroid + viral (CMV/parvo/syphilis/toxo/rubella) + Kleihauer + APL antibodies + thrombophilia (selective) + autoimmune; cultures if infective

Fetal workup: ANTEMORTEM imaging + postmortem (parental consent — uptake higher with empathetic approach) + placental histology (ESSENTIAL even if no PM) + karyotype / microarray + photographs + footprints + measurements
Cord blood + cardiac puncture for chromosomes / culture
Document for future pregnancy planning + parental closure
management: WHO + RCOG + ACOG + Sands + ISA (International Stillbirth Alliance):
ACUTE care:
PRIVATE quiet room + continuity of care + named midwife/clinician
RESPECTFUL communication — use baby's name + parental wishes + remember pronouns + acknowledge as baby not 'fetus'
Informed choices — labour vs LSCS, birthing position, presence of family
Pain relief generous + epidural if requested
INDUCTION usually preferred over expectant (DIC risk + psychological) — mifepristone + misoprostol regimen; oxytocin
Optimal time-to-delivery flexible based on maternal preference + health
MEMENTOS + MEMORIES (offer + revisit):
Holding baby (offered, never forced); cuddle cot to extend time
Photographs (own + professional — NILMDTS volunteer programmes)
Footprints, handprints, lock of hair, blanket, clothes, name bracelet
Naming baby + birth certificate where law allows
Faith/cultural rituals respected + facilitated
Cold cot/cuddle cot for extended time in room/at home
FAMILY support — partner / siblings (age-appropriate) / grandparents; cultural-sensitive
DISCHARGE planning:
Lactation suppression options + counselling (cabergoline 1 mg single dose or supportive)
Postnatal recovery + contraception discussion (NOT pressured but offered)
Mental health screening (Edinburgh PND scale + PTSD + complicated grief)
Discharge information pack: bereavement leaflet + support orgs (Sands, Tommy's, local) + memorial information + funeral arrangements + benefits + return-to-work + legal registration
Avoid ward with newborns; private discharge + side-door if requested
FOLLOW-UP:
Consultant-led debrief at 6-8 wk — review results + cause + risk subsequent pregnancy + emotional
GP visit 1-2 wk + community midwife / health visitor
Peer support group + counselling (CBT for PTSD)
Subsequent pregnancy — early consultant input + EARLY scan + extra support + Rainbow pregnancy clinic
PROFESSIONAL care:
Staff bereavement training + own support (debrief, supervision, time off if needed)
Documentation thorough for future pregnancy
Audit + perinatal mortality review (UK MBRRACE-PMRT; WHO Standards)
PREVENTION + REDUCTION:
Antenatal care quality + WHO 8-contact + risk assessment + GROW (customised growth)
Recognise + act on reduced fetal movements
Smoking cessation + BMI optimisation + glycaemic control + APL screen + aspirin in PE risk
Sleep position (lateral after 28 wk — MIDIRS evidence)
Each Baby Counts UK + WHO Every Newborn Action Plan + Kenya ENAP
SSA: Kenya — burden 21/1000 ; integrate respectful care + perinatal mortality review + Each Newborn Action Plan + community education + obstetric quality.

title: Paediatric obesity — family-based lifestyle + GLP-1 from 12 yr + metabolic-bariatric for severe
population: Globally rising 124 million children + adolescents; SSA increasing especially urban. Genetics + environment + socioeconomic + intrauterine programming + sleep + screens + ultra-processed food + sedentary.
presentation: BMI > 95th percentile (obesity), > 99th percentile / +2.33 z-score (severe). Comorbidities: T2DM, NAFLD, OSA, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, PCOS, depression, joint pain, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, Blount's, SCFE.
redFlags: Hypothalamic / endocrine (Cushing, hypothyroidism, GH excess/deficiency) — short stature + weight gain
diagnostics: BMI + percentile / z-score (WHO < 5 yr + 5-19 yr charts; CDC 2-19 yr; IOTF)
Waist circumference + BP + Tanner stage
Comorbidity screen: HbA1c / OGTT (T2DM), lipid panel, ALT/AST (NAFLD), TSH if growth concerns, vit D, urinalysis
Sleep history + STOP-BANG/PSQI; polysomnography if severe
Mental health screen + bullying + eating behaviour + family environment
Genetics if extreme obesity + early-onset (< 5 yr) + syndromic features
Liver US + bariatric workup if considered
management: AAP 2023 + WHO 2024 + NICE NG189 + ISPAD:
FAMILY-BASED INTENSIVE BEHAVIOUR LIFESTYLE TREATMENT (IHBLT):
Multi-component — diet + activity + behaviour change + family
≥ 26 contact hours over 3-12 months — strongest evidence (AAP 2023)
Motivational interviewing + goal-setting + self-monitoring
School + community integration
Address SOCIAL DETERMINANTS: food insecurity, housing, safety, screen time, parental work patterns
AVOID weight-stigma + 'diet talk'; focus health behaviours + weight as one metric
NUTRITION:
Whole foods + vegetables + fruits + lean protein + reduce ultra-processed
Reduce sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB) + juices + portion sizes
Family meals + structured eating times
Dietitian-led where available
PHYSICAL ACTIVITY:
60 min/d moderate-vigorous activity (WHO)
Reduce screen time + sedentary
Enjoyable + family + community
Address barriers (safety, equipment, programmes)
SLEEP: age-appropriate hours; screen-free bedroom; consistent routine
MENTAL HEALTH: assess + treat depression + anxiety + body image + bullying + ED behaviours; CBT
PHARMACOTHERAPY (≥ 12 yr per AAP 2023):
LIRAGLUTIDE 3 mg SC OD (Saxenda — FDA 2020 ≥ 12 yr)
SEMAGLUTIDE 2.4 mg SC weekly (Wegovy — FDA 2022 ≥ 12 yr) — STEP-TEENS 16% weight loss
PHENTERMINE-TOPIRAMATE (Qsymia — FDA 2022 ≥ 12 yr)
ORLISTAT 120 mg with meals (≥ 12 yr) — GI side effects
SETMELANOTIDE for selected genetic (POMC / LEPR / Bardet-Biedl) — IMCIVREE FDA
AGE OUT: GLP-1 for adolescent obesity = ALONGSIDE lifestyle (not replacement); contraindications + counsel + access barriers
METABOLIC-BARIATRIC SURGERY (MBS) — adolescents ≥ 13 yr severe (BMI ≥ 35 + comorbidities or ≥ 40):
Vertical sleeve gastrectomy (most common adolescent)
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
Adolescent MBS centre + comprehensive psychosocial workup + family engagement (Teen-LABS NEJM 2016 — durable weight loss + comorbidity remission)
Lifelong micronutrient supplements + follow-up
T2DM-SPECIFIC: lifestyle + metformin first-line (often inadequate alone); insulin if HbA1c > 8.5; GLP-1 (liraglutide ≥ 10 yr ELLIPSE T2DM) + dapagliflozin (≥ 10 yr)
OSA: ENT + adenotonsillectomy + CPAP
NAFLD: lifestyle + vitamin E selected; resmetirom adult only
POPULATION + POLICY:
WHO Childhood Obesity ECHO + SSB tax + food labelling + advertising restriction + school nutrition + active transport
Kenya — urbanisation + SSB tax debate + school food policy
Double-burden — undernutrition + obesity coexist; nuanced messaging
STIGMA-FREE care, family-centred, long-term, no shame.

NICE NG189 Obesity Children + Young People

title: Failure to thrive — multidisciplinary assessment + WHO IMCI scale-up + targeted nutritional
population: Young children (most often < 2 yr) with growth faltering — weight < 5th percentile, weight crossing 2 percentile lines down, or weight-for-length / BMI low. Global burden — large in SSA + S Asia (often part of malnutrition spectrum).
presentation: Inadequate weight gain, sometimes linear growth (stunting), feeding issues, developmental delay risk, irritable, sleep, immune compromise.
redFlags: SEVERE acute malnutrition (SAM — MUAC < 11.5 cm OR weight-for-height < -3 z-score OR bilateral pitting oedema) — WHO/UNICEF emergency
Anaemia + micronutrient deficiency (vit A, iodine, zinc, iron)
Underlying medical cause: heart, GI, endocrine, renal, neuro, infection (HIV/TB), CF, coeliac, milk protein
Safeguarding — neglect / abuse / mental health caregiver
diagnostics: Anthropometry serial: weight, length/height, head circumference, WAZ/HAZ/WHZ/MUAC — WHO charts < 5 yr; growth velocity
Detailed feeding history: breast/formula/complementary food + amounts + frequency + difficulties
Caregiver mental health + social + financial + food security
Examination: dysmorphology + system + dental + developmental + signs of nutritional deficiency
Investigations TARGETED — not blanket:
FBC + iron + UEC + LFT + TFT + coeliac (TTG) + urinalysis + faecal occult + faeces fat / parasites + lead
HIV testing (essential SSA + risk)
TB (consider + Mantoux + GeneXpert if exposure)
Genetics + cardiology / GI / neuro / metabolic per clinical
Bone age if linear growth
management: WHO + UNICEF + ENN + AAP + NICE NG75:
MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM (MDT): paediatrician + dietitian + speech and language (feeding) + nurse + social worker + community health worker + GP
ROOT CAUSE-BASED treatment:
Treat medical cause (HIV, TB, GI, heart, etc.)
Address feeding behaviour + technique (latch, paced bottle, positioning, oromotor)
Caregiver education + support + mental health treatment + food security + parenting
NUTRITIONAL RESCUE:
Breastfeeding optimisation: assess + support + lactation counsellor; relactation possible
Complementary feeding: from 6 mo — diverse + energy-dense + iron + zinc + frequency increased; WHO IYCF education
Calorie supplementation: high-calorie foods + thickeners + oils + nut paste + fortification
SAM: WHO 2013 + 2023 simplified management:
Outpatient if no complications + appetite test passed (eat RUTF) — community-based therapeutic feeding (CMAM/IMAM) with RUTF (ready-to-use therapeutic food — Plumpy'Nut + locally produced)

Refeeding syndrome — gradual increase + monitor phosphate / Mg / K / glucose; thiamine before glucose
MICRONUTRIENT:
Vit A high-dose every 6 mo < 5 yr in deficient settings (WHO)
Iron + folate for anaemia
Zinc supplementation
Iodised salt + multimicronutrient
Deworming albendazole 400 mg q6 mo > 1 yr + STH endemic

Suspected neglect / abuse → safeguarding pathway + multi-agency + social work
Inpatient observation may clarify

Breastfeeding promotion (BFHI) + WHO Code marketing of breastmilk substitutes

title: Disability-inclusive primary care — accessible communication + reasonable adjustments + UNCRPD
population: 1 billion+ people globally living with disability (15% population — WHO World Report on Disability); higher in SSA; women + older + conflict-affected populations especially. Includes physical, sensory (visual/hearing), intellectual, psychosocial, neurodevelopmental, chronic disease.
presentation: Persons with disability face health inequities: barriers to access (physical, communication, attitudinal, financial), poorer health outcomes, shorter life expectancy, higher unmet need, less preventive care, more emergency visits.
redFlags: Diagnostic overshadowing — attributing symptoms to disability rather than investigating
Lack of accessible communication leading to misdiagnosis
Abuse / neglect — 3-4× higher in persons with disability — safeguarding
Specific risks: pressure ulcers (wheelchair / immobility), aspiration (dysphagia), seizures (intellectual disability + epilepsy 22%), osteoporosis (low weight-bearing), polypharmacy
diagnostics: Standard clinical assessment + reasonable adjustments (longer appointment, accessible format, communication support)
Functional assessment + ADL/IADL + WHODAS 2.0
Care plan + multidisciplinary team if complex needs
Annual health check (esp. learning/intellectual disability — Cardiff Health Check / UK NHS LD Annual Health Check — improves detection)
Pain assessment in non-verbal: behavioural pain scales (DisDAT, FLACC, Abbey, PAINAD)
Capacity + supported decision-making + Mental Capacity Act (UK) + UNCRPD principles
management: WHO Disability Inclusion 2022 + UNCRPD + WHO World Report on Disability + Sustainable Development Goals:
ACCESSIBILITY:
Physical — ramps, accessible toilets, accessible equipment (height-adjustable couches, weighing scales for wheelchair users, hoists), parking

Communication — Easy Read, pictorial, sign language interpreter (BSL/ASL/local), longer appointment slots, plain language, hearing loop, augmentative + alternative communication (AAC), Braille / large print
Sensory-friendly environment for autism (quiet room, sensory adjustments)
Telehealth + outreach for those who can't attend
Affordability — fee waivers + NHIF for chronic + supports
REASONABLE ADJUSTMENTS (legal duty UK Equality Act + ADA US + UNCRPD globally):
Individual to each patient + ask + record + act on
Examples: longer appointment, first / last slot, separate waiting area, named clinician familiarity, advance information, sedation for dental / procedures, social story
CO-PRODUCTION + AUTONOMY:
'Nothing About Us Without Us' — engage persons with disability in service design + decisions
Supported decision-making (UNCRPD Art 12) — even with cognitive impairment, supported autonomy + best interests
Carers + family supported but patient is centre
AVOID DIAGNOSTIC OVERSHADOWING:
Investigate symptoms thoroughly — don't attribute to disability without workup
Pain may be expressed differently (behavioural change in intellectual disability + non-verbal)
Use objective + collateral + careful assessment
PREVENTIVE CARE — same as general population PLUS specific:
Cancer screening (cervical, breast, colorectal) — often missed; adapted access
Vaccinations
Bone health (low activity + epilepsy meds + low BMI)
Mental health screening (high prevalence depression + anxiety + PTSD)
Dental + vision + hearing checks (regularly missed)
Sexual + reproductive health (often denied; rights-based)
Continence + bowel + skin assessment
MEDICATION REVIEW:
Polypharmacy common; STOPP/START + anticholinergic burden + interactions
Avoid sedating in those at falls / aspiration risk
Psychotropic over-use (STOMP / STAMP UK — Stopping Over-Medication in People with Learning Disability / Autism)
SAFEGUARDING + ADULT PROTECTION:
Higher rates of abuse + neglect + hate crime
Routine enquiry + safe disclosure pathways + multi-agency
MULTIDISCIPLINARY:
GP + specialists + PT/OT/SLT + community nurse + social worker + carer + advocate
Transition from paediatric to adult — planned + 'Ready Steady Go' pathway
REHABILITATION + ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY:
WHO GATE — Global Cooperation on Assistive Technology; APL — assistive products list
Wheelchair, hearing aid, glasses, prosthetic, communication device
Community-based rehabilitation (CBR) approach in LMIC
INTERSECTIONAL: gender + race + ethnicity + LGBTQ+ + age + rurality + refugee — compounding marginalisation
TRAINING for clinicians on disability + UNCRPD principles + rights-based approach + co-production with persons with disability + experts by experience
POPULATION + POLICY:
UNCRPD ratified Kenya 2008 + national disability action plan
WHO Disability Inclusion + Rehabilitation 2030
Persons with Disabilities Act Kenya 2003 (in revision)
Disability employment + education + transport + social protection (cash transfers)
Inclusive disaster + emergency response
Data — disaggregate by disability (Washington Group Questions)

title: Pulmonary embolism — PESI/sPESI + PERT for intermediate-high / massive; catheter-directed lysis
population: 1-2/1000 person-years; post-op, hospitalised, cancer, OCP, pregnancy, COVID, prior VTE, thrombophilia. 25% present as sudden death.
presentation: Dyspnoea + pleuritic chest pain + tachycardia + hypoxia + DVT signs; massive — shock + syncope + arrest; saddle embolus on CTPA.
redFlags: MASSIVE PE — shock / cardiac arrest — PEA — consider PE if pulseless + risk factors; bolus thrombolysis
Submassive (intermediate-high) — RV dysfunction + biomarker positive — consider PERT + reduced-dose lysis
diagnostics: Risk stratify clinical: Wells + Geneva; if low + D-DIMER NEG (age-adjusted) — PE excluded
CTPA (gold standard); V/Q if contrast / renal contraindication / pregnancy
Bedside US — RV dilatation + McConnell + tricuspid regurg + RA thrombus + DVT lower-limb (DVT confirms PE in clinical context)
ECG (S1Q3T3 classic but rare; tachycardia + RBBB), troponin (RV strain → mortality predictor), BNP/NT-proBNP
RISK CLASS ESC 2019:
Low (PESI I-II / sPESI 0): outpatient
Intermediate-low: anticoagulation + monitor
Intermediate-HIGH (RV dysfunction on echo + biomarker pos): ANTICOAGULATION + WATCH; PERT consideration if deteriorating
HIGH (shock): MASSIVE PE — thrombolysis
management: ESC 2019 + 2024 update + AHA + CHEST + ASH:
ANTICOAGULATION FIRST-LINE all confirmed (or high clinical suspicion before confirmation):
DOAC preferred for haemodynamically stable + non-cancer + non-pregnant — apixaban 10 BD × 7 d → 5 BD; rivaroxaban 15 BD × 21 d → 20 OD; dabigatran/edoxaban after parenteral LMWH 5-10 d
LMWH first-line cancer-associated (apixaban / edoxaban alternative in non-GI cancer per HOKUSAI-VTE-cancer + CARAVAGGIO); pregnancy LMWH only
Warfarin (target INR 2-3) with LMWH bridge until therapeutic — alternative; KEML-affordable resource-limited
Duration: provoked (transient RF) 3 mo; unprovoked + cancer + thrombophilia 6 mo to indefinite — shared decision (HERDOO2 for women)
MASSIVE PE (high-risk — hypotension / shock / arrest):
SYSTEMIC THROMBOLYSIS — alteplase 100 mg over 2 h (or 0.6 mg/kg over 15 min bolus arrest) — class I
Avoid in active bleeding / recent surgery / stroke / pregnancy late
PEA cardiac arrest + risk factors — bolus + CPR 60-90 min

Surgical embolectomy / CATHETER-DIRECTED THROMBOLYSIS for thrombolysis contraindicated or failed (SEATTLE-II + EXTRACT-PE + FLARE — EkoSonic, FlowTriever — reduce RV/LV ratio + less bleeding than systemic)
Veno-arterial ECMO + thrombolysis / embolectomy refractory
INTERMEDIATE-HIGH (submassive — RV strain + troponin):
Anticoagulation + close monitor — ICU/step-down
PERT (Pulmonary Embolism Response Team) review for catheter-directed thrombolysis or surgical embolectomy — PEITHO trial (alteplase reduced decompensation but bleeding) + ongoing trials
No clear benefit of routine systemic lysis (PEITHO NEJM 2014)
PERT (Pulmonary Embolism Response Team):
Multidisciplinary — interventional cardiology / IR / cardiac surgery / ICU / pulmonary / haematology
Rapid activation for intermediate-high + massive PE
Decision for advanced therapies — catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT), mechanical thrombectomy, surgical embolectomy, ECMO
Centres + national PERT consortium
PREGNANCY PE:
CTPA or V/Q (V/Q lower fetal radiation but breast); MRI alternative
LMWH (therapeutic weight-based) throughout pregnancy + 6 wk postpartum; switch to UFH peri-delivery
Massive PE: thrombolysis acceptable if life-threatening (alteplase doesn't cross placenta)
POST-DISCHARGE follow-up:
Anticoagulation review + extension decision
Symptom follow-up — CTEPH (chronic thromboembolic PH) — 4% develop — echo + V/Q if persistent dyspnoea at 3-6 mo
Cancer workup if unprovoked + risk + age
Lifestyle + secondary prevention
IVC FILTER: only when anticoagulation contraindicated (active bleeding, immediate surgery) or progressive despite anticoag; remove when contraindication resolved (PREPIC-2 + others)
SSA: Kenya — CTPA available tertiary; alteplase + apixaban/rivaroxaban affordability + access advocacy; PERT formation tertiary centres; warfarin alternative resource-limited.

title: Serotonin syndrome — Hunter criteria + supportive + cyproheptadine
population: Iatrogenic — combinations of serotonergic drugs (SSRI/SNRI/MAOI/TCA/triptan/tramadol/pethidine/fentanyl/linezolid/methylene blue/St John's wort/MDMA/cocaine). Severity from mild to lethal.
presentation: Triad: AUTONOMIC (hyperthermia, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, mydriasis, diarrhoea, flushing), NEUROMUSCULAR (clonus — esp. lower limbs + spontaneous + inducible + ocular, hyperreflexia, rigidity worse legs, tremor), MENTAL STATUS (agitation, confusion, coma). Onset within 6-24 h of trigger; recently after dose change or addition.
redFlags: Severe — temp > 41 °C → ICU + paralysis + intubation + cooling
Confused with NMS (NMS = slower onset days, lead-pipe rigidity, hyporeflexia, antipsychotic context); both can overlap
diagnostics: HUNTER CRITERIA (preferred over Sternbach) — exposure to serotonergic + one of: spontaneous clonus, inducible clonus + agitation/diaphoresis, ocular clonus + agitation/diaphoresis, tremor + hyperreflexia, hypertonia + temp > 38 + ocular/inducible clonus
Bloods: FBC + UEC + LFT + CK (rhabdo) + lactate + ABG + coag (DIC) + cardiac enzymes
ECG (QT, arrhythmia)
Exclude: NMS, anticholinergic toxicity (dry, urinary retention, mydriasis without clonus), malignant hyperthermia (perioperative + succinylcholine), meningitis/encephalitis, thyroid storm, sepsis
Drug + alcohol history exhaustive (over-the-counter + supplements + recent changes)
management: ACMT + EAPCCT:
STOP all serotonergic agents IMMEDIATELY
SUPPORTIVE — mainstay:
IV fluids + electrolytes + monitor
Cooling for hyperthermia (active — ice packs, evaporative, cooling blanket; tepid sponging; avoid antipyretics — temperature is muscle-driven not central)
Continuous cardiac + temp + neuro monitoring; ICU for moderate-severe
BENZODIAZEPINES first-line for agitation + autonomic + rigidity + clonus:
Diazepam 5-10 mg IV q5-10 min titrated, or midazolam 1-2 mg
Lorazepam 2-4 mg IV alternative
CYPROHEPTADINE (5-HT2A antagonist) — moderate-severe — 12 mg PO/NG initial then 2 mg q2h until response (max 32 mg/24h); maintenance 8 mg q6h
Limited evidence but recommended; only oral form (NG if intubated)
Reduces duration of mild-moderate cases
CHLORPROMAZINE 50-100 mg IM has 5-HT2A antagonism — alternative (avoid in hypotension)
SEVERE (temp > 41 °C, rigidity + rhabdo):
Intubate + sedate + PARALYSE with non-depolarising (rocuronium/vecuronium) — SUXAMETHONIUM CONTRAINDICATED (hyperkalaemia in rhabdomyolysis)
Reverses muscle rigidity → controls hyperthermia
Rhabdomyolysis — IV fluid + monitor K + CK + AKI; dialysis if severe
DIC — supportive replacement
AVOID:
Dantrolene (no good evidence; reserved for malignant hyperthermia)
Bromocriptine (NMS treatment — not for serotonin syndrome)
Antipyretics (paracetamol/NSAID — ineffective; hepato-renal risk in rhabdo)
Physical restraints alone (worsens hyperthermia)
PROGNOSIS: most resolve within 24-72 h of stopping trigger
WASHOUT before restart: SSRI 2 wk; FLUOXETINE 5-6 wk (long t½); MAOI 2 wk before serotonergic
PREVENTION + EDUCATION: review medication list; especially primary care + ED prescribing tramadol/fentanyl/triptan/linezolid/methylene blue/St John's wort in patient on SSRI/SNRI/MAOI
SSA: educate primary care + pharmacy + recognition + ED capacity for ICU; benzodiazepine + cyproheptadine widely available.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome — stop neuroleptic + dantrolene + bromocriptine
population: Idiosyncratic adverse effect of antipsychotic (typical > atypical), antiemetic dopamine antagonist (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine); withdrawal of L-DOPA or anti-Parkinson. Risk: high-potency typical, rapid dose escalation, dehydration, agitation, prior episode, lithium combination.
presentation: Tetrad over days: HYPERTHERMIA + RIGIDITY (lead-pipe, more global, hyporeflexia) + AUTONOMIC INSTABILITY + ALTERED MENTAL STATUS. Slower onset (days-1-2 wk) than serotonin syndrome.
redFlags: Hyperthermia > 41 °C + rhabdomyolysis + AKI → ICU + active cooling

Differentiate from serotonin syndrome (faster, lower limb clonus, hyperreflexia, recent serotonergic) + malignant hyperthermia (anaesthesia + sux) + heat stroke + lethal catatonia (overlap — catatonia + autonomic + rigidity)
diagnostics: DSM-5/Levenson criteria — neuroleptic exposure + hyperthermia + rigidity + 2 of: autonomic + altered mental + CK > 4× ULN + tremor + leucocytosis + diaphoresis + incontinence
CK markedly raised (often > 10,000)
FBC leucocytosis; LFT raised; raised renal function (AKI from rhabdo); raised lactate; ABG metabolic acidosis
Coagulation (DIC)
Exclude: serotonin syndrome (Hunter criteria), heat stroke, anticholinergic, meningitis/encephalitis (LP if uncertain), thyroid storm, sepsis, malignant hyperthermia
Drug history — recent neuroleptic / antiemetic / L-DOPA withdrawal
management: Position statements + Strawn 2007 + Caroff:
STOP NEUROLEPTIC / dopamine antagonist immediately; RESTART L-DOPA if withdrawal-precipitated
SUPPORTIVE — mainstay:
IV fluid resuscitation + electrolytes
Active COOLING (ice, evaporative, cooling blanket)
ICU monitoring + correct rhabdomyolysis (IV fluid + monitor K, Mg, PO4, CK, urine output, alkalinise if pigmenturia)
Treat acidosis + hypoxia + DIC + AKI (dialysis if severe)
BENZODIAZEPINES — first-line for agitation + autonomic; lorazepam 1-2 mg IV q4-6h
DANTROLENE — direct skeletal muscle relaxant — 1-2.5 mg/kg IV q6-12h (max 10 mg/kg/24h) for severe rigidity + hyperthermia; switch to PO 100-200 mg/d as improves
BROMOCRIPTINE — dopamine agonist — 2.5-5 mg PO/NG q8h titrate up to 45 mg/d; restart L-DOPA if Parkinsonian (CAUTION serotonergic combined)
AMANTADINE 100-200 mg PO/NG BD alternative
ECT — for refractory or overlap with catatonia
INTUBATE + PARALYSE (non-depolarising — NOT suxamethonium — hyperK rhabdo) for refractory hyperthermia / rigidity
DURATION 5-10 d typically; longer for depot neuroleptic

RESTART NEUROLEPTIC after recovery — wait ≥ 2 weeks; switch to LOWER potency / atypical (clozapine sometimes used) + start low + slow + monitor; share decision with patient + family; risk of recurrence 30%
AVOID dopamine antagonist if life-long care + use alternative for nausea (ondansetron, antihistamine)
PREVENT: avoid rapid neuroleptic escalation + dehydration + monitor temp + CK in early initiation in high-risk; L-DOPA — gradual titration + don't stop abruptly

DIFFERENTIAL: serotonin syndrome (hyperreflexia + lower-limb clonus + recent serotonergic + faster onset hours), heat stroke (environment + heat exposure), thyroid storm (TFT), malignant hyperthermia (anaesthesia + sux + 'cousin' but distinct genetic susceptibility), lethal catatonia (catatonia + autonomic — overlap exists)
SSA: education on antipsychotic + antiemetic prescribing + early recognition + ICU access advocacy.

Kenya National Cancer Treatment Guidelines (National Cancer Control Programme), Ministry of Health
WHO Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis / WHO Essential Medicines for Cancer

title: Catatonia — Bush-Francis recognition + lorazepam challenge + ECT for refractory
population: 10% of acute psychiatric admissions; medical (encephalitis, autoimmune NMDAR, metabolic, drug-induced) + psychiatric (schizophrenia, mood disorders, autism); all ages.
presentation: Mutism + immobility + posturing + waxy flexibility + negativism + stupor + echolalia / echopraxia + automatic obedience + stereotypies + grimacing + verbigeration. Stupor to excited subtypes. MALIGNANT CATATONIA — adds hyperthermia + autonomic instability + risk like NMS.
redFlags: MALIGNANT catatonia — hyperthermia + autonomic — ICU + treat as emergency (overlaps NMS)

Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis — young women + ovarian teratoma + psych + dystonia + seizure + autonomic — ICU + immunotherapy (high-dose steroid + IVIG + PLEX + rituximab + cyclophosphamide; teratoma removal)
DVT/PE from prolonged immobility — anticoagulant prophylaxis
Underlying medical cause requiring urgent treatment
diagnostics: BUSH-FRANCIS CATATONIA RATING SCALE — 23 items; ≥ 2 of first 14 + total ≥ 6 = catatonia
DSM-5 catatonia criteria — 3+ of 12 features

Medical workup ESSENTIAL — NMDAR antibodies + autoimmune panel + UEC + LFT + Ca + Mg + glucose + TSH + B12 + folate + CRP + creatine kinase + drug screen + neuroimaging (CT/MRI) + EEG + LP if encephalitis suspected

Differentiate from: NMS (recent neuroleptic + rigidity), serotonin syndrome (recent serotonergic + clonus), stiff person syndrome, locked-in syndrome, depression with psychomotor retardation, akinetic mutism, conversion disorder
Identify underlying — psychiatric (mood/psychotic) vs medical/neurological
management: BFI 2013 + Lancet Psychiatry 2019:
STOP any neuroleptic (can worsen + precipitate malignant catatonia)
TREAT UNDERLYING — anti-NMDA encephalitis immunotherapy + tumour resection; autoimmune; metabolic; infection
LORAZEPAM CHALLENGE 2 mg IV (or 4 mg) — DIAGNOSTIC + therapeutic — observe 5-10 min for response (improvement in mutism, immobility, eye contact)
Response in 70-80% of catatonia — confirms diagnosis
MAINTENANCE LORAZEPAM 6-24 mg/d divided q4-8h titrated — most respond; may need surprisingly high doses; safe sedation
ALTERNATIVES: zolpidem (occasionally), memantine (NMDA antagonist), amantadine, carbamazepine, valproate
ECT — gold standard for refractory or malignant or rapid response needed; bilateral; daily initially then taper; 80-90% response rate (more than lorazepam alone)
NUTRITION (NG tube), hydration (IV fluid), DVT prophylaxis (LMWH), positioning + pressure care, mouth care, monitor electrolytes
Treat aspiration pneumonia if develops
MALIGNANT CATATONIA: ECU + ECT urgently + lorazepam + supportive (cooling, fluids, electrolyte); avoid neuroleptic
ANTI-NMDA RECEPTOR ENCEPHALITIS specific:
Ovarian teratoma screen (US + MRI + tumour markers — young woman essential)
Immunotherapy: methylpred 1 g/d × 5 d + IVIG 0.4 g/kg × 5 d OR plasma exchange first-line
Second-line if no response: rituximab + cyclophosphamide
Tumour resection essential if found
Long-term (1-2 yr) immunomodulation; relapse 20%
Recovery may take months
RECOVERY: most resolve with appropriate treatment; psychiatric underlying may relapse
FOLLOW-UP psychiatric + neurological as appropriate
EDUCATION: family + carer about catatonia recognition + early treatment
SSA: lorazepam + ECT capacity expanding tertiary; train psychiatry + neurology + medical wards.

title: Refeeding syndrome — risk-stratify + thiamine before glucose + cautious calorie reintroduction
population: Anyone malnourished or undernourished starting feeding (oral, enteral, parenteral): severe anorexia nervosa, prolonged starvation, alcoholism, refugee/famine, post-bariatric, oncology, prolonged ICU NPO, SAM children, post-stroke dysphagia. Mortality if missed.
presentation: Within 72h of feeding reintroduction: hypophosphataemia (most characteristic), hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, hyperglycaemia, fluid retention, thiamine deficiency manifesting as Wernicke's. Cardiac (arrhythmia, HF), respiratory failure, neuro, haemolysis, rhabdo.
redFlags: High-risk patient — BMI < 16 or weight loss > 15% past 3-6 mo or > 10 d minimal/no intake or pre-existing low electrolytes — needs slow + monitored
Severe hypophosphataemia (< 0.32 mmol/L) — replace IV + ICU monitor
Cardiac arrhythmia + HF onset during refeeding
Wernicke's encephalopathy — confusion + ophthalmoplegia + ataxia — IV THIAMINE EMERGENCY
Anorexia nervosa with BMI < 13 — high mortality + ICU level care
diagnostics: NICE CG32 high-risk criteria
Baseline: weight + height + BMI + dietary history + duration of poor intake
Pre-feeding bloods: PHOSPHATE + POTASSIUM + MAGNESIUM + sodium + chloride + glucose + UEC + LFT + albumin + thiamine if available + Ca + B12/folate + Hb
ECG baseline + repeat
Daily electrolytes for first 7 d then every 2-3 d
Fluid balance + weight daily (sudden gain = retention)
management: NICE CG32 + ESPEN + NHS:
RISK STRATIFICATION:
HIGH RISK ≥ 1 major OR ≥ 2 minor:
MAJOR: BMI < 16, weight loss > 15% past 3-6 mo, > 10 d minimal/no intake, low pre-feeding K/PO4/Mg
MINOR: BMI < 18.5, weight loss > 10%, > 5 d minimal intake, history of alcohol/drug/insulin/chemo/diuretic/antacid use
VERY HIGH RISK ≥ 2 major or BMI < 14 or > 15 d no intake
BEFORE feeding (or at start):
THIAMINE 200-300 mg IV/IM (Pabrinex 1+2 high-dose IV in alcoholic / severe over 30 min) + multivitamin daily for first 3-10 d — THIAMINE BEFORE GLUCOSE (Wernicke prevention)
Correct fluid + electrolytes BEFORE feeding (or together if delay would harm)
Replace K/PO4/Mg even if low-normal in high-risk; aim K > 4, PO4 > 0.8, Mg > 0.7 mmol/L
CALORIE PRESCRIPTION:
HIGH RISK: START 10 kcal/kg/d (max 5 kcal/kg/d if very high risk, BMI < 14 or > 15 d nil)
Increase slowly over 4-7 d to estimated need (25-35 kcal/kg/d)
Carbohydrate ≤ 50% energy initially (high carb worsens refeeding); balanced protein + fat
Salt + fluid restrict to avoid fluid retention (if cardiac risk); usual ESKD restrictions
ELECTROLYTE REPLACEMENT during refeeding (daily monitor):
Phosphate IV (preferred severe) — Phosphate Polyfusor 500 mL infused over 12-24 h (50 mmol); oral Phosphate Sandoz tabs (16.2 mmol) BD-TDS for mild-moderate
Potassium IV or oral
Magnesium IV (severe) or oral
Maintain levels during increasing feed
MONITORING:
Daily: weight, fluid balance, electrolytes (PO4/K/Mg), glucose, UEC × 7 d → 2-3× weekly week 2
Cardiac: ECG + telemetry high-risk; clinical HF
Refeeding bloods even after target reached × 2 wk
WERNICKE's: thiamine 500 mg IV TDS × 2-3 d then 250 mg IM/IV daily; oral 100 mg TDS long-term; if missed → Korsakoff
SAM children (WHO): F-75 then F-100; cautious calorie progression; antibiotics + vit A + folate + Zn; specific WHO protocol

ANOREXIA NERVOSA: specialist eating disorder team + MDT + medical + psychiatric + dietitian + family; calorie monitoring + supervised; capacity assessment + Mental Health Act if life-threatening refusing treatment
PARENTERAL nutrition: same risk + slower titration + central line; specialist input
SSA: SAM IMAM + RUTF + WHO 10 steps; raise awareness of refeeding in ICU + onco + alcoholic admissions.

title: Nephrolithiasis — analgesia + MET + imaging + metabolic workup recurrence
population: 12% lifetime prevalence; male 2:1; peak 30-50; recurrent ~50% within 10 yr. Hot climates + dehydration + diet + obesity + hyperparathyroid + cystinuria + RTA + gout + bowel surgery.
presentation: Severe colicky loin-to-groin pain + restless (cannot lie still — unlike peritonitis) + haematuria (90%) + nausea + LUTS if low + fever (infection — emergency).
redFlags: INFECTED + obstructed kidney — fever + obstruction + sepsis — EMERGENCY decompression (nephrostomy or stent) + antibiotics
Pregnancy + stone — modified imaging (US/MRI; avoid CT) + careful management
Stone > 10 mm — unlikely to pass + plan intervention
Recurrent / staghorn — metabolic workup + complex management
diagnostics: CT KUB (non-contrast) GOLD STANDARD — high sensitivity all stone types except indinavir; size + location + density
Renal US first-line in pregnancy + paediatric + alternative low-dose
Urinalysis (haematuria; nitrites/leuks + culture if infection)
Bloods: UEC + Ca + urate + FBC + CRP
Pregnancy test in women
ANALYSE PASSED STONE (sieve urine) — calcium oxalate (most), calcium phosphate, uric acid, struvite, cystine
METABOLIC WORKUP after first stone in selected (recurrent / young / family / SAM-causing): 24h urine (volume, Ca, Na, citrate, oxalate, urate, creatinine, pH); serum PTH + Ca; uric acid
management: EAU 2024 + AUA 2016 + NICE NG118:
ACUTE COLIC:

ANALGESIA NSAID first-line (diclofenac 75 mg IM/IV/PO or ketorolac 30 mg IM/IV) — superior to opioid alone (Cochrane); paracetamol IV adjunct; OPIOID if NSAID contraindicated / inadequate (morphine; tramadol cautious)
ANTIEMETIC (metoclopramide, ondansetron)
IV fluids only if dehydrated (forcing fluids does NOT accelerate stone passage)
Hot pack analgesia adjunct
STONE SIZE + LOCATION:
< 5 mm proximal/distal ureter — 80-90% pass spontaneously; trial of passage 2-4 wk + analgesia + sieve urine
5-10 mm — 50% pass; MET (medical expulsive therapy) — TAMSULOSIN 400 μg/d × 4 wk for distal ureteric stones 5-10 mm (SUSPEND trial — modest benefit; NICE 2019 still recommends)
> 10 mm or failed passage or upper ureter — intervention
INTERVENTION:
ESWL (extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy) — stones < 2 cm renal or ureteric upper
URS (ureteroscopy + holmium laser lithotripsy) — most stones; +/- JJ stent
PCNL (percutaneous nephrolithotomy) — large > 2 cm + staghorn
Stent for obstruction relief; nephrostomy if infected/septic
EMERGENCY — INFECTED + OBSTRUCTED:
SEPSIS bundle + broad-spectrum antibiotic (ceftriaxone + gentamicin or piperacillin-tazobactam)
URGENT decompression — RETROGRADE STENT or PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROSTOMY (within hours)
NEVER delay decompression for full stone treatment
Definitive stone treatment after sepsis resolved
STONE TYPE-SPECIFIC:
Calcium oxalate (most): hydration + lower oxalate diet (rhubarb, spinach, nuts) + adequate Ca + thiazide if hypercalciuria + citrate (K-citrate 10-30 mEq TDS)
Uric acid: alkalinise urine (K-citrate or NaHCO3) to pH > 6.5; allopurinol if hyperuricaemic
Struvite (infection): treat infection + complete stone removal (won't resolve with antibiotic alone)
Cystine: high hydration + alkalinise + tiopronin / D-penicillamine
Calcium phosphate: investigate RTA + hyperparathyroid
PREVENTION (key for recurrent):
HYDRATION — > 2.5 L/d (urine > 2 L)
Dietary: moderate Ca (NOT low — actually increases oxalate absorption), reduce Na (< 100 mmol/d), reduce animal protein, reduce oxalate (if hyperoxaluria), normal-low purine if uric acid
Address modifiable: obesity + DM + gout
Identify + treat secondary cause (hyperparathyroidism — parathyroidectomy; RTA — treat; gout)
THIAZIDE (chlortalidone 25 mg) if hypercalciuria + recurrent (NOSTONE recent + Cochrane)
CITRATE supplementation for hypocitraturia

PREGNANCY: US first; conservative analgesia (paracetamol; codeine; avoid NSAID 1st + 3rd trimester); urology if obstruction (JJ stent or nephrostomy until post-partum); MET tamsulosin off-label cautious
PAEDIATRIC: increasingly common; metabolic workup essential; cystinuria + hyperoxaluria + RTA + structural
SSA: hot climate + dehydration + access to imaging + urology + ESWL/URS at tertiary; build capacity; awareness for primary care.

title: Food allergy IgE — diagnosis + avoidance + auto-injector + emerging oral immunotherapy
population: 6-8% children + 4-5% adults; peanut + tree nut + cow milk + egg + wheat + soy + fish + shellfish + sesame (top 9). Lifelong for nut/shellfish/fish; milk/egg often outgrown by adolescence.
presentation: IgE-mediated within 2 h of ingestion: urticaria + angioedema + GI (vomiting, diarrhoea) + respiratory (cough, wheeze, throat) + anaphylaxis. Oral allergy syndrome (cross-reactivity pollen + raw fruit/veg — limited). Non-IgE: FPIES (vomiting + lethargy + shock 2-4 h after milk/soy/grain), eosinophilic oesophagitis (chronic), proctocolitis (infant breast/cow milk — bloody stool, well).
redFlags: ANAPHYLAXIS — IM adrenaline thigh + supportive (see Anaphylaxis algorithm)
Severe reaction history — 2 auto-injectors at all times + action plan + medic-alert + allergist referral
Multiple food + severe + co-asthma/atopic — high risk
Infant with chronic reflux + eczema + GI bleed — non-IgE workup
FPIES — recurrent severe vomiting + shock often misdiagnosed as sepsis
Pollen-food syndrome severe (kiwi, peach, nuts can anaphylax in pollen-allergic)
diagnostics: DETAILED clinical history — food + timing + reaction + reproducibility
Skin prick testing (SPT) and/or specific IgE (ImmunoCAP) — sensitisation marker, NOT diagnostic alone (high false positives 30-50% positive without clinical allergy)
Component-resolved diagnostics (Ara h 2 peanut, Cor a 14 hazelnut, Gly m 8 soy) — increase specificity + risk stratification
ORAL FOOD CHALLENGE — gold standard for diagnosis + outgrowth assessment + tolerance threshold; supervised + emergency-ready (allergist clinic + day case)
Basophil activation test (research)
Total IgE + atopic markers + asthma assessment
Tryptase if anaphylaxis (within 4 h)
Eczema severity + dietary history + family
management: EAACI + AAAAI 2024 + BSACI + WAO:
AVOIDANCE strict for confirmed allergens:
Read labels (legislation now requires highlighting top allergens; precautionary 'may contain' confusing)
Eating out — communicate, choose safer venues; high-risk events (school, parties, travel)
Cross-contamination awareness + dedicated utensils
Lower thresholds in children with severe reactions
ADRENALINE AUTO-INJECTOR:

TWO AUTO-INJECTORS (EpiPen / Jext / Emerade) for anyone at risk of anaphylaxis — anaphylaxis history, severe reaction, multiple food, asthma + food allergy, persistent peanut/tree nut, mast cell disorder, exercise-induced
TRAIN family + school + carer + child age-appropriately
ANAPHYLAXIS ACTION PLAN — pictorial individualised written; review annually + after each reaction
Replace before expiry
ALWAYS CARRY — never one-only — biphasic + injector failure
EDUCATION + DIETITIAN + psychosocial + transition planning
MEDIC-ALERT bracelet
RESCUE for non-anaphylactic mild: oral antihistamine (cetirizine 10 mg adult / 5 mg child < 6 + weight-dose); observe; if symptoms severe or progressing → adrenaline
ORAL / SUBLINGUAL IMMUNOTHERAPY (OIT/SLIT) — EMERGING — allergy specialist + research / approved indication:
PEANUT OIT (Palforzia — Aimmune) FDA 2020 — ages 4-17 — desensitisation + improved threshold; risk of reactions during build-up; eosinophilic oesophagitis risk; access cost

EARLY introduction of allergenic foods (LEAP study NEJM 2015) — peanut from 4-6 mo in high-risk eczema/egg allergic infants — REDUCES peanut allergy 80% — PARADIGM SHIFT (replaced 'delay' recommendation)
EARLY EGG, milk emerging
Tolerance-induction protocols
Omalizumab adjunct OIT (OUtMATCH 2024 — omalizumab raises threshold + safer OIT) — multi-food
OUTGROWING:
Milk + egg: 50-80% outgrow by school age (re-challenge q12-24 mo allergist)
Peanut + tree nut + fish + shellfish: usually persist lifelong
Component results help predict
FPIES (non-IgE):
Acute: IV fluid + ondansetron + (refractory — methylpred 1 mg/kg); admit if severe
Chronic: avoid trigger; reintroduce in supervised manner at 12-18 mo (then yearly)
Common triggers: cow milk, soy, rice, oats, egg
EOSINOPHILIC OESOPHAGITIS: PPI + topical steroid (swallowed fluticasone/budesonide); diet (elimination 6-food, 4-food, milk-only); dilatation for strictures; dupilumab FDA approved
PROCTOCOLITIS: maternal dietary exclusion if breastfed; extensively hydrolysed formula if formula-fed; resolves usually by 1 yr
POLLEN-FOOD (oral allergy syndrome): cook trigger food (denatures protein); avoid raw if symptoms; usually mild; rare anaphylaxis
PREGNANCY + LACTATION: continue normal diet (no benefit to restriction); promotes oral tolerance
SSA: emerging awareness; auto-injector access + cost advocacy; community + school education; train primary care; integrate with anaphylaxis algorithm.

title: Nocturnal enuresis — exclude underlying + reassure + alarm + desmopressin
population: 16% of 5-yr-olds, 10% of 7-yr-olds, 5% of 10-yr-olds, 1-2% adolescents/adults; male 2:1; strong family history; PRIMARY (never dry) vs SECONDARY (re-emerged ≥ 6 mo dry — investigate). Day + night vs night-only.
presentation: Involuntary wetting during sleep > 5 yr age. Often asymptomatic otherwise. Daytime symptoms suggest bladder dysfunction.
redFlags: Daytime wetting / urgency / frequency / dysuria — underlying bladder/UTI/structural — workup
Secondary enuresis — UTI, DM, CKD, constipation, sleep apnoea, abuse, emotional distress
Snoring / OSA / mouth-breathing — adenotonsillar — treat OSA may resolve enuresis
Constipation severe + impacted — common contributor + treat
Adolescent + adult onset — neurological / structural workup
diagnostics: History — primary vs secondary + frequency + day/night + onset + family + family stressors + sleep + drinking pattern + bowel
Examination — abdomen + genitalia + spine (sacral dimple, hair patch) + neurology + tonsils + nasopharynx
Urinalysis — exclude UTI / DM (glycosuria) / proteinuria
Bladder diary (3-d voiding chart) + bowel diary
Selective: US KUB if recurrent UTI / daytime symptoms / suspected structural; MRI spine if neuro signs
management: NICE CG111 + ICCS + ICCSG:
REASSURE — common + most outgrow + not naughtiness + no punishment
Address underlying — treat constipation (laxatives), UTI, OSA, secondary causes
LIFESTYLE FOUNDATION:
Adequate daytime fluid (6-8 drinks evenly spaced); restrict evening fluid 2 h before bed
Avoid caffeine + dark fizzy drinks + chocolate
Regular voiding day (q2-3h) + before bed; double void at bedtime
Treat constipation (Movicol/laxative + regular toileting)
Positive reward chart (dry nights) + no punishment
Lifting / waking — limited evidence — discontinue if not working
TREATMENT ages 5-7+ (or distress earlier):
ENURESIS ALARM (bedwetting alarm) — first-line — body-worn or pad-with-sound — child wakes to alarm → toilet → reset; 14-week trial; supportive parent + child engaged
Cure ~ 65% (better than meds long-term; low relapse)
Continue until 14 consecutive dry nights or 14 wk
DESMOPRESSIN — alternative or combination — for short-term (sleepover, camp) or if alarm not feasible / family pref / older child
120-240 μg sublingual (or 200-400 μg tablet) at bedtime — restrict fluid evening (avoid hyponatraemia) — NEVER if fluid restriction not possible
Caution: hyponatraemic seizures (if drink water late) — counsel + monitor
Withdraw periodically — 1 wk break every 3 mo to assess tolerance
COMBINATION alarm + desmopressin for refractory
IMIPRAMINE 25-50 mg nocte — historic — TOXIC overdose + cardiac risk — last resort + specialist
ANTIMUSCARINIC (oxybutynin, tolterodine) if daytime overactive bladder symptoms — specialist
REFER specialist if refractory / daytime + nocturnal / structural / underlying suspected / safeguarding / mental health
PSYCHOSOCIAL: reassurance + sibling teasing + school + sleepovers + camp planning + self-esteem; address bullying + parental frustration; counselling if needed
FOLLOW-UP regular; encourage; revisit if treatments fail; ongoing in adolescent + adult — refer specialist + investigate structural / neurological
ADULT enuresis — neurological / structural / sleep / OUD (opioid) / alcohol / psychiatric workup essential — never assume primary
SSA: addressing constipation + UTI common + train primary care + reassurance + non-pharm for resource-limited.

title: Tinnitus + acoustic neuroma — MRI IAM for asymmetric loss, CBT for management
population: Tinnitus 10-15% adults; vestibular schwannoma 1/100,000/yr; bilateral suggests neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2 — formerly bilateral acoustic neuroma).
presentation: Tinnitus — perception of sound without external source; usually subjective + variable; primary (no identifiable cause) vs secondary (e.g. hearing loss, otosclerosis, Meniere's, ototoxic, vascular, TMJ, cervicogenic, depression). Vestibular schwannoma (VS) — UNILATERAL progressive sensorineural hearing loss + tinnitus + imbalance + late facial nerve / brainstem.
redFlags: UNILATERAL or ASYMMETRIC sensorineural hearing loss + tinnitus → MRI IAM for VS
Pulsatile tinnitus (vascular — AVM, glomus tumour, dural fistula, atherosclerosis, BIH) — investigate
Facial weakness or brainstem signs → urgent imaging
Sudden onset SNHL — emergency (see SSNHL pathway)
Severe psychological distress + tinnitus + suicide risk
Bilateral VS + family history → NF2 + genetic referral
Large VS + brainstem compression / hydrocephalus — surgical emergency
diagnostics: Audiology: pure-tone audiogram + tympanometry + acoustic reflexes + speech audiometry
If ASYMMETRIC SNHL (≥ 15 dB at any frequency or ≥ 10 dB at 2 adjacent — variable thresholds per society) — MRI internal auditory meatus + cerebellopontine angle with gadolinium — GOLD STANDARD for VS
Tinnitus questionnaire: TFI (Tinnitus Functional Index), THI (Tinnitus Handicap Inventory)
Identify treatable cause: cerumen, OME, otosclerosis, Meniere's, ototoxic drugs review
Pulsatile tinnitus: MRA + MRV + duplex carotid + audiometry + autoimmune + ferritin
Bilateral VS / family — NF2 genetics
management: AAO-HNS 2014 Tinnitus + 2018 VS + ENT UK + BSA:
TINNITUS:
Reassure benign primary tinnitus + most habituate; address fears + catastrophising
Identify + treat treatable cause (cerumen, OME, ototoxic drug, Meniere's)
HEARING AID for tinnitus + hearing loss — single most effective intervention (masks tinnitus + improves background sound)
CBT (cognitive-behavioural therapy) — strongest evidence for distress reduction (NICE NG98 + AAO-HNS) + Tinnitus Retraining Therapy (TRT)
Sound enrichment / masking (white noise, fan, music, hearing aid with masker, smartphone apps)
AVOID promising silence cures; AVOID gingko, B12, melatonin lack solid evidence (AAO-HNS Recommendation Against)
Sleep hygiene + relaxation + meditation + mindfulness + low-dose antidepressant if mood comorbid
Avoid ototoxic + further noise; hearing protection
Severe distress + suicide risk — mental health + acute support
Cochlear implant for SNHL + tinnitus (severe-profound bilateral)
Emerging — bimodal stimulation (Lenire — auditory + tongue) FDA 2023
Surgical (microvascular decompression) — rare + selected
VESTIBULAR SCHWANNOMA:
Small (< 1.5 cm intracanalicular) — WATCH + WAIT — MRI surveillance q6-12 mo initially then yearly (most slow-growing — Wait + Scan strategy);
Growth or symptoms or larger (> 1.5-2 cm) — INTERVENE:
STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY (Gamma Knife / CyberKnife / linac) — preferred small-medium + hearing preservation goal
MICROSURGICAL excision (translabyrinthine — sacrifices hearing; middle fossa / retrosigmoid — hearing preservation in selected small)
Combined / staged for large
Facial nerve preservation paramount + skilled centre
Hearing aid + cochlear implant + auditory brainstem implant (NF2 + bilateral) — rehab
NF2 — multidisciplinary (genetics + ENT + neurosurgery + ophthalmology + cardiac + tumour surveillance — multiple meningiomas + ependymomas + schwannomas)
Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) — for refractory NF2 schwannoma — reduces growth + preserves hearing (small trials)
PSYCHOLOGICAL: tinnitus + asymmetric loss + VS diagnosis can be distressing — peer support (Tinnitus UK, ANA — Acoustic Neuroma Association)
SSA: MRI access tertiary; audiology + ENT scale-up; raise awareness for asymmetric hearing loss + appropriate referral; bevacizumab + radiosurgery access limited.

title: Mental capacity assessment — UNCRPD-aligned + decision-specific + supported decision-making
population: All adults; commonly assessed in older adults, dementia, intellectual disability, severe mental illness, brain injury, intoxicated, severely ill in ICU, end-of-life, paediatric maturity (Gillick / Fraser).
presentation: Decision about treatment, finances, residence, lifestyle — concerns about person's ability to make + understand consequences. Capacity is DECISION-SPECIFIC + TIME-SPECIFIC + can fluctuate.
redFlags: Coercion, undue influence, abuse, financial exploitation — safeguarding pathway
Lack of capacity + family disagreement + difficult best interests
Lack of capacity + suicide risk + refusing life-saving treatment
Cultural / language / sensory barriers — ensure adequate support before declaring lack capacity (UNCRPD)
Children + adolescents — Gillick + Fraser + parental responsibility
diagnostics: 5 PRINCIPLES (MCA 2005 UK + similar frameworks globally):
1) Presumption of capacity unless proven otherwise
2) All practicable steps to support decision-making
3) Unwise decisions ≠ lack of capacity
4) Best interests if lack capacity
5) Less restrictive option
FUNCTIONAL TEST (2-stage in MCA):
1) Diagnostic — impairment of mind/brain (temporary or permanent)?
2) Functional — Can the person:
- UNDERSTAND the information relevant to the decision
- RETAIN it long enough to decide
- WEIGH it up + apply to themselves
- COMMUNICATE their decision (any means including blinking, AAC)
Inability in ANY ONE due to the impairment = lacks capacity for THAT DECISION
Assessor: usually clinician making the decision; complex cases — formal IMCA + court of protection / equivalent
Document — what was assessed + how supported + outcome + best interests if lack capacity
management: MCA 2005 UK + UNCRPD Art 12 + Mental Capacity (Amendment) Act + national variations + Kenya draft:
BEFORE assessing — REASONABLE ADJUSTMENTS to support capacity:
Quiet + private + time-of-day when best
Use Easy Read, pictorial, plain language, interpreter, AAC, advocate, family if patient wishes
Address treatable causes — UTI, hypoxia, electrolyte, drug, infection (delirium reversible)
Multiple sessions; re-assess after improvement
Respect cultural communication norms
CAPACITY EXISTS — RESPECT decision even if 'unwise'
LACK CAPACITY — best interests decision (UK + similar):
Decision-specific + minimum restriction + maximally permissive
Consider patient's PAST + PRESENT wishes + values + beliefs (life story + family + advance statement)
Consult those close (LPA + family + advocate) but final decision is clinical / proxy
Document reasoning + 5 principles applied
ADVANCE DIRECTIVE / ADVANCE DECISION:
Validity — specific, signed, witnessed (life-sustaining), patient had capacity when made, applicable to current situation
Refuse treatment ADRT — legally binding if valid + applicable
Advance statement — wishes + preferences — guides best interests
Lasting Power of Attorney — Health + Welfare AND/OR Property + Finance
DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY (DoLS UK / equivalent):
Continuous supervision + control + not free to leave + lacks capacity to consent
Authorisation required (Liberty Protection Safeguards in transition)
Always least restrictive
SUPPORTED DECISION-MAKING (UNCRPD Art 12):
Even with intellectual disability / dementia, support to express + exercise legal capacity
Move from substitute → supported decision-making globally
PAEDIATRIC:
GILLICK competence (UK 1986) — child < 16 with sufficient understanding can consent to medical treatment
FRASER guidelines (specific to contraception under 16)
Parental responsibility holders consent for younger / non-Gillick-competent
Disagreement child vs parent — court if necessary
EMERGENCY:
Treat to preserve life under doctrine of necessity / emergency where capacity cannot be assessed; reassess + comply with directives if any
MENTAL HEALTH ACT (UK) — separate from MCA — for compulsory psychiatric admission/treatment under specific criteria (not best interests but specific section)
RESEARCH + clinical trial — additional safeguards for those lacking capacity (informed consent or proxy)
DOCUMENT thoroughly; explain decisions to patient + family + record
TRAINING all clinicians + regular updates + safeguarding pathway
SAFEGUARDING — undue influence + abuse + financial — pathway

SSA: Kenya — Mental Health (Amendment) Act 2022 + Care + Mental Capacity Bill draft + UNCRPD ratified 2008; develop frameworks + train + community awareness + supported decision-making + safeguarding.

title: Drug allergy assessment + de-labelling — penicillin allergy review + skin / oral challenge
population: 10% reported 'penicillin allergy' — 90-95% NOT truly allergic on testing — leads to second-line antibiotic use + worse outcomes + AMR. Other drugs: NSAID, cephalosporin, sulfa, contrast, biologic, vaccine.
presentation: History of reaction often vague / childhood / family-reported. Important: timing (immediate < 1 h vs delayed > 6 h), nature (urticaria vs rash vs anaphylaxis vs SJS vs serum sickness vs DRESS), severity, hospitalised, since how many years.
redFlags: Severe reaction history (SJS/TEN, DRESS, anaphylaxis, AGEP, fixed drug, hepatitis, nephritis) — NEVER rechallenge + alternative class lifelong
Beta-lactam true allergy + need for ATB → choose alternative class (not just avoid all β-lactam)
Multiple drug allergies — referred to allergy specialist
MASTOCYTOSIS / mast cell disorder — special protocols
Active asthma poorly controlled + planned challenge — delay until stable
diagnostics: DETAILED HISTORY — drug, indication, timing, nature of reaction, severity, treatment, since how long, intervening exposure, similar reactions to related drugs
PENICILLIN ALLERGY DECISION TOOL — UK Penicillin Allergy Algorithm + ALLERGY-NICE Toolkit:
LOW-RISK (childhood rash, > 10 yr ago, isolated GI, family reported, vague) — may proceed with direct oral challenge (single 250 mg amoxicillin observed) outpatient or inpatient by trained team
MEDIUM-RISK (urticaria within hours but not anaphylaxis) — skin testing + graded challenge (allergist)
HIGH-RISK (anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reaction — SCAR; recent < 5 yr) — allergist + skin testing + caution; avoid if SCAR
Skin prick + intradermal testing (major + minor determinants) — penicillin available + extends sensitivity
Specific IgE (lower sensitivity than skin)
Patch testing for delayed cutaneous
DRESS / SJS — biopsy + RegiSCAR + steroid + ICU; avoid retest
Direct oral challenge — definitive in low-medium risk under supervision
management: EAACI 2024 + AAAAI + BSACI + NICE NG134 + AHRQ Penicillin Allergy De-labelling:
PENICILLIN ALLERGY DE-LABELLING:
Identify low-medium risk patients (most reported allergies)
Direct oral challenge protocol — single oral amoxicillin 250 mg observed 60-120 min
Negative — DE-LABEL in records (electronic medical record alert removed + patient counselled + alert card)
Specialist for higher risk + complex
Should be SYSTEMATIC programme — hospital antibiotic stewardship + outpatient clinic
Pharmacist-led + integrated with stewardship
CROSS-REACTIVITY:

Penicillin → cephalosporin: traditionally 10% — modern evidence < 2% (esp. if different R1 side chain); cefuroxime + ceftriaxone + cefepime + ceftazidime usually safe; cefadroxil + cephalexin + cefaclor more cross-reactive (similar R1 to ampi/amox)
Penicillin → carbapenem: < 1% — can use if penicillin allergy not severe
Cephalosporin → cephalosporin — R1 side-chain dependent
Penicillin → monobactam (aztreonam) — minimal cross-reactivity (unless ceftazidime allergy — same side chain)
Modern guidance — based on side-chain + severity, not blanket avoidance
ANAPHYLAXIS to drug — IM adrenaline + anaphylaxis algorithm + AVOID drug + class + auto-injector + medic-alert + allergist follow-up + alternative documented
MILD DELAYED rash penicillin (T-cell) — safe to use alternative penicillin / class; NOT contraindication to all β-lactam (after evaluation)
SCAR (SJS/TEN/DRESS/AGEP) — NEVER rechallenge; lifelong alternative; record clearly + alert + counsel
DRUG DESENSITISATION — for true allergy when no alternative + treatment essential (e.g. penicillin for syphilis in pregnancy, sulfa for PCP in HIV, chemotherapy allergy):
Inpatient + allergist + ICU-ready + graded protocol (3-12 h)
Temporary tolerance — must continue uninterrupted; restart desensitisation if missed dose
VACCINE ALLERGY: skin test + graded challenge if essential vaccine + suspected egg / gelatin / latex (MMR + influenza usually safe even with egg allergy now per UK + US)
CONTRAST MEDIA: pre-medication (pred + antihistamine) controversial; use low-osmolar non-ionic; emergency-ready
BIOLOGIC reactions: infusion reaction vs true allergy + tryptase + IgE testing + desensitise selected
POPULATION + STEWARDSHIP:
Penicillin allergy de-labelling programme = single highest-impact stewardship intervention (reduces vancomycin, broad-spectrum, healthcare-associated infection, cost) — AHRQ + WHO advocate
Hospital alert + medical record + electronic prescribing integration
Train primary care + ED + pharmacy
Counsel patients + alert card + electronic record updated
SSA: AMR + stewardship priority; de-labelling programme cost-effective; train + integrate with hospital stewardship.

title: Pheochromocytoma / paraganglioma — α-blockade before β-blockade, surgical referral
population: Rare (0.2-0.6/100k). 25% hereditary — VHL, MEN2A/B, NF1, SDHx (SDHB → metastatic risk), TMEM127, MAX. All adrenal (pheo) or extra-adrenal sympathetic chain (paraganglioma).
presentation: Triad — headache + sweating + palpitations + hypertension (sustained or paroxysmal). May be normotensive (esp. paraganglioma, dopamine-secreting). Pallor, anxiety, weight loss, hyperglycaemia. Often missed — investigate any resistant HTN + family history + symptoms.
redFlags: Hypertensive crisis with anaesthesia / surgery / contrast / β-blocker monotherapy (worsens — unopposed α)
Hereditary syndrome — index case → screen family
Pregnancy + pheo — high maternal + fetal mortality
diagnostics: PLASMA FREE METANEPHRINES (most sensitive — first-line) or 24h URINE FRACTIONATED METANEPHRINES
Avoid: pre-test caffeine + paracetamol + TCA + SSRI + labetalol (false positive); supine seated 30 min before draw
CT/MRI adrenal + abdo + chest + pelvis for localisation; MRI in pregnancy + paragangliomas
MIBG / 68-Ga DOTATATE PET — functional imaging + metastatic + paraganglioma
Genetic testing — all <50 yr + bilateral + extra-adrenal + family history + metastatic (10 known genes)
ECG + echo (catecholamine cardiomyopathy); HbA1c
Workup family of confirmed hereditary
management: ESE 2014 + Endocrine Society 2014 + ENS@T:
PREOPERATIVE α-BLOCKADE 7-14 days BEFORE surgery — MANDATORY:
PHENOXYBENZAMINE (irreversible α-blocker — gold standard but limited supply) 10 mg BD titrate to 1-2 mg/kg/d in divided doses
OR doxazosin (selective α1) 2 mg BD titrate to 16-32 mg/d — less postural hypotension but rebound HTN possible
Goals: BP < 130/80 sitting; orthostatic to 90 systolic acceptable; no paroxysms; nasal congestion + postural symptoms (signs of effective blockade)
Liberal salt + fluids in last 3-5 days (catecholamines deplete volume; collapse on surgery if not preloaded)
ADD β-BLOCKER ONLY AFTER α-blockade established (≥ 3-4 days):
Atenolol / metoprolol / propranolol — controls reflex tachycardia + arrhythmia from α-blocker
NEVER β-blocker first — unopposed α-vasoconstriction → hypertensive crisis + cardiogenic shock + death
CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER (nicardipine / amlodipine) — adjunct if BP still uncontrolled or labile
AVOID: metoclopramide / glucagon / opioid (some) / cold pressor / IV contrast in unblocked patient — all release catecholamines
SURGERY:
Laparoscopic adrenalectomy preferred (open if > 6-8 cm or invasive)
Extra-adrenal — depends on location, sometimes en bloc resection

Anaesthetist expertise essential — labile BP intraoperative (manipulation releases stored catecholamines); arterial line + CVP + esmolol / phentolamine / nitroprusside / nitroglycerin / magnesium ready
Post-op: hypotension common (catecholamine withdrawal) — fluid + pressor if needed; hypoglycaemia possible
FOLLOW-UP:
Plasma metanephrines at 2-6 wk post-op to confirm cure
Annual biochemical (metanephrines) lifelong — recurrence 6-23% over 10 yr; higher SDHB + hereditary + paraganglioma
Imaging if biochemical recurrence
METASTATIC / unresectable:
131-I-MIBG therapy
Sunitinib (TKI emerging — KEYNOTE-158)
Lutetium-177 DOTATATE (peptide receptor radionuclide therapy)
Chemotherapy CVD (cyclophosphamide + vincristine + dacarbazine)
Belzutifan emerging (HIF-2α inhibitor — VHL + SDH-related)
Symptom control with α + β blockade
PREGNANCY:
Diagnose with plasma metanephrines + MRI; CT contraindicated
α-blockade essential; β-blockade after (avoid in 1st trimester atenolol)
Multidisciplinary — endocrine, obstetric, anaesthesia
Resect ideally in 2nd trimester or post-delivery (LSCS with synchronous resection or staged); maternal + fetal mortality higher in 3rd trimester
GENETICS + family — refer index case to genetics; screen family for hereditary syndrome
SSA: phenoxybenzamine access often limited — doxazosin alternative; surgical + anaesthetic expertise + MDT essential; advocate access + training.

title: Hyperprolactinaemia + prolactinoma — exclude drug / hypothyroid / pregnancy, dopamine agonist first-line
population: 10-30/100k; female predominance (microadenomas) and gender-balanced (macroadenomas). Causes: pituitary adenoma (most), drugs (antipsychotic, metoclopramide, antiemetic, SSRI, methadone, verapamil, ranitidine), hypothyroidism, renal failure, chest wall lesion, idiopathic.
presentation: Female: galactorrhoea + amenorrhoea / oligomenorrhoea / infertility. Male: hypogonadism + reduced libido + erectile dysfunction + infertility + osteoporosis. Macroadenoma: headache + visual field defect (bitemporal hemianopia) + hypopituitarism + diplopia.
redFlags: Visual field defect / acute visual loss — bitemporal hemianopia → urgent MRI + neurosurgical / endocrine
Pituitary apoplexy (sudden severe headache + ophthalmoplegia + visual + altered mental) — emergency (covered separately)
Pregnancy + macroadenoma — counsel + monitor (oestrogen stimulates growth)
Cabergoline + valvular heart disease at high cumulative dose (rare Parkinson dose; reassuring at prolactinoma doses)
diagnostics: MORNING prolactin (after rest 30 min, no breast exam, fasting) — repeat if borderline
Levels:
< 25 ng/mL (530 mIU/L) normal female; < 20 male
> 100 ng/mL (2120 mIU/L) usually adenoma
> 200 ng/mL macroadenoma
EXCLUDE 'HOOK EFFECT' with macroadenoma — assay falsely low — dilute sample if disconnect imaging + level
MACROPROLACTIN (PEG precipitation) — false-high prolactin if asymptomatic — common reason
WORKUP CAUSE: drug history (medication review), TSH (hypothyroid → TRH → prolactin), creatinine + eGFR, hCG (pregnancy)
Pituitary MRI with contrast — if hyperprolactinaemia confirmed + cause not drug / thyroid / pregnancy / renal
Pituitary function: cortisol + ACTH + FT4 + TSH + LH/FSH + testosterone / oestradiol + GH/IGF-1 + ADH
Visual field testing if macroadenoma or compression suspected
management: Endocrine Society 2011 + ESE 2024:

TREAT CAUSE if non-tumour: stop / switch culprit drug (psychiatry consult for antipsychotic — aripiprazole + quetiapine prolactin-sparing); treat hypothyroidism (L-thyroxine); pregnancy normalises post-delivery
PROLACTINOMA — DOPAMINE AGONIST FIRST-LINE:

CABERGOLINE 0.25 mg twice/week initially → titrate by prolactin response (typical 0.5-1 mg twice/week; max 3.5 mg/week) — first choice (more effective + better tolerated than bromocriptine; high MRI shrinkage response)
BROMOCRIPTINE 1.25 mg nocte titrate to 2.5-15 mg/d (TDS for nausea) — alternative; preferred in pregnancy planning (more pregnancy safety data)
Quinagolide — alternative; not available everywhere
Monitor prolactin q1-3 mo until normal, then q6-12 mo + MRI 1 yr + every 1-2 yr; visual field if macro
Withdrawal after 2+ yr normal prolactin + tumour shrinkage on MRI — about 30-40% sustained remission
SURGERY (transsphenoidal):
Indications: intolerance / resistance to dopamine agonist; visual field not improving on medical; CSF leak; apoplexy; pregnancy planning with macro near optic chiasm
Pituitary surgeon — high-volume centre — better outcomes + lower hypopituitarism rate
Cure rates microadenoma 70-80%; macroadenoma 30-40%
RADIOTHERAPY (stereotactic / fractionated) — selected refractory / aggressive — slow response + hypopituitarism risk
TEMOZOLOMIDE — aggressive / malignant prolactinoma (rare)

MANAGE HYPOGONADISM if persistent (oestrogen + progesterone in female; testosterone in male) once tumour control established — bone health + libido + fertility (but oestrogen may stimulate tumour growth — discuss)
BONE: DEXA + Ca + vit D + bisphosphonate / denosumab if osteoporotic
PREGNANCY:
Most women resume fertility on DA → conceive
STOP DA at confirmed pregnancy IF microadenoma (low risk of growth)
CONTINUE DA throughout pregnancy IF macroadenoma > 1 cm or near optic chiasm (bromocriptine more data)
Visual field testing each trimester + headache awareness
Symptomatic growth → restart DA (or surgery 2nd trimester)
Breastfeeding usually OK after delivery (encourage); restart DA after weaning if needed
MEN1 + AIP screen — young patients + family history
SSA: cabergoline + bromocriptine widely available; transsphenoidal expertise limited (KNH + few centres); telemedicine MDT + neurosurgery referral.

references.label: Kenya National Guidelines for Quality Obstetrics and Perinatal Care (EmONC), Ministry of Health
WHO Recommendations on Maternal and Newborn Care

title: PMDD — luteal-phase SSRI + COC (drospirenone) + lifestyle
population: 3-8% menstruating women; underdiagnosed. Heightened sensitivity to normal cyclical hormonal change; family + personal history of mood disorder.
presentation: Severe mood + behavioural + physical symptoms in luteal phase (week before menses) with resolution within 2-3 days of onset of menses, symptom-free week after. ≥ 5 of 11 DSM-5-TR symptoms (at least 1 affective): markedly depressed mood, marked anxiety / tension, marked affective lability, marked irritability / anger, decreased interest, concentration, fatigue, appetite, sleep, overwhelm, physical symptoms. Confirmed by prospective daily ratings × 2 cycles.
redFlags: Severe affective + functional impairment cyclical with menses — formal psychiatric review
Differential — premenstrual exacerbation of underlying MDD / bipolar / anxiety (symptoms persist outside luteal phase — different management)
diagnostics: DSM-5-TR criteria for PMDD
DAILY RECORD OF SEVERITY OF PROBLEMS (DRSP) — prospective daily symptom diary for 2+ cycles confirms cyclical pattern
Rule out underlying MDD / bipolar / anxiety / OCD / PTSD / thyroid / anaemia / endometriosis / migraine
Suicide risk assessment
Pregnancy + lactation status
management: ACOG + RCOG + ISPMD:
MILD-MODERATE:
Lifestyle — regular aerobic exercise + adequate sleep + reduce caffeine/alcohol/sodium luteal phase + mindfulness + CBT
Calcium 1200 mg/d + vit B6 50-100 mg/d + magnesium 200-360 mg/d + evening primrose oil (modest evidence)
Symptom diary tracking
SEVERE / functional impairment — FIRST-LINE:

SSRI — continuous OR LUTEAL-PHASE-ONLY dosing (day 14 to menses; emerging — symptom-onset dosing — Eriksson) — sertraline 50-150 mg/d, fluoxetine 20 mg/d, paroxetine, escitalopram, citalopram, venlafaxine
Effective within 1-2 cycles (much faster than MDD response)
Side effects + sexual + weight: warn + monitor
Combined oral contraceptive with DROSPIRENONE 24/4 cycle (Yaz/Yasmin) — FDA approved PMDD — superior to other COCs
Some women — continuous (extended) COC eliminates withdrawal symptoms
REFRACTORY:
GnRH ANALOGUE (leuprolide / goserelin) + add-back oestrogen + progesterone — ovulation suppression — significant relief
Bone health — DEXA + Ca + D + bisphosphonate if prolonged
Surgical: bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy ± hysterectomy + HRT — last resort + women who completed family + severe refractory
Mindfulness-based + dialectical behaviour therapy + ACT
Sepranolone (allopregnanolone modulator) — in trials
CO-OCCURRING — treat in parallel (MDD/anxiety/OCD/eating disorder)
PSYCHOSOCIAL: education + family + partner; reduce stigma (validate cyclical pattern); peer support; impact on relationships + work
PERIMENOPAUSE: PMDD symptoms can worsen; HRT may help; transition to MDD/anxiety pattern
PREGNANCY/POSTPARTUM: PMDD usually quiescent in pregnancy; postpartum depression/anxiety risk increased — anticipate + screen + treat
SSA: education + recognition + access to SSRI affordable (KEML) + integrate with women's mental health services; advocacy + reduce stigma.
